abbey-farm.md.programme_names: - Farm Visits - EYFS/Primary - Secondary/Colleage [sic, as published] - Booking Information
abbey-farm.md.activities_verbatim: (Early Years Foundation Stage: Nursery / Reception / Years 1 & 2, from the EYFS/KS1 information pack): - Abbey Farm trail - Where does our food come from? - Teddy Bear's Picnic (nurseries) - The Big Bug Hunt - Woodland activities (Primary schools: Key Stage 2, from the KS2 information pack): - Abbey Farm trail - Where does our food come from? - Farming through the Ages - Making Science come to life - Plant growth: inhibitors / acclerators [sic] - Woodland activities - Abbey Farm Numeracy Quiz (from the "Secondary/Colleage" page, listed as curriculum links rather than named activities): - Farming as a business - Hedgerow / Microclimate investigation - Woodland Comparison - Land-Use mapping
abbey-farm.md.duration: "Then the group is taken on a farm walk and tractor and trailer ride which takes around 1 hour." "We would suggest a class visit lasting 2 – 2 ½ hours each." EYFS/Primary page: "Visits are run for around 2 ½ hours either in the morning or afternoon." Pre-visit meeting: "This usually takes about ½ hour."
abbey-farm.md.group_size_min_max: "Please note: a maximum of 30 per group is recommended." No stated minimum.
abbey-farm.md.participant_thresholds: Maximum of 30 per group recommended (see above). No other numeric participant threshold stated. ## Inventory
abbey-farm.md.facilities: "Oak Barn, our Mud and Stud building"; "NEW for 2015: 40 seat, open sided trailer, Mud & Stud barn & new loos and hand washing facility"; "The barn, trailer and loo facilities all have disabled access."; Kirkstead Abbey ruin and St Leonard's Church, both sited on the farm.
abbey-farm.md.equipment_provided: none listed beyond the trailer used for the tractor and trailer ride; no separate list of loaned equipment (e.g. magnifying glasses, nets) is given on the pages read.
abbey-farm.md.staff_qualifications_stated: "This all takes place in an enjoyable and safe, CEVAS trained environment." No individual staff qualifications named beyond the CEVAS (Countryside Educational Visits Accreditation Scheme) training reference.
abbey-farm.md.accessibility_provision: "The barn, trailer and loo facilities all have disabled access. The farm visit can be tailored to maximise use of the trailer for any wheelchair users so the experience of seeing the crops in the fields can still be enjoyed."
abbey-farm.md.animal_species_held: "feeding the chickens" is listed as one of the additional on-farm activity options; no other animal species named on the pages read. ## Curriculum
abbey-farm.md.curriculum_links: "School visits can be tailored to link with specific topics but generally our genuine educational and fun-filled experience links well with cross-curricular subjects at all levels within the National Curriculum." Secondary/College page frames the farm around "Modern food production," "Sustainability of agriculture," "Globalisation – the smaller world," "Citizenship – responsibilities and rights," plus hedgerow/microclimate investigation, woodland comparison, and land-use mapping as curriculum-linked study topics.
abbey-farm.md.teacher_materials: "download pack keystage 1" and "download pack keystage 2" links referenced from the Farm Visits and EYFS/Primary pages; four such packs (2013 and 2015 editions, EYFS/KS1 and KS2) were found downloadable directly from the site's file store. ## Trust
abbey-farm.md.risk_assessment_available: "Pre-visits usually lasts about 30 mins and involves visiting us to draw up a timed visit plan, a run through health & safety and receive our risk assessment (which should assist in producing your own risk assessment!)"
abbey-farm.md.accreditations_displayed: "This all takes place in an enjoyable and safe, CEVAS trained environment." The farm is described as "kindly funded by Natural England" for these visits, and land is described as under a "Natural England Higher Level Environmental scheme," but no formal safety or quality accreditation badge (e.g. LOtC Quality Badge) is stated. ## Commercial
abbey-farm.md.price_and_structure: "Visits are FREE to schools." "As we are kindly funded by Natural England these visits are FREE to schools."
abbey-farm.md.booking_lead_time: "All visits must be pre-booked and a pre-visit is compulsory by the group leader." "Please note: For EVERY visit we require the group leader or teacher to make a pre-visit meeting covering health & safety, risk assessment and a work plan for the day. This usually takes about ½ hour and will be arranged when you book a visit date." "We are more than happy to run 'back to back' visits for one school to allow 2 (or possibly 3) consecutive groups to visit on one day, minimising the transport costs." ## Conversion
abbey-farm.md.how_to_book: "Please contact Jo at jo@abbeyfarming.com or 07795 396979 to book a visit." Site-wide contact: "Email: enquiries@abbeyfarming.com. School visits and weddings: Jo Nelstrop: 07795 396979."
abbey-farm.md.price_visible_without_asking: Yes — "Visits are FREE to schools" is stated directly on the Farm Visits and EYFS/Primary pages, without needing to ask.
abbey-farm.md.downloadable_pack: Yes — "download pack keystage 1" and "download pack keystage 2" information packs (EYFS/KS1 and KS2 editions) were found downloadable from the site.
abbey-farm.md.testimonials_from_schools: "Lovely environment and great learning experience." "A lovely visit, very friendly, fun and informative." "Despite the weather the children thoroughly enjoyed themselves and continued to talk about the visit at school the following day. There was a good balance of adult / whole group discussions and working in smaller groups. They really enjoyed their tractor ride too!" "Really interesting. Pitched at right level for the age group."
abbey-farm.md.title_and_opening_line: Title: "Farm Visits". Opening line: "Abbey Farm specifically caters for educational visits. We aim to provide schools with an opportunity to learn about where their food comes from, share the countryside we live in and learn about the environment." </content>

adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.programme_names: - "A quintessential School Trip!" - "school package" (teacher pack title, 2023)
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.activities_verbatim: (in the order given on the schools page and in the school-package-visit-guide-2023.pdf itinerary): - Tailored Educational Workshops (45-minute talk, KS1–KS3, delivered "In Dolly's") - Pre-Visit Learning Material - Pre-Visit Teacher Familiarisation - Higher/Further Educational groups talks: "Farming and Climate Change"; "Farm to Fork"; "Bio-security – Zoonotic disease control on a farm visitor attraction" - Self-Led Activities: play equipment, treasure hunt in the woodlands, animal identification "bingo" on the rare breeds trail - Teacher/Leader Information Packs - Post-Visit Learning Material (via "Explorify") - Rare Breed Walkway Challenge (looped walk, approximately 20 minutes long, laminated bingo cards) - Feeding the animals (goats and sheep; feed shoots for double-fenced animals such as cattle) - Woodland Walk Activity: "Den building", "Mud kitchen" - Conservation area: "Bird spotting", "Bug detecting" - "Take a look inside our live bee hive (In the warmer months)" - Play Areas (outdoor play areas, allocated time; inflatable bouncy pillows "only open when they are dry") - Discovery Barn & Animal Barn Exploration (group splits into two, 15 minutes per barn before swapping over)
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.duration: Talk/workshop is 45 minutes; the Rare Breed Walkway loop is approximately 20 minutes; Discovery/Animal Barn visits are 15 minutes per barn; arrival window is between 9.30am and 10am; full-day itinerary sent in advance.
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.group_size_min_max: Pricing tiers run from "Up to 20 children and 4 adults" to "Up to 100 children and 20 adults"; groups "Over 100" must contact for details. Pre-visit teacher familiarisation is capped at "up to 4 adults".
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.participant_thresholds: - Pre-Visit Teacher Familiarisation: up to 4 adults - Pricing tiers, each stated as a maximum: 20 children + 4 adults; 30 children + 6 adults; 40 children + 8 adults; 50 children + 10 adults; 70 children + 14 adults; 100 children + 20 adults; over 100 by quote ## Inventory
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.facilities: Waymarked map; designated indoor lunch area ("education room"; additional lunch area allocated if more than 2 schools visit on one day); coach drop-off separate from car park; bag/lunchbox storage; hand-washing stations in both barns, at the end of the walkway, and in toilet blocks (running water, soap, disposable towels/hot-air dryers; the guide states "hand sanitisers are not a suitable replacement"); Changing Places washroom at Admissions, described as "brand-new for 2023"; accessible toilet and baby change; listening posts; sensory play area; viewing tower; fire assembly point; flat-surfaced pathways to all barns and the Rare Breed's Trail; low-level wash facilities; Ox Shed restaurant and other catering outlets, stated as unable to cater for school groups (schools must bring packed lunches, though pre-purchased ice-creams can be arranged).
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.equipment_provided: Animal feed ("Animal Snacks") supplied for the group on arrival; laminated bingo cards for the Rare Breed Walkway Challenge; welcome pack containing wristbands for accompanying adults; downloadable pre-visit PowerPoint presentation; teacher/leader information packs for self-led activities; booking itinerary/schedule emailed in advance.
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.staff_qualifications_stated: none listed beyond "a member of staff" and "our expert team"; no named qualifications, certifications, or training levels are stated for the education/handling staff. Vehicles: "Only trained members of staff to drive vehicles in farm park during opening hours."
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.accessibility_provision: Free disabled parking next to the entrance; Changing Places Toilet with ceiling hoist, height-adjustable changing table and wash basin; queue-jump option via the gift shop for sensory needs/autism; Essential Companion +1 free ticket with Access Card or Digital Access Pass (DAP) via partner Nimbus; mobility scooter hire, £10/day plus £50 deposit, first come first served; extra-wide ramped doorways to shop and café; concrete, gravelled and grassy walkways described as wide enough for wheelchairs, "many of these areas are sloped and may require a bit of strength to navigate in a manual wheelchair"; listening activities/audio for visually impaired visitors; assistance dogs allowed "as long as they are working at the time"; printed copy of seasonal demonstration information available on request, one week's notice; baby changing facilities and a microwave for baby food/milk in the Ox Shed; breastfeeding welcomed "in all non-animal contact areas"; all areas pushchair accessible; for school groups specifically, the guide states "If you have any specific needs, please get in touch and we can see if we can adapt our program for you directly as a booking outside of our standard school package."
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.animal_species_held: Cattle (Highland, White Park, Albion, Gloucester Bull breeds named); sheep (Norfolk Horn, Hebridean, Border Leicester, Cotswold, Shetland breeds named); horses/ponies (Suffolk Punch, Exmoor breeds named); pigs (Tamworth, Berkshire, British Lop, Saddleback, Old Spot, Iron Age breeds named); goats (Golden Guernsey, Pygmy, Bagot, Boer breeds named); poultry (Brahma chickens, Call Ducks, chicks — noted as sometimes withdrawn from public areas during Avian Influenza outbreaks); guinea pigs; rabbits; donkeys; bees (live bee hive, viewable "in the warmer months"). ## Curriculum
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.curriculum_links: Talks pitched by Key Stage (KS1–KS3); "STEM focus" cited via the Explorify partnership; talks for higher/further education named "Farming and Climate Change", "Farm to Fork", "Bio-security – Zoonotic disease control on a farm visitor attraction"; no named National Curriculum subject or attainment-target references found on the pages read.
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.teacher_materials: Downloadable pre-visit learning material/resources aligned to the talk topic; downloadable pre-visit PowerPoint presentation; downloadable information pack for self-led activities; post-visit learning material signposted via the free "Explorify" teacher platform (search "Cotswold Farm Park"); school-package-visit-guide-2023.pdf teacher pack including a park map and station-by-station activity notes with "Talking Point" prompts for staff to use. ## Trust
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.risk_assessment_available: Yes — "A publicly available Risk Assessment for school teachers and leaders managing their school groups", downloadable from the website (schoolvisits.pdf), rated "MEDIUM RISK" overall with a stated 67% risk reduction from control measures, itemising specific hazards (cars/coaches, uneven surfaces, log-burning stove, slippery surfaces, farm vehicles, lost children, unauthorised access, electrical equipment, zoonosis, play equipment, fire, chemicals/medicines, insect bites, falling from height, weather, animal bites) each paired with a control measure.
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.child_safety_checks_stated: none listed — no DBS or equivalent vetting statement found on the pages or documents read.
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.accreditations_displayed: "Cotswold Farm Park has NFAN, AAA accreditation under the animal attraction assurance scheme" (stated within the risk-assessment control measures, with a link to farmattractions.net's Animal Attraction Assurance Scheme page). ## Commercial
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.price_and_structure: Tiered flat group price by size band: up to 20 children + 4 adults £250; up to 30 children + 6 adults £300; up to 40 children + 8 adults £360; up to 50 children + 10 adults £400; up to 70 children + 14 adults £420; up to 100 children + 20 adults £500; over 100, contact for quote. Further/higher education groups: £12.50 per student. "Our pricing structure has remained unchanged this year. If you have larger groups, the cost per child is reduced, so why not bring 2 classes along instead of one?"
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.adults_free_ratio: Adult numbers are bundled into each price tier (e.g. 4 adults free within the £250/20-child tier, 20 adults within the £500/100-child tier) rather than stated as a standalone ratio; the risk assessment separately states a supervision ratio "generally 5:1 but may be greater depending on the needs of the children."
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.catering: "Please bring a packed lunch as our catering outlets are unable to cater for school groups." Pre-purchased ice-creams can be arranged in advance for collection during the visit. Education room / additional lunch area allocated for storage and eating packed lunches.
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.cancellation_and_weather: none listed on the pages and documents read (no cancellation policy or weather/wet-weather policy text found).
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.booking_lead_time: none listed as a stated minimum lead time; the booking itinerary/schedule is said to be sent "shortly in advance of the visit" and "should have received a week before the visit" (a communication timing, not a booking lead time requirement). ## Conversion
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.how_to_book: Online enquiry form on the schools page (school name, organiser name, contact email/invoicing email, address, phone, Key Stage, estimated number of children, special requirements, date, flexible dates, data-consent checkbox); further/higher education groups directed to email hello@cotswoldfarmpark.co.uk.
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.price_visible_without_asking: Yes — the full tiered price table is published on the schools page.

adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.testimonials_from_schools: none listed on the pages read.
adam-hensons-cotswold-farm-park.md.title_and_opening_line: Title: "Cotswold School Trips | Cotswold Farm Park" (on-page heading "A quintessential School Trip!"). Opening line: "Immerse your students in an engaging and educational experience at Cotswold Farm Park, where learning meets fun."

almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.programme_names: - Learning Visits (the overall school offer) - Inventing Tomorrow (full title: "Inventing Tomorrow - The Story of James Young") - Voices of Shale (subtitled "(The Child)") - Sow and Grow - Meet Our Rare Breeds
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.activities_verbatim: - "A 40-minute guided session led by a member of our Learning Team" - "Resources to support to self-led activity" - "Suggested pre and post visit activities to support your learning visit" - Inventing Tomorrow - The Story of James Young: "Who is James Young? Discover more about the life and innovations of the Scottish Chemist. How did James Young's pioneering discoveries shape the future of the Scottish Shale oil industry? Join us on a fact finding mission to unlock the history of Young, take on the STEAM challenge and unleash your creativity and innovation. This activity is suitable for primary school children working at second level." - Voices of Shale (The Child): "Explore the voices of the Shale Oil community in this hands on workshop and take on the role of a child in the mines. Immerse yourself in the daily hardships and the physical conditions they endured. Join us in our handling session where we will look at objects, photographs and listen to stories from the past. This activity is suitable for primary school children working at first and second level." - Sow and Grow: "Available only during the Autumn term. This session explores our orchards, polytunnel and wartime garden to support historical themes or study of diet and sustainability issues. This activity is suitable for primary school children working at early, first and second level." - Meet Our Rare Breeds: "Our animal house is home to many rare breeds animals, which normally include goats, sheep, donkeys and horses. Meet the residents, and consider the characteristics that they share, and what makes them different. This activity is suitable for primary school children aged 5+, and can address learning outcomes related to classification and characteristics of living things. This activity is suitable for primary school children working at early and first level" - Tractor and Trailer rides: "Tractor and Trailer rides are available on most dates @ £1 per person. These must be pre-booked."
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.duration: "Discovery Sessions are hands-on learning activities that can be linked to curriculum studies and are delivered by an experienced demonstrator. Sessions usually involve groups of 15-20 children and last about 40 minutes. Large parties are therefore split into a number of sessions. Children can only receive a single discovery session during the course of their visit."
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.group_size_min_max: "The school class must be of at least 15 children; we can accommodate smaller ASN groups." Discovery Sessions "usually involve groups of 15-20 children."
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.participant_thresholds: - Learning Visit qualification: "The school class must be of at least 15 children; we can accommodate smaller ASN groups" - Discovery Session: "Sessions usually involve groups of 15-20 children" - Group Visits (non-qualifying groups): "The group must contain 20 or more individuals who are charged for admission" - School Group and Nursery ratio: "School Group and Nurseries eligible for 1 free adult ticket for every 10 paying children" ## Inventory
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.facilities: Millfield site of 23 acres described as "natural, built and cultural heritage and with an abundance of indoor and outdoor adventure areas"; Rare Breed Farm; The Mill & Water Wheel (Livingston Mill, historic waterwheel); The Railway Station (narrow-gauge light railway); The Shale Oil Museum; Play and Adventure areas including soft play; picnic barn and picnic areas for eating packed lunches; "Across the site there are a range of covered (unheated) spaces suitable for eating packed lunches"; café and Shepherd's Hut food outlet; disabled parking bays "positioned directly in front of the visitor entrance"; toilet cubicles with wide entrances and rails in the main farm toilets, and accessible unisex toilets in the cafe, the threshing barn, and the soft play area
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.staff_qualifications_stated: Discovery Sessions "delivered by an experienced demonstrator"; a "40-minute guided session led by a member of our Learning Team"
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.accessibility_provision: "There is level access into the main reception building through doors that are 900mm wide. All other buildings on site are on a single level and are fully accessible, other than a small cellar in the watermill, most of which can be viewed from outside." "There are no steps in any of the main circulation routes around the site, although there is a modest slope in front of the mill buildings. All pathways are hard surfaced, or have a rolled-stone finish." "Other than a tiny area downstairs in one of the mill buildings, all of Almond Valley is wheelchair and buggy accessible, though some of the outdoor pathways can be uneven and/or wet/muddy." "Due to the historic nature of our Narrow-Gauge railway the carriages are unable to accommodate wheelchairs and buggies, however our Tractor Ride is fully accessible." "Play facilities cater for all abilities, but include some active play equipment, such as swings and slides, which are particularly suited for those with impaired mobility." "Visitors who require special assistance are offered free admission for one accompanying carer when they pay the full adult/concession/child price." "Assistance dogs that are accompanying a disabled person are welcome."
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.animal_species_held: goats (Bagot and Pygmy goats named); sheep (North Ronaldsay sheep named); donkeys; horses (Clydesdale horses named); polecat ferrets; harvest field mice; alpacas; miniature animals in "Wings & Whiskers"; poultry ("traditional breeds of poultry") ## Curriculum
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.curriculum_links: "In consultation with school children and leaders, we've created an innovative and engaging heritage education programme aligned to the Curriculum for Excellence and responding to Learning for Sustainability." Each session's suitability is stated by Curriculum for Excellence level: Inventing Tomorrow (second level); Voices of Shale (first and second level); Sow and Grow (early, first and second level); Meet Our Rare Breeds (early and first level, primary children aged 5+).
almond-valley-heritage-centre.md.teacher_materials: "Each class are given resource material to assist with their onsite learning." Downloadable Visit Risk Assessment. Downloadable "Industry Code of Practice — guidance for teachers and other farm visits by children." ## Trust

aongatete-outdoor-education-centre.md.programme_names: No single named "school programme"; the Educational Groups booking page serves schools, youth groups and adult education groups, who select activities from eight named activity categories: Bush Walks and Tramps; Outdoor Safety & Bush Craft; Aongatete River Activities; Nature & Environmental Studies; Self-Confidence / Personal Performance; Night Time Activities; Team Building Challenges; Gap Fillers & other activities. Within Nature & Environmental Studies is a named sub-programme, "Aongatete Forest Discovery Program".
aongatete-outdoor-education-centre.md.activities_verbatim: From the Activities overview page: "we work with you to create customised camp programmes that match your group's goals, age range, and budget. Simply choose the activities you're interested in, and our experienced team will help design a safe, engaging, and memorable outdoor learning experience — with support and activity SOPs provided." Bush Walks and Tramps: Nature Trail: A 20 minute walk through easy terrain following a track with signs about the areas Natural Habitat. This track is ideal for any other nature study activities. Short Loop: A 1 hour walk through intermediate terrain, this track is a B grade and is about 2.2km long. Long Loop: A 3 hr walk with challenging parts and river crossings. A C grade track about 6.5 km long. Swimming Hole Track/River Crossing towards North/South Track: a 30 minute one-way walk to the river. Upland Road Track: an easy C grade. It takes about 2 1/2 - 3 hours to reach AOEC and is about 5km long and includes a river crossing. Wairere Falls (8 hrs one way): several schools start their AOEC camp by walking in from the Wairere Falls. Outdoor Safety & Bush Craft: The Aongatete Survivor Experience (Full Day)*: a full day experience led by a trained and experienced AOEC Instructor, covering Trip Planning, Outdoor Safety & Environmental Care, Navigation with Map & Compass, Outdoor Cooking, Shelter Building, Environmental Care, River Safety. The Aongatete Survivor Experience (Half Day)*: a half day experience, 3hrs in the bush, led by a trained and experienced AOEC Instructor. Shelter Building: a simple session designed to learn how to shelter from the elements in different ways. Fire Lighting: led by a trained and experienced AOEC Instructor. Outdoor Cooking: children can cook on hobo or hexi stoves; equipment available to hire. Navigation: Basic Map Orienteering on Lodge Grounds; Map Reading using a Topo50 Map; Compass Confidence Basics; Compass Navigation through the bush led by an AOEC Instructor. Camp Outs: sleep in dormitories, in a tent, under canvas or tarpaulin bivvy style, or under the stars. Aongatete River Activities: Aongatete River Challenge: an adventurous walk up/down the river with experienced AOEC Instructors. River Studies & Discoveries: find and watch eels, what lives in our rivers, plants that grow in or near the river. Dam Building. Rock Sculptures. Boat Races. Swimming. Nature & Environmental Studies: "Thanks to the generous support of the Wright Family Foundation, all of our Environment Education Activities are fully subsidised for 2025, 2026, and 2027." Aongatete Forest Discovery Program: an AOEC Instructor led, full day hands on program where students explore the forest, learn about plants and trees, forest colours, pest control and conservation, and identify birds; concludes with a night walk. Forest Discovery - Get to know a tree. Forest Discovery - Native Birds in our Forest. River Studies & Discoveries (as above). Layers of the Forest: can be extended with a team building lesson to last a whole morning or afternoon. Pest Control & Conservation. Nature Trail: 15 minutes to 2 hours depending on detail and design. Nature Crafts & Forest Art. Rongoa Maori Medicine: with AOEC Rongoa qualified Instructor. Waste Management (Mandatory). Night Time in the Forest. Solos: can be run day or night, for any length of time. Self-Confidence / Personal Performance: Challenge Course: informal (play time, adult supervision and spotting required) or formal (set goals and objectives) sessions. Archery: "an AOEC trained staff instructor is required to take this session." Indoor Climbing Wall: "(Currently unavailable)". Night Time Activities: Burma Trail. Night Walk: equipped with torches, magnifying glasses and night creatures identification cards. Candle Trail. Camp Concert. Camp Fire: "*Strict Conditions apply". Bouldering (on the indoor climbing wall): "this activity can only be run with the presence of our rock climbing instructors." Team Building Challenges: Pancake Challenge. "Below are collection of short challenges commonly used as team development activities... Each activity takes 15-20 minutes depending on the age and capabilities of the students." Tram Tracks. Lava Flow. Tyre Shift. Stacker. Spot Maze/Swamp Crossing. Balancing Pole. The Wall. Pipe Line. Tarp Flip. Gap Fillers & other activities: Fire drill: "a quick 20-30 minute exercise or you can spend a good hour." Bouldering (on the indoor climbing wall): "this activity can only be run with the presence of our rock climbing instructors." Camp Journal: printable PDF journal available to download. Nature Crafts: Nature Weaving and Leaf Creatures.
aongatete-outdoor-education-centre.md.duration: No single fixed duration for a school visit as a whole; occupancy is per booked day/night (see Commercial > booking-related occupancy times below). Individual activities carry stated durations as transcribed above, ranging from 15 minutes (some team-building challenges) to 8 hours one way (Wairere Falls track).

aongatete-outdoor-education-centre.md.participant_thresholds: Minimum charge of $500 per day/night applies for groups smaller than 22 occupants. Maximum accommodation capacity of 92 people; regulation maximum of 100 people on site. ## Inventory
aongatete-outdoor-education-centre.md.facilities: Dormitory-style bunkroom accommodation for up to 92 people (site regulation maximum 100). Separate male and female bathroom and toilet facilities. Wheelchair access provided to buildings, toilets and showers. Well-equipped self-catering kitchen. Lounge/dining area seating 100 people with a fireplace. Main Building Dorms: 20 bunks in 3 bunk rooms (two sleeping 8, one sleeping 4). Main Building Ablutions: shower (electric hot water cylinder), sinks, two toilets. The Lions Den Dorm: 32 bunk beds in 8 cubicles of 4. The Nettleingham Dorm: 40 bunk beds in 10 cubicles of 4. Ablution Block: male and female facilities each with 4 toilets and 4 showers, including a shower and toilet suitable for wheelchair use. Boiler Room & Laundry: industrial coin-operated washing machine and dryer, Marshal Boiler supplying hot water. Activities Centre containing the indoor climbing wall (noted elsewhere as "Currently unavailable"). Automated security gate at the lodge entrance.

auckland-zoo.md.activities_verbatim: - "Early Childhood Education — Visit the Zoo with your little ones." - "Dinosaur Discovery — Explore the amazing prehistoric world of dinosaurs through song, story, movement, and play! Available for: ECE, from 10 June 2026" - "Awesome Aotearoa — What has shaped New Zealand's biodiversity? Available for: Years 0 - 13" - "Adaptations — How have animals adapted to their habitat? Available for: Years 0 - 13" - "Zoo Care (formally known as Role of the Modern Zoo) — Taking care of our animals every day in a way that ensures their overall wellbeing. Available for: Years 0 - 13" - "Classification — Discover the fascinating world of animal grouping and classification. Available for: Years 0 - 4" - "Matariki — Discover how we can celebrate Matariki through stories that link people to nature and Aotearoa's native wildlife. Available for: Years 0 - 8" - "Behavioural Enrichment — Explore one of the ways we engage and enrich the species in our care. Available for: Years 0 - 8" - "Whakapapa — Discover how living things are classified in te ao Māori (the Māori worldview) Available for: Years 0 - 8" - "Protecting Aotearoa — Learn how Aotearoa is home to unique animals which face modern day threats from introduced pests. (also referred to as "the Lord of the Rings Trail") - "A Fine City" — "Your group will travel to Norwich to examine the development of the city through the centuries." - "Pirates" — "The purpose of this day is the personal development of the individual child combined with an element of team building." - "Twilight Safari" — "Very few children (or indeed, adults) have ever experienced the woods at night. The Twilight Safari is an excellent opportunity to do so." - "Medieval Shrine" — "This study unit is based on a visit to the village of Walsingham in North Norfolk." - "Rock Pools, Geology & Erosion" — "West Runton is known throughout the world for its geology." - "Woodland Fun & Hide Building" — "This activity involves an examination of the woodland habitat of the National Trust estate at Felbrigg which is directly opposite our Centre." - "From Source to Sea" — "This activity involves following the River Glaven along its course from as near to the source as possible to the estuary at Blakeney." - "The Ropes Course" — "NEW ADDITION." "Enjoy the views and build your sense of adventure with our exciting ropes course. Opened in 2023, the ropes course is a real Aylmerton 'highlight'." Named park features (from park-features and animals pages): "Waterfall"; "Ancient Woodland"; "Three circular walking trails" — Blue Trail ("gentler walk through the ancient oak woodland," site of the "Children's Nature Challenge"), Red Trail ("stunning waterfall and its dramatic 70ft cascade," "boulder scramble"), Purple Trail ("views of the beautiful lower falls on more rugged terrain"); "Café & facilities"; "Animals"; "Keeper Talks"; "Children's Nature Challenge"; "Ample free parking"; "Dogs welcome." Animal Discovery Zone described as containing "majestic pythons to intriguing invertebrates" and a "Keeper Kitchen." "Chat to Tosh!" (a Blue and Gold Macaw). "Feed the Goats" (goat feed sold from the Gift Shop, £1, "limited and sold on a first-come, first-served basis"). "Kid's Activity Pack" (£2.99 from the gift shop, "spotter guides" and other activities).
becky-falls-woodland-park.md.duration: Itinerary spans 10:15am to approximately 2:30pm (based on the timed slots in the group itinerary document, "Updated 26/03/2024"). Meet-the-Keeper talks run "every hour from 11am to 4pm" as the general (non-group) timetable.
becky-falls-woodland-park.md.group_size_min_max: "We offer an educational group rate for groups of 10 or more children." Booking form: "15% discount for groups of 15+." No stated maximum group size.
becky-falls-woodland-park.md.participant_thresholds: - Educational group rate: 10 or more children - 15% discount: groups of 15 or more - Accompanying-adult ratio: "1:5 for Key Stage 1 & 2" and "1:10 for Key Stage 3 & 4" (booking form); Code of Conduct states this as "1 adult for every 5 students (primary school age)" and "1 adult for every 10 children (secondary school age)" - Animal Experiences (Meerkat/Reptile, general public not specifically school groups): 2–4 person experience, paying adult must accompany children aged 8–15, maximum 4 people total - Junior Keeper Experience: 1–4 child experience, adult must accompany children aged 8–15 ## Inventory
becky-falls-woodland-park.md.facilities: Woodland Café (indoor, "cream teas and cakes to burgers and freshly prepared paninis," gluten-free and vegan options available on request); Gift Shop; picnic area adjacent to the Blue Walk (cannot be pre-booked; "limited storage facilities for packed lunches" available on request); toilets adjacent to the café, including disabled toilet facilities and unisex baby changing; designated coach bays in the car park, free coach parking; Animal Discovery Zone (wheelchair-friendly, "Keeper Kitchen" visible); Children's Nature Challenge trail-side activity boards on the Blue Trail with a free prize on completion.
becky-falls-woodland-park.md.equipment_provided: Child carriers (backpack, ages 6 months+; front baby carrier, under 6 months) available on loan from the Gift Shop for a returnable deposit. becky-falls-woodland-park.md.staff_qualifications_stated: "We have qualified first aiders on site at the main café." "A dedicated team of zookeepers who care for our animals and reptiles" (guidelines document, in the context of the zoo licence). No further named qualification or certificate body stated.
becky-falls-woodland-park.md.accessibility_provision: "Due to the nature of the woodland walks, the trails are not accessible to wheelchair users." bocketts-farm.md.activities_verbatim: - "A Small Animal Encounters session" - "A Tractor and Trailer Ride - lots of animals to see along the way and often great views of London!" - "A tour of the farm by your team leader (Reception years and older only, unless requested)" - "Pig Racing - not to be missed!" - "Lunch" - "Free Time - an opportunity to visit the animals again or play (PLEASE NOTE THE USE OF OUR INDOOR SOFT PLAY IS NOT GUARANTEED)" Full stated itinerary sequence: "On arrival, you will be greeted by your team leader and shown to your designated undercover area. Every school and nursery group is given their own undercover area where they can leave their belongings and eat their lunch, so that you can enjoy your visit whatever the weather." Then "The whole group will then be given a health and safety briefing and the structure and timings of the day will be explained." Then the day's activities as listed above. General (non-school-specific) farm activities pages also describe: "Small Animal Encounters — Meet some of the farm's smallest residents in our cosy small animal village. Say hello to our friendly guinea pigs, rabbits and chickens. Sessions run daily at 11am, 12pm, 2pm, 3pm and 4pm." "Pony Rides — Enjoy a short pony ride around our woodland track. Children must be over the age of 3 to ride and under 12 years or 45kg. Each ride costs £3, payable by card. Sessions run from 11am - 12pm + 2.30pm - 3.30pm during Weekends and School Holidays and 3pm - 3.30pm Mon - Fri during term time." "Pig Racing — Don't miss the action! Our racing pigs run daily at 12:45 PM and 3:45 PM, pick your favourite, cheer them on, and see who takes the crown at the finish line." "Tractor & Trailer Rides — Climb aboard for a fun and relaxing ride around the farm. Meet the animals, learn about farm life, and take in the views of the Surrey Hills and even London on a clear day. £2 per person, approx. 15 minutes. Monday to Friday during term time, rides run at 12pm, 2pm, 3pm and 4pm. During weekends and school holidays, rides run regularly throughout the day."

bore-place.md.programme_names: Marvellous Minibeasts; Habitat Detectives; Sow and Grow; Field to Fork; Team Challenge Day; Weekly Outdoor Education Programmes; Home Education Level 1 Awards 2026-27 (Level 1 Award in Land-based Studies); Additional Needs Club; Bore Place Family Adventure; School Residentials (delivered "in partnership with the Ernest Cook Trust's OWL Collaboration programme")
bore-place.md.activities_verbatim: School Day Visits — every visit: "A tour around our regenerative farm giving your class an opportunity to explore and take part in a citizen science survey is part of every visit." Marvellous Minibeasts: - Minibeast hunting in logs, leaf litter and/or grassland - Meadow walk - Games to learn about predators and prey, and camoflage - Maybe some pond dipping! Habitat Detectives: - Seasonal survey e.g. worm, hedgerow, butterfly - Habitat trail to compare types of habitats - Footprint survey tunnels and mammal ID - Nest building or den building - If there's time, an animal signs scavenger hunt Sow and Grow: - Parts of a plant, germination and pollination games - Visit the garden to see the range of plants and what parts we can eat - Exploring the importance of soil - Plant a seed to take home/grow at school Field to Fork: - Foraging or harvesting ingredients - Look at natural vs. processed foods - Cook a simple food (KS2 only) - Taste testing Team Challenge Day (Suitable for KS2; adaptable for KS3 and KS4): - Orienteering style challenge trail - Den building - Firelighting - Campfire cooking Weekly Outdoor Education Programmes: activities not individually named on the education page; programme is described as delivering "hands-on outdoor experiences" toward accredited qualifications
bore-place.md.duration: Sample generic itinerary in the Teacher Handbook: "1000 Welcome, introduction and safety chat... 1030 Explore the farm... 1200 Lunch... 1230 Theme based activity... 1400 Session ends" — a four-hour day, 10:00 to 14:00. Weekly Outdoor Education Programmes: "Students attend a one day per week over a 34-week academic year." Home Education Level 1 Award in Land-based Studies: "Time: 10:00-12:00 (ages 11–14), 13:00-15:00 (ages 15–17)." Additional Needs Club: "Each session runs from 09:00-13:00."
bore-place.md.group_size_min_max: School Day Visits: "All programmes are designed for a class of up to 30 pupils... If you would like to bring more than one class on the same day, we can often accommodate two classes (up to 60 pupils) on a Friday." SEN classes: "the maximum group size for an SEN visit is 20 pupils, though this depends on the needs of the group." Weekly Outdoor Education Programmes: "Schools can book for a group of up to 10 students." Home Education Level 1 Award: "Class size: around 6 learners."
bore-place.md.participant_thresholds: - School Day Visits, maximum 30 pupils per class ("All programmes are designed for a class of up to 30 pupils") - School Day Visits (two classes, Friday only), maximum 60 pupils ("we can often accommodate two classes (up to 60 pupils) on a Friday") - SEN School Day Visits, maximum 20 pupils ("the maximum group size for an SEN visit is 20 pupils") - Weekly Outdoor Education Programmes, maximum 10 students ("Schools can book for a group of up to 10 students") - Home Education Level 1 Award, class size around 6 learners ("Class size: around 6 learners") - Residentials, accommodation for up to 28 guests ("Accommodation is available for up to 28 guests (children and accompanying adults) in The Old Stable") - Corporate/group stays, groups as large as 65 ("We offer accommodation for small groups as well as groups as large as 65") ## Inventory

brownings-farm.md.activities_verbatim: Under "YOUR VISIT" (the structure of a visit): - Introduction- which will consist of a brief outline of the farm and an explanation of the ongoing projects. - Farm walk- we explore the different areas of the farm focusing on various habitats which include the woodlands, fields, orchard and ponds. - Interactive Activity- This depends on the learning objectives you have for your students. The activities range from discovering different species of plants and animals in the woodlands which include building a hybernation chamber and and installing wildlife boxes to provide homes for protected species like bats, owls and dormice. - We will look at cattle husbandry and discuss sustainable farming practices. - Summing up your visit- We will finish by evaluating what we have learnt and discussing the importance of farming practices within the environment. We will discuss what choices we can make and action we can take that will restore our environment and wildlife. Under "INTERACTIVE ACTIVITY OPTIONS FOR YOUR STUDENTS": - Pond dipping and species identification. - Measuring field parcel sizes and calculating fence distances. - Collecting and recording samples of plants and bugs. - Identifying indicator species like butterflies and bees. - Comparing organic and non-organic pastureland for species diversification. - Identifying different bird & insect habitats. - Damn building to create water bodies. - Finding and identifying badger sets and other animal habitats.
brownings-farm.md.facilities: Toilet and washing facilities; Parking; Tea, Coffee & biscuits for staff (listed under "Onsite Facilities & Resources").
brownings-farm.md.staff_qualifications_stated: From "Meet the Team": John Nicholls BSc (Hons) Cert Ed. — "lives at Brownings Farm and will lead your visit. He is an associate lecturer in conservation and ecology at Brinsbury Agricultural college." Todd Lewis BSc (Hons), PhD, PTS card, ROLO H&S — "completed a BSc in Environmental Biology at University of London Wye College, followed by a PhD at the University of Surrey investigating environmental influences on the population ecology of amphibians in tropical forests... At UWE I teach across ecology, biogeography, conservation and environmental themes." Tabitha Allfrey BA (Hons) — "takes care of our website, administration and is an instructor on our farm visits... Her background is in teaching, publishing and student support."

ca-nature-grand-river-conservation-autho.activities_verbatim: - "During your visit, students will explore fields and forests and will have hands-on learning opportunities that encourage curiosity and nature connection. Every season brings new opportunities for learning. Using our imaginations, we might explore how animals use their senses, or we could follow clues and trails that animals leave behind. Spring offers a great opportunity to investigate the pond. Winter visits may give your students the opportunity to hand feed wild Black-Capped Chickadees." (Make Sense of Nature) - "During this program, outdoor \"child-centered\" play is our goal. The Nature Centre sites provide natural features like rocks, dirt, trees, bugs, flowers, mud, and water for children to enjoy and discover. Students will be able to dig, collect, build, splash and play. This program is rich in Vitamin \"N\" for nature." (Nature Play) - "A snowshoe hike to enjoy a little winter vitamin D. Investigate how a gentle hike changes your body's system - pulse, temperature and breathing rate. The length of the snowshoe hike will depend on grade level. Program dependent on snow depth." (Active Living: Snowshoeing) - "Camouflage like a weasel, migrate like red-winged blackbirds, store food like squirrels and hibernate like groundhogs. We will explore nature to discover what nature has to offer and how plants and animals prepare for seasonal changes." (Daily and Seasonal Changes) - "We will go on an interactive hike to discover the different types of animals and their needs and roles in helping to keep our ecosystem healthy. There may be the opportunity for students to some of the Nature Centre creature teachers and learn about their characteristics and needs." (Needs and Characteristics of Living Things: Our Living World) - "An animal's environment has an impact on its development and survival. Humans need to protect animals and the places where they live. Students will take a closer look at a habitat and the animals that can live there. Choose from Water Creatures, Incredible Insects, Birds of a Feather and Explore the Forest." (Growth and Changes in Animals) - "They can't hide. Discover clues left behind in the snow to learn about the local wildlife. An animal's tracks, scat, bite marks and sounds can all lead to a possible wildlife sighting. What feathered friends stick around for the winter? We will use our ears and some sunflower seeds to find out which feather friends are still local. Enjoy a close-up encounter with Black-Capped Chickadees." (Growth and Changes in Animals: Wonderful Winter Wildlife) - "Air and water form a major part of the environment and are essential materials for life. A fall or spring program may include a pollution simulation, water cycle game, temperature and wind speed measurements. A winter program will take a closer look at the composition of snow. With magnifiers, heat and filters we will melt, measure and examine snow. What do animals do when we are not around? In the fresh snow we will track some animals to discover what they do. We may be able to snowshoe with a full day booking." (Air and Water in the Environment) - "Are your students lost? Exploring in teams, students will try to find their way around the wilderness using a map. We will tour a map to discover how real life features are represented on a map, how hills are represented, which way is north, and what all the symbols mean." (People and Environment: Mapping / Active Living: Mapping) - "Soil is not dirt, but an essential source of life and nutrients for many organisms, including humans. From the tiniest soil particles to the giants of the plant world, students will learn that soil provides the foundation for the forests. Best combined with Growth and Changes in Plants to create a full day." (Soils in the Environment) - "Are you aware that one tree has the cooling effect of ten air conditioners? In this program, budding foresters will identify common coniferous and deciduous trees and learn about these giants of the plant world through activities, games and up-close encounters. Best combined with Soils in the Environment to create a full day." (Growth and Changes in Plants: Trees of the Forest) - "Plants and animals are interdependent and are adapted to meet their needs from the resources available in their particular habitat. Can amphibians survive in any habitat? Who can live in a forest under a log? These are some of the questions student biologists will answer when they investigate and compare different habitats." (Habitats and Communities: Home Sweet Habitat) - "How many endangered species can you name that live in Ontario? During this role-playing game, explore how humans have a major impact on endangered species and their habitats." (Habitats and Communities: Species at Risk Game) - "Feed a feathered friend. Explore ways to identify common and not-so-common birds living in our area. Students will use binoculars when we hike the trail to find a diversity of birds in different habitats." (Habitats and Communities: Birds of the Watershed) - "Using special aquatic dip nets, the students will catch creatures that live in a local stream or pond. After identifying the invertebrates using field guides and identification keys, the students will determine if the water is a healthy ecosystem. Students may touch a dragonfly nymph, capture a crayfish and discover damselflies. Rubber boots or water shoes are required. In the full day program, students will also examine the physical aspects of the water habitat; this determines what creature can live there." (Habitat and Communities: Water Ecology) - "Using all our senses we will become nature detectives and collect the clues left behind by wild creatures. What do deer beds look like, why is there a \"pile of coffee beans\" in the forest, are rabbits the only animals that hop, who is singing that song? Students will explore in small groups to collect clues and unravel the mysteries." (Habitats and Communities: Wild Animal Search) - "Reading a map in a classroom is one thing - applying map-reading skills outdoors is the real challenge. Exploring in teams students will navigate their way around the wilderness using a map. We will tour a map to discover how natural and human features are represented on maps, how hills are depicted, how distance is measured, which way is north, and what all the symbols mean." (Active Living: Cartography: A Map Game) - "Learn the basics of direction and how to navigate with a map and compass. With a bit of practice, the students will navigate their way to different locations outside. Each team of students will take a bearing and travel to several destinations around the property." (Active Living: Orienteering with a Compass and Map) - "Search for sedimentary, igneous, and metamorphic rocks as we explore the geology of southern Ontario. Find out how rocks are formed. Investigate the characteristics that make rocks and minerals different. Students may complete a Scavenger Hunt for Rock Hounds or make a trace fossil of natural materials to take back to school." (Rocks and Minerals) - "During this fun-filled, active program, students will build shelters with natural materials. During the full day program, lunch time may include a hotdog cookout. Students will do various experiments to learn about the importance of insulation and waterproofing in the winter." (Conservation of Energy and Resources: Survival - Shelter Building) - "Do you know people who have a GPS in their car, but are always lost? We unravel the wonders of this simple technology during this program. Students will learn how the compass and map relate to the GPS. After exploring how the GPS works, students will participate in a GPS scavenger hunt or course." (Active Living: GPS Navigation) - "Biodiversity is best learned outdoors where students can observe, examine and experience the diversity of life around them. Using nets students will collect invertebrates either from an aquatic or terrestrial ecosystem (or both for a full day). Students will examine and observe their finds to divide and classify them. If you chose to do the aquatic program your class preplan will include detailed notes about requirements for footwear and clothes. You will get wet!" (Biodiversity: Aquatic / Terrestrial) - "All living things are connected. Maintaining biodiversity is critical to the health of the planet. By playing the role of a predator or a prey animal in this active, food chain game, students will see how energy is transferred through an ecosystem. Discover how animals, including humans, interact and are affected by living and non-living parts of the environment." (Biodiversity: Predator Prey Game) - "Every animal, including humans, leave clues wherever they go. Using our awesome powers of observation we will decipher the clues left by the animals living around the nature centre. We might find cocoons, tracks, scat, body parts, left over food or hear the sounds of winter birds. In small groups the students will collect as many clues as possible to discover who lives here." (Biodiversity: Wildlife Survey) - "All organisms require energy and in obtaining that energy, interactions occur. Playing the role of mammals in this active game, students will experience how energy is gained, transferred or lost in an ecosystem. Discover how animals, including humans, interact and are affected by biotic and abiotic parts of the environment. Better understand the food chain through a predator or prey." (Interactions in the Environment: Predator Prey Game) - "Student biologists collect and identify aquatic animals from a water habitat. Using scientific equipment we take a close look at this aquatic ecosystem to see which creatures are consumers, predators or recyclers. Some of the creatures build their own homes; some can skate on top of the water. Many other discoveries will be made during this popular program. Your class preplan will include detailed notes about requirements for footwear and clothes. Students will be expected to go into the water and will get wet!" (Interactions in the Environment: Pond or Stream Ecology) - "During this fun-filled, active winter day, students will build shelters with natural and human-made materials to keep themselves warm. We will see who survives the activity by building a warm shelter." (Heat in the Environment: Shelters) - "Join us for a unique opportunity to learn about some of the area's largest dams. Learn about the role of conservation authorities in Ontario and how the dams, including the Guelph Lake Dam, help control water levels downstream. The dams are also a producer of hydro-electricity. Best combined with Everybody Lives Downstream for a full day program." (Water Systems: The Best Dam Tour) - "Find out where Guelph's water comes from, how it is treated before we use it and after we flush it. First, we'll tour Waterworks and discover how the city provides its residents with a clean and safe drinking supply 24 hours a day. Combined with a tour of the city's wastewater treatment plant, it is an awesome way to learn about water conservation in our community. Best combined with the Best Dam Tour for a full day program." (Water Systems: Everybody Lives Downstream) - "Aquatic invertebrates are closely connected to their environment and human activities upstream have a lasting effect on what can live in the water. By collecting living creatures and using a biotic index students will determine the health of this ecosystem. We will investigate the health and possible solutions to human impacts on this habitat. We will discuss how scientific data can be used to look at the potential impacts of climate change on ecosystem's sustainability. Rubber boots or water shoes are needed." (Sustainable Ecosystems and Climate Change: Aquatic Ecosystem Survey) - "Students take part in a population study of an ecosystem. They collect and identify many species of animals, either in an aquatic or terrestrial habitat. This is followed by a release and recapture to determine a population estimate of a particular species. An example species is the eastern crayfish in an aquatic ecosystem. We will assess impacts of climate change on ecosystem sustainability and on various communities and describe way to mitigate these impacts. Best combined with an Aquatic Ecosystem Survey" (Sustainable Ecosystems and Climate Change: Crayfish Aquatic Population Study) - "Students, playing the role of mammals in this active game, will see how energy is transferred through an ecosystem. Discover how animals, including humans, interact and are affected by living and non-living parts of the environment. See the food chain through the eyes of a coyote, skunk or mouse. We will assess impacts of climate change on ecosystem sustainability and on various communities and describe way to mitigate these impacts." (Sustainable Ecosystems and Climate Change: Predator and Prey) - "Students visit a natural ecosystem, and collect and examine live animals, to discover their shared and different characteristics. They will understand the concept and importance of diversity in natural habitats, and how humans affect biodiversity. Chose an Aquatic or Terrestrial program. If you chose to do the Aquatic program your class preplan will include detailed notes about requirements for footwear and clothes. Students will be expected to go into the water and will get wet!" (Human Impact on the Environment, Human Health and the Environment: Biodiversity Rules!) - "This program can take place over one day, or a series of days. The GRCA manages water and other natural resources on behalf of 38 municipalities and close to one million residents of the Grand River watershed. Through hands-on activities in the field, students learn management techniques that the GRCA currently uses in its projects and programs. Options include reservoir and river studies, floodplain mapping, habitat restoration, wildlife and forest management, GPS and others." (Human-Environment Interactions, Geographic Foundations: Environment and Resource Management) - "Identifying benthic invertebrates (small but fascinating bottom-dwelling animals) in rivers is one way to assess the health of a stream or river. With the expert guidance of a GRCA biologist, students visit a local stream or river and learn to catch and identify these indicators of water quality. Students must pass an on-site field identification test to complete this certification. Your class preplan will include detailed notes about requirements for footwear and clothes. Students will be expected to go into the water and will get wet!" (Introduction to Stream Assessment Protocol Certification) - "Students learn how to identify many of our fascinating local birds. A presentation outlines how to use size, shape, song, colour, habitat and habits to make this a nice challenge. We'll head outside to look for our local feathered friends with a GRCA naturalist, using binoculars and field guides to help in our identification. Later in the day, students will take part in an independent bird survey to demonstrate the skills they have learned." (Species Identification Certification - Birds) - "This program can take place over one day, or a series of days. Students take part in a habitat restoration project, such as 'rabbitat' construction (shelter for small animals), tree planting, stream rehabilitation, invasive plant removal or erosion control, among others. A habitat restoration tour will show students areas that have been worked on and others that are in need of restoration. At lunch - students watch a presentation to learn about projects undertaken by the GRCA to restore, rehabilitate or create natural habitats within our watershed. A short test at the end of this day will complete the certification." (Habitat Restoration Certification) - "Students learn to identify a wide variety of local coniferous and deciduous trees. A GRCA naturalist will introduce tree identification techniques, such as distinguishing opposite and alternate branching, bud or leaf type, bark characteristics and more. A field identification test will complete this certification." (Species Identification Certification - Trees) - "GPS skills are an important part of our world today and used in numerous jobs or fields of study. GPS certification is mandatory for numerous SHSM sectors including Environment. Our two day program gives you both a Map & Compass certification along with a GPS one. Day 1 will start in a classroom and we'll introduce your students to the GRCA online mapping tool (GIS skills) and learn to read topographic maps. In the afternoon, we'll head outside and learn to use compass skills to orient ourselves in the real world. Day 2 we'll learn how to use GPS units in the field and how our organization (GRCA) uses GPS technology and mapping in a wide variety of its resource management projects. In the afternoon we'll combine our mapping, compass and GPS skills together to explore outdoors with some practical and fun activities." (Compass/Map, Global Positioning System (GPS) Certification) - "Students learn how watersheds, including reservoirs, river and land ecosystems, are managed to maintain healthy environments. Students tour water control structures such as dams or dikes, visit water treatment centres and learn how the GRCA manages our local watershed." (Watershed Management Certification) - "Our Nature Centres offer hands-on, curriculum-based outdoor education classes for students in Kindergarten through high school" (school programs page opening line) - "trained nature interpreters with a passion for kids and environmental education" (staff description) - "There is currently no availability for additional school program bookings" (current status statement) - "Whether it's a company picnic, family reunion or club celebration, we have many locations available to rent" (group facilities page opening line) - "Each person entering the conservation area must also pay the gate admission fee." (group facilities page) - "these facilities are booked by contacting the conservation area directly, and many need to be reserved well in advance" (group facilities page) - "Large barbeques are available at many locations, but not all." (group facilities page)

candlebark-farm.md.programme_names: none listed as a single named "programme" product. The venue instead operates as a self-catered/fully-catered residential campsite that a school books and staffs (via its own or Candlebark's optional instructors), assembling its own itinerary from an activities list. The downloadable "Sample Program" is headed with a sample school name and dates ("Big Hill Primary School 1-3 August") and is offered as a template, not a fixed product name.
candlebark-farm.md.activities_verbatim: (from the Activities page, in the order given):** Super Swooper (led by 2 instructors) Archery (instructor led) Canoeing (instructor led) Flying Fox (instructor led) Swimming Pool (lifeguard led) All Aboard Boundary Walk Camp Fire GaGa Ball Games Shed Golf Frisbee Low Ropes Course Night Trail Orienteering Photo Find and Treasure Hunt Rock Room Ski Race Spider Web Table Tennis and Games Shed The Campsite Booklet's "ON-SITE ACTIVITIES" table separately categorises these as Physical Activities, Group Initiative Activities and Passive Activities, each with a stated duration (see duration field).
candlebark-farm.md.duration: From the Campsite Booklet's on-site activities table: Archery 1 hr; Boundary Walk 1 hr; Canoeing 1 hr; Flying fox 1 hr; Gaga Ball 1 hr; Games Shed 1 hr; Golf Frisbee 1 hr; Low ropes Course 1 hr; Night trail 1 hr; Rock Room 1 hr; Super Swooper 1 hr; Swimming 1-2 hrs; All aboard 20 min; Ski race 20 min; Spider Web 30 min; Camp Fire 1 hr; Orienteering 1 hr; Photo Find 1 hr; Treasure Hunt 1 hr. The Sample Program (a 3-day/2-night itinerary for "Big Hill Primary School") shows a full timed schedule: e.g. Monday Session 1 starts 12:45 PM, 60 minutes; Session 2 starts 1:45 PM, 45 minutes; snack/rotation breaks of 30 minutes between sessions; Tuesday's six activity sessions each run 60 minutes from 9:15 AM to 5:00 PM; the camp runs from arrival at camp 10:30 AM Monday to arrival back at school 4:00 PM Wednesday.
candlebark-farm.md.group_size_min_max: "Candlebark Farm Enquiry Form (we are for groups of 40 to 112)". The Campsite Booklet states: "Activities are generally designed for one supervising adult led group of 10-15 campers." The campsite sleeps 112 across 3 accommodation blocks (16 bunkrooms plus a teacher's room).
candlebark-farm.md.participant_thresholds: Super Swooper: "90kg weight limit applies, best with two groups over two sessions"; "maximum turnover for the Super Swooper is 78 students per day"; Flying Fox: "70kg weight limit applies"; instructor-led optional extras have a stated minimum: "a minimum of 40 applies even if you have fewer" (per-person costed optional extras); linen provision "In minimum lots of 10"; recommended supervision ratio "one adult leader to ten campers (1:10) for schools and twice that for family groups (2:10)"; the enquiry form separately notes "at least 1 adult leader per 10-13 children" for schools running their own activities. ## Inventory
candlebark-farm.md.facilities: Candlebark Lodge (sleeping 54 in 9 ensuite bunkrooms); Stringybark Lodge (sleeping 26 in 3 ensuite bunkrooms and teacher's lounge); Blackwood Lodge (sleeping 32 in 4 ensuite bunkrooms); air-conditioned Conference Hall (9 x 18 m, carpeted, data projector, screen, surround sound, bluetooth/DVD/USB player, whiteboard); Games Shed with table tennis and Rock Room; air-conditioned dining room seating 112 (in Candlebark Lodge); air-conditioned art/craft room (in Stringybark Lodge); swimming pool (fenced); GaGa Pit; Giant Checkers Board; Camp Fire area; hard-wired smoke detectors in all bunkrooms, separated by fire-rated walls. "STOP PRESS: Our 16 ensuite bunkrooms now have air-conditioning" and "Our 30 kWh solar panels help offset our carbon footprint."
candlebark-farm.md.equipment_provided: 7 canoes (for Canoeing); modern archery gear (for Archery); the Super Swooper and Flying Fox rigs; low ropes course equipment; "we provide a towel and linen for participants to make their own bed" (linen is an extra-cost optional, $12.00 per person, in minimum lots of 10; beds are not made up by staff). Camper groups are required to bring their own first aid kit: "groups are required to bring their own first-aider with first aid kit and a vehicle for emergency transport of ill campers" (Enquiry Form).
candlebark-farm.md.staff_qualifications_stated: "Swimming Pool requires a Lifeguard with either AUSTSWIM or Bronze Medallion. Canoeing requires an Australian Canoeing Inc Level 1 FlatWater Guide/Instructor. The qualified person must be present at all times." "Candlebark Farm staff do not supervise campers. User group leaders must supervise campers." "There is no first aider resident on site." Resident Manager named as "Michael Hill" (facilities page). Staff and volunteers are stated (Child Protection Policy) to require a Working With Children Check or equivalent, or a Police Check where a WWCC does not apply.
candlebark-farm.md.accessibility_provision: none listed on the pages read (the ACA directory record's "Accessibility Details" field for this venue was blank/NULL)
candlebark-farm.md.animal_species_held: "The farm has kangaroos, wombats, possums, goannas, and a good bird population." (Campsite Booklet, "Wildlife" section). These are free-ranging wildlife on the property, not a held/managed collection; the venue is a residential camp, not an animal park. ## Curriculum
candlebark-farm.md.curriculum_links: none listed by curriculum code or subject name
candlebark-farm.md.teacher_materials: "Candlebark Farm Booklet" (47-page downloadable PDF covering facilities, activities, local hazards, hirer responsibilities, room allocation, dietary requirements form, menu plan, a 3-day sample program, "A GUIDE TO CAMP PROGRAMMING", a check list, camper briefing notes, camper information, an emergency management plan, and a full activities list with descriptions); "Sample Activity Program" (downloadable timetable template); "Map of Candlebark Farm"; activity templates for "Treasure Hunt", "Orienteering" and "Photo find", offered explicitly for schools "you may wish to include in your own campsite booklet"; a "Room Allocation" form; a "Dietary Requirements Form"; "Campers Information" (what to bring); "Leader EMP Information" (leader-facing emergency procedures); "Candlebark Farm Child Protection" policy document; a "COVID Safe Plan". ## Trust
candlebark-farm.md.risk_assessment_available: none listed as a pre-prepared risk assessment document for the hirer to use as-is. The Campsite Booklet instead places this responsibility on the hirer: "Please note: Any safety issues associated with excursions are to be identified by the hirer and any necessary precautions taken." Candlebark Farm supplies its own Emergency Management Plan and posts emergency phone numbers on site, with a condensed leader version in the booklet (pages 17-18), described as "suitable for your Group Leaders. This should be copied and handed to each Camp Leader so they know what to do in an emergency."
candlebark-farm.md.insurance_stated: "Although Candlebark Farm carries its own Public Liability insurance, this will not necessarily protect your organization/leaders from claims made by your participants against your organization/group. Your organization/ group is responsible for ensuring that they have appropriate public liability insurance and so it is highly recommended that your organization/group seek advice from an insurance broker about the event you wish to hold here."
candlebark-farm.md.child_safety_checks_stated: Candlebark Farm's own Child Protection Policy document states that staff, contractors and volunteers are required to hold a Working With Children Check ("WWCC") or other state equivalent, or, where a WWCC does not apply, to provide a Police Check, before commencing duties.
candlebark-farm.md.accreditations_displayed: ACA directory record shows "ATAP Accreditation" = yes, dated 30 June 2020, and "ATAP Camps Activity Accreditation" = yes, also dated 30 June 2020; and a "NARTA Accredited Date" of 30 June 1989. The ACA search-results listing tags the venue "QT accredited". The venue's own homepage links out to trustthetickvic.com.au/pages/camping (a tick-safety external accreditation reference), not opened as part of the four core pages for this record. ## Commercial
candlebark-farm.md.price_and_structure: No price list or per-person rate is published on any page read. The Enquiry Form is explicitly the mechanism for costing: "To check costs and availability of dates for your camp/retreat, please fill in this form." The form distinguishes "standard price" from a "packaged price" for schools: "For school groups we can provide a packaged price and full program assistance which includes transport, entry to Healesville Sanctuary and instructor numbers geared to the number of children attending." Stated per-item optional-extra charges: linen $12.00 per person (minimum lots of 10); Duty Groups taken over by staff, extra $7.00 per person per meal; instructor-led extras (Super Swooper, Archery, Canoeing, Flying Fox, Swimming Pool lifeguard, "Extra Instructor") are costed on request with "a minimum of 40 applies even if you have fewer".
candlebark-farm.md.adults_free_ratio: none listed as a free-adult ratio. The stated ratios are supervision requirements, not free-entry allowances: "one adult leader to ten campers (1:10) for schools" (Campsite Booklet); "at least 1 adult leader per 10-13 children" (Enquiry Form).
candlebark-farm.md.catering: "We offer fully catered camps with a range of different meals and can cater for various dietary requirements, when notice is given." "Self catering is only possible when a food safety qualified person is in charge of the meals and kitchen." Vegetarian or vegan catering "available by arrangement." A downloadable Dietary Requirements Form and sample menu are provided. The Enquiry Form asks whether catering is "Self catered (SC) or Fully catered (FC)" and notes "Bringing your own lunch the first day is more economical."
candlebark-farm.md.cancellation_and_weather: "Activities may be modified or cancelled by camp or group leaders to address; weather, participants abilities, needs, behaviour and comfort requirements." No cancellation/refund policy is stated on the pages read.
candlebark-farm.md.booking_lead_time: none listed as a minimum notice period; "Room Allocation, Menu selection, Dietary Requirements Form" are to be submitted "Two weeks before you arrive" (Downloads page) ## Conversion
candlebark-farm.md.how_to_book: "Detailed Enquiry Form" (the PDF "Candlebark Farm Enquiry Form", filled in and emailed to info@candlebarkfarm.com.au) to "check costs and availability of dates". The form collects organiser and group details, expected and maximum numbers, dates, catering choice, optional extras, budget, and how the enquirer heard about Candlebark.
candlebark-farm.md.price_visible_without_asking: no — no per-person or per-night rate appears on any page read; price is obtained only by submitting the Enquiry Form
candlebark-farm.md.downloadable_pack: yes, extensively: Enquiry Form, Campsite Booklet, Site Map, Room Allocation form, Sample Menu, Dietary Requirements Form, Sample Activity Program, Treasure Hunt template, Orienteering map, Photo Find template, Campers Information, Leader EMP Information, Child Protection policy document, COVID Safe Plan

candlebark-farm.md.title_and_opening_line: ACA directory listing text: "Candlebark farm is an accredited campsite nestled on 100 acres of the treed foothills overlooking the beautiful Yarra Valley near Healesville. Just 65 km east of Melbourne, it is an easy hours drive from the city's centre. We provide a range of facilities and outdoor experiences which help to develop confidence and a caring, supportive attitude among campers that can contribute to important lifeskills." chesterfield-farm.md.activities_verbatim: From the School Excursion Info flyer, "Your students' day at Chesterfield Farm will include ~": - Animal feeding (emus, goats, deer, kangaroos and much more) - Visiting and handling many of the farm's newest additions in our large animal nursery. - A ride in our fun tractor-drawn wagon. - A visit to our pig stys. - A visit to our educational discovery barn where children will talk with one of our farmers about Australian farming eras and farm produce (* suitable for primary aged children only). - And of course our fun farm shows which include sheepdog work and hand milking a cow with a show. From the VM Animal Studies Guideline, "ACTIVITY GUIDELINE" (this timed schedule is stated on the guideline for the VM Animal Studies booking option, not stated as applying to the general School Excursion): - 10:00AM Morning Tea - 10:30AM Activity 1: Rabbit/Guinea Pig handling/weighing for worming - 11:15AM Hand milking - 11:30AM Milking Show - 11:45AM LUNCH - 12:15PM Tractor - 12:30PM Activity 2*: Chicken run handling and health check/feed trail - 1:00PM Dog Show - 1:15PM Activity 3: Mock sheep drenching and treatment record keeping (with Scout) - *Can swap out Activity 1 for dog grooming/handling. - *Can swap out Activity 2 for nursery or feed trail time. Activity detail, verbatim, from the same guideline: - ACTIVITY 1: Safely handle and pick up rabbits/GP's using a towel and keeping four paws in contact with floor or handler's chest/lap; Move animal to weighing scale and weigh in bucket (make sure to zero the scale first!); Record weight and choose correct dosage rate for small animal wormer; Record treatment in appropriate paperwork; Safely move animal back to their original pen - ACTIVITY 2: Safe handling of chickens and overall health check? - ACTIVITY 3: Move sheep into raceway next to shearing yards, then tie Scout up on show barn stage; Discuss drenching – why it is done and how often, how the drench gun works, how to drench safely; Practise mock drenching (no liquid in barrel); Record treatment details and note down estimated weight of sheep (80kg) and dose rate; Scout's station – practise record taking for wormer tablets/flea treatment and health check of dogs
chesterfield-farm.md.duration: "Our school excursion programs on weekdays from 10am to 2pm" (School Excursion Info flyer). The VM Animal Studies Guideline schedule runs from 10:00AM to 1:15PM as the last listed timed item; no explicit finishing time is stated beyond that.

collingwood-childrens-farm.md.activities_verbatim: (School Tours page, "Itinerary") Students often get to meet and pat our guinea pigs, goats and/or sheep and typically get to see pigs, cows, horses, chickens, ducks, goats, cats and peacocks. We usually visit one of our food growing spaces such as the market garden. (School Tours page, "Learning Intentions") To explore the Farm using the senses. To learn and use correct terminology for living things, their features and their offspring. To explore where our animals live and what we do to keep them healthy and happy. To identify the food and fibre products which we get from our Farm animals. (Self-Guided Groups page) Self-guided groups are welcome to join in on the daily activities put on by our friendly farmers. (Camping Groups page) Immersive & Educational: Get a firsthand look at sustainable urban farming, animal care, and environmental stewardship. A Peaceful, Nature-Based Retreat: Step away from screens and city noise for a night of fresh air, open space, and simple living. Hands-On Learning: Connect with the rhythms of farm life while gaining practical outdoor skills. A Safe & Well-Equipped Site: Stay in designated camping areas with access to the historic Barn, toilets, and a secure overnight setup.
collingwood-childrens-farm.md.duration: School Tours: "A one-and-a-half-hour tour running from 10:30 am to 12:00 pm." Groups must arrive by 10:00 am.
