currumbin-wildlife-sanctuary.md.activities_verbatim: Primary School page: "Primary students get hands-on with nature while exploring the Sanctuary on a self-guided journey. Greeted by an Education Officer upon arrival, your class can also add on an engaging 45-minute Education Session, aligned to v8.4 of the Australian Curriculum." High School page: "For students in Years 7 to 10, Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary offers unforgettable, curriculum-linked experiences. After being welcomed by an Education Officer, groups can explore at their own pace or add a 45-minute Education Session focused on biology, conservation, and the real-world impact of environmental science." Booking form, on the "Nature Ed Session (CWS Expert Led Experience)": "Led by one of our experienced and qualified wildlife education officers, this interactive experience is linked to the Australian Curriculum and tailored to your students' year level. Your students will have the opportunity to meet and learn about three of our amazing animals; while participating in interactive activities to facilitate learning." On the "Nature Ed First Nations Experience": "This 45-minute hands on experience has been designed specifically to entertain all age groups. The audience will explore our collection of Indigenous Cultural items such as ochre and a variety of artefacts including weapons, instruments and plants that ensured the survival of the world's longest continuing culture. Participants will learn of cultural teachings and the importance that story telling held within First Nations cultures." On "Walking Tours": "Our 45 minute walking tour routes are a fantastic way for your students/participants to see the Sanctuary, whilst learning about wildlife", with routes named "Iconic Aussies (E.g. koalas, kangaroos, crocodile, dingo)", "Conservation Champions (koala, Tasmanian devil, brush-tail rock wallaby)" and "Exotic Species (Lost Valley and Outback Springs)". On "Koala Connections Experience": "Koalas like never before as you wander through a purpose-built, immersive habitat...This isn't a typical photo-op; it's a slow-paced walk where you can observe, not intrude...knowledgeable Wildlife Keepers will share fascinating insights", with inclusions listed as "15-minute experience", "Wildlife keeper present, providing information about Koalas and conservation", "Take unlimited selfies and photos" and "Professional photo, including a print and digital copy". On "Meet Moose": "Add something unforgettable to your visit with a live conservation detection dog demonstration...a complimentary 15-minute presentation by Moose and Mikey, subject to availability". On "Nest Boxes": "Why not set up a nesting box back at your school, it's as easy as 1, 2, 3: 1. Identify which native species are in your local area 2. Select the appropriate box when you book your excursion 3. Collect during your excursion, assemble and set up back at your school." The booking form also states general purpose: "This booking form is for Australian schools and educational organisations...Our objective is to increase awareness about our native animals and their environment."

Activities described in the Branston Junior Academy case-study visit (bja-visit-oct22 page; a specific past visit reported on the site, not a standing menu): management project (wildlife plot exploration and management planning); "Ask a farmer" Q&A session; farming equipment and soil health demonstration, including a drone flight; soils investigation (soil type identification and crop root comparison); British produce discussion; Nocton Wood walk.
dyson-farming.md.duration: The visit-information-form page offers two options: "Half Day Visit" and "Full Day Visit." No other durations or activity-level timings stated.
dyson-farming.md.group_size_min_max: The visit-information-form page states a maximum of 30 visitors per visit ("maximum of 30"). No minimum stated.
dyson-farming.md.participant_thresholds: Maximum 30 visitors per visit (from the visit-information-form page). No other numeric thresholds found. ## Inventory
dyson-farming.md.facilities: "The Hive" (stated meeting/gathering location for the Branston Junior Academy visit); Education Centre at Nocton (referenced in the CPD training page as available for exploration); Nocton Wood, described as "private protected woodland on estate"; farm plots used for wildlife and wildflower management; 26-acre glasshouse in Carrington, Lincolnshire (strawberry production, featured in the "Virtual Tour").
dyson-farming.md.equipment_provided: Combines, foragers and tractors shown to visiting students (equipment demonstrations); drones used for a soil-health assessment demonstration; shovels for digging up crop roots during the soils activity.
dyson-farming.md.staff_qualifications_stated: No qualification, certification, or training level named for any role. Staff are named by role rather than credential in the Branston Junior Academy case study: Ian Willoughby (plot allocation); Paul Carrott (Farm Manager); Tom Wilks (Livestock Manager); Ed Ford (Technical Agronomist); Dr Tom Storr (Research Agronomist); Jo Knight (Estates and Environment Manager).
dyson-farming.md.accessibility_provision: none listed on the pages read.
dyson-farming.md.animal_species_held: none listed by species name. The Branston Junior Academy case study mentions "wildlife," "wildflowers," and "animal droppings/pellets" generically in the wildlife-management activity, with no species named; "sugar and strawberries" are mentioned as British produce examples rather than livestock. ## Curriculum
dyson-farming.md.curriculum_links: The education page states curriculum resources bring "real-life examples to the curriculum" and cover "British farming, food production, renewable energy, and environment." The CPD training page states the programme uses "newly developed Dyson Farming resources and their links to the curriculum," focused on "food, farming and natural environment." No specific subject or Key Stage breakdown (of the kind published by other venues in this cell) was found on the pages read; the visit-information-form page instead lists the age-group options a school selects when booking: Pre School; Key Stage 1 (age 5–7); Key Stage 2 (7–11); Key Stage 3 (11–14); Key Stage 4 (14–16); Sixth Form/College (ages 16–18); University; "A mix of ages"; "Other."
dyson-farming.md.teacher_materials: "School Resources" is named on the education page as "worksheets and activities to help children understand the importance of British farming," but no downloadable file was found linked on the pages read. The CPD training session itself functions as a form of teacher preparation, stated to make participants "applicable for a visit to the farm within 6 months of CPD qualification." ## Trust
dyson-farming.md.risk_assessment_available: No risk assessment is published by the venue for schools to download. Instead, the visit-information-form page requires the school to supply its own "Risk Assessment Details" as part of the booking form.
dyson-farming.md.child_safety_checks_stated: none listed — no DBS or equivalent vetting statement found on the pages read.
dyson-farming.md.accreditations_displayed: none listed on the venue's own pages read. (A third-party Countryside Classroom directory listing for Dyson Farming states the farm has "CEVAS accredited personnel," but this was not found stated on the venue's own website, so it is not recorded here as venue-published. The same CEVAS claim pattern was also seen on a third-party listing for New Hall Farm, Ardsley, suggesting it may be a scheme associated with Countryside Classroom-listed venues generally rather than page text unique to Dyson Farming.) ## Commercial
dyson-farming.md.price_and_structure: none listed as a price. Third-party search-result summaries (not the venue's own pages) describe visits as "usually free of charge" and mention "a small fee for car parking" to help fund the education area; these figures were not found stated in venue-page text read directly, so are not recorded as a confirmed venue-published price.
dyson-farming.md.booking_lead_time: none listed as a stated minimum number of days or weeks. The visit-information-form asks for "Planned date of visit" and "Has your organisation/school visited before?" but states no minimum lead time. ## Conversion
dyson-farming.md.how_to_book: A dedicated online booking form, the "Dyson Farming Visit Information Form," at dysonfarming.com/dyson-farming-visit-information-form/, opening: "Thank you for your interest in visiting the Dyson Farming. Please complete the form below to help us plan a meaningful and enjoyable experience for your students." Fields: visit type (Half Day/Full Day); age group; maximum group size (30); Organisation/School Information; Organisation/School Address; Lead Contact Name; Lead Contact Role/Position; Email Address; Phone Number; Planned date of visit; prior-visit history; free-text "Visit Objectives"; "Risk Assessment Details" (supplied by the school). CPD sessions are booked separately by email to communications@dysonfarming.com. The LEAF Education Pop-Up Knowledge Hub is booked externally via a link to leaf.eco/events/pop-up-knowledge-hub.
dyson-farming.md.downloadable_pack: No downloadable pack, teacher materials, or risk assessment found linked on the venue's own pages read; "School Resources" is named but no working download link was found.
dyson-farming.md.testimonials_from_schools: none listed as a standing testimonial; the Branston Junior Academy page is a case-study/news post about one past visit rather than a testimonial quote from the school, and includes the venue's own framing: "we gave the children a chance to see behind the scenes of a farm they'll pass regularly."
dyson-farming.md.title_and_opening_line: Page title: "Education – Dyson Farming". Opening line: "Inspiring the future of farming."

earth-products.md.price_and_structure: none listed. The Farm Visits page states visit funding comes via "DEFRA's ED1 scheme" so "schools only have to pay to transport the children to us," but no fee amount or structure is given.
earth-products.md.catering: none listed beyond the log-seating/fire-pit lunch area described under facilities; no food provision is stated
earth-products.md.how_to_book: The Farm Visits page states "Contact Tanya and Will for more details." The Contact page gives a phone number, "01752 776730," and an enquiry form with a topic dropdown including "Visits," plus email info@porshamfarm.co.uk.
earth-products.md.testimonials_from_schools: The Farm Visits page carries a "School and College Testimonials" section with multiple dated, attributed quotes, including: "Fabulous informative experience with a clear and friendly guide, great for the children to follow through the food chain." — Woodford Primary School, May 2026. "Brilliant - the children learnt so much!" — High Street Academy, Sep 2025. "An amazing day out - our Yr 6 had a ball. earth-products.md.title_and_opening_line: Homepage `<title>` reads "Porsham Farm in Devon". The homepage/footer strapline reads: "An almost organic, high welfare Red Tractor Devon farm. Pasture fed retired Dairy Beef. Forest school. Camping. Rewilding. Tree planting. Wildlife." The Farm Visits page opens: "Since 2010 we have opened the farm to visitors – from schools, clubs and the public for different events and we are always delighted to be approached by groups who would like to visit." ## Additional note A "Forest School" page exists but states this is delivered by a third party, not directly by the farm: "Forest school can be booked With Suzanne through Wild About Woods Ltd for Birthday parties, Team Building, Forest Fun, Woodland Stories, Halloween Spooky Stories," with a link to wildaboutwoods.co.uk and a phone number for "Caroline." No pricing/booking page distinct from the Farm Visits and Contact pages was found; no dedicated general "what is here" attractions page exists beyond the "Porsham Farm" (Our Farm) page, which was read.

eco-nature.md.facilities: "Centre d'exploration (musée et café de l'Archipel)" at 345 boulevard Sainte-Rose, Laval. Permanent exhibition "Incroyable, mais vrai!" inside the museum. A laboratoire d'écologie ("le laboratoire d'écologie et rencontrez les spécimens de notre collection vivante") visited as part of "Visite animée au musée". Centre de réhabilitation des tortues du Québec (Quebec Turtle Rehabilitation Centre), referenced as part of the organisation's mission.

exploramer.md.programme_names: Solaster (Submarine Simulator) Baleines à l'école (Whales at School) Bassin tactile mobile (Mobile Touch Basin) Explo-Mer Hydro-Québec (competition) Petits curieux (Young Explorers) Museum Visit Requins : non coupables ! (Sharks: Not Guilty!) Scalpel ! Littoral sous la lentille (Shoreline Under the Lens)
exploramer.md.activities_verbatim: Solaster: virtual deep-sea exploration of St. Lawrence biodiversity Baleines à l'école: giant whale specimen with scientific mystery-solving component Bassin tactile mobile: live marine species handling (sea urchins, starfish, crabs) Explo-Mer Hydro-Québec: species biology research competition, "Offert gracieusement par Hydro-Québec" Petits curieux: multi-activity day at museum facilities Requins : non coupables !: film excerpts and scientific debate format Scalpel !: live animal dissection demonstrations, priced by specimen Littoral sous la lentille: field-based biodiversity inventory with optional social-media documentation component
exploramer.md.duration: Solaster: 45 min / animation Baleines à l'école: 45 à 60 min / animation Bassin tactile mobile: 60 à 75 min Explo-Mer Hydro-Québec: plusieurs séances (several sessions) Petits curieux: une journée (a full day) Requins : non coupables !: 90 à 120 min Scalpel !: 60 à 75 min Littoral sous la lentille: une demi-journée (half day)
exploramer.md.group_size_min_max: Solaster: 30 élèves max / animation Baleines à l'école: 30 élèves max / animation Bassin tactile mobile: 30 élèves max Explo-Mer Hydro-Québec: 30 élèves Petits curieux: 120 élèves max Requins : non coupables !: 200 élèves max Scalpel !: 30 élèves max Littoral sous la lentille: 30 élèves max
exploramer.md.participant_thresholds: Solaster capped at 30 students per animation; Baleines à l'école capped at 30 students per animation; Bassin tactile mobile capped at 30 students; Explo-Mer Hydro-Québec capped at 30 students; Petits curieux capped at 120 students; Requins : non coupables ! capped at 200 students; Scalpel ! capped at 30 students; Littoral sous la lentille capped at 30 students. ## Inventory
exploramer.md.facilities: Museum; aquarium with "a vingtaine de bassins contenant plus de 1 000 individus de 60 espèces différentes" (around twenty tanks holding over 1,000 individuals from 60 different species); five touch pools recreating tide-pool environments; sea-excursion vessel(s); shoreline/beach activity area.
exploramer.md.staff_qualifications_stated: Guided tours led by "scientific animators" ("animateurs scientifiques"); no formal qualification stated beyond that title.
exploramer.md.animal_species_held: Touch pools: common crabs, common starfish, polar starfish, whelks, purple snails, moon snails, sea cucumbers, green sea urchins, American lobsters, hermit crabs. Aquarium: "60 espèces différentes" of St. Lawrence estuary and gulf marine life, individual species not further enumerated on the pages read. Scalpel! dissection specimens: Calmar gros (large squid), Calmar petit (small squid), Myxine (hagfish), Poisson osseux (bony fish, e.g. Morue/cod, Truite/trout), Lamproie juvénile (juvenile lamprey), Étoile de mer commune (common starfish). ## Curriculum
exploramer.md.curriculum_links: "Toutes les activités proposées par Exploramer, La mer à découvrir ont été conçues en prenant en considération les objectifs pédagogiques du Programme de formation de l'école québécoise" (all activities are designed taking into account the pedagogical objectives of the Quebec school curriculum). Activities are organised by primary and secondary level, with Explo-Mer Hydro-Québec specified for "grades 1-2 secondary".
exploramer.md.price_and_structure: School programme costs: Solaster $456.75/day; Baleines à l'école $456.75/day; Bassin tactile mobile $185; Explo-Mer Hydro-Québec free ("Offert gracieusement par Hydro-Québec"); Petits curieux "selon les activités choisies" (varies by activities chosen); Requins : non coupables ! $270; Scalpel ! priced by specimen — Calmar gros $280, Calmar petit $225, Myxine $255, Poisson osseux $215, Lamproie juvénile $210, Étoile de mer commune $210; Littoral sous la lentille $230. Additional costs: transportation "0,63 $ du kilomètre" and "$145 par nuitée dans un hébergement, lorsque nécessaire" (per night of accommodation, when needed). Taxes (TPS/TVQ) not included in any listed price. General admission group rate (15+ persons): Museum & Aquarium — youth (6-17) $10.70, student $13.40, adult $16.10, child (5 and under) free; Sea Excursion — youth $30.35, student $42.85, adult $51.80.
exploramer.md.cancellation_and_weather: A separate cancellation policy page exists (https://exploramer.qc.ca/politique-annulation-remboursement/) but was not itself among the four required page categories and was not read in detail; the tarifs page refers visitors to it without stating terms.
exploramer.md.how_to_book: Contacts: Charlotte Baron (interpretation@exploramer.qc.ca / 418-763-2500 poste 225) and Gabriel Leduc (adj.interpretation@exploramer.qc.ca / 418-763-2500 poste 225); Google Forms provided for registration to specific programmes.
exploramer.md.price_visible_without_asking: Yes, for all named school-programme activities and for general/group admission — prices are published on the programme and tarifs pages.
exploramer.md.title_and_opening_line: Nav label for schools: "Programme éducatif" under the "Youth Section" (Jeunesse) menu; site strapline seen in curriculum text: "Exploramer, La mer à découvrir".

five-sisters-zoo.md.programme_names: - Class Visits - Global explorers - So you want to be a Snow Leopard... - Bears picnic - Bugs Count Using OPAL Guides - Classify This - Rainforests - Guided Tour - Habitats and Adaptations - Everything's Connected (Pond Dipping) - Endangered Wildlife - Conservation at the Zoo - Ecosystems, Species and Genes - Zoo Careers - Outreach
five-sisters-zoo.md.activities_verbatim: - Early years, Global explorers: "Come with us on a journey around the world! One of our expert education officers needs some help from your team of young explorers as they travel to a variety of world habitats. Should we wear sunglasses in the Kalahari Desert? Will a snorkel be required in the wetlands of the Pantanal? It is all down to your team to decide as we attempt to observe some of the most incredible and unique species at FSZ." - Early years, So you want to be a Snow Leopard...: "Snow leopards are the ultimate hunters in their Himalayan habitats. How well would your class survive high in the mountains? This session compares how humans and snow leopards use their senses and aims to put participants in their paws for the day by exploring the threats against this truly majestic species." - Early years, Bears picnic: "This is no teddy bear's picnic... We have two very hungry brown bears here at FSZ and we need to get their food prepped fast. Our education team need some help from your class! What food should go in the perfect bear feed bucket? It is all down to your class to decide before they have a snack themselves and take a snooze in their own brown bear day bed." - Early years, Bugs Count Using OPAL Guides: "Man made vs. natural... This session provides an opportunity for your young learners to start exploring what makes the perfect habitat for many of our native species. In this session they will investigate manmade surfaces and more natural plant beds to find out which is the better home for insects, spiders, millipedes, woodlice, and many other small animals." - P1-P3, Classify This: "What is an animal with a spine called? What groups of animals are covered in scales? and what on earth is a mammal? Join one of our education officers as they walk your class through the world of animal classification before putting their knowledge to the test out in the zoo..." - P1-P3, Rainforests: "Where in the world are the tropical rainforests? What do they look like? What lives in them? Get your class enthusiastic about one of the most incredible and biodiverse habitats on earth! This education officer led session involves lots of class participation as pupils discover why these forests are so important and how we can all do our bit to protect them." - P1-P3, Guided Tour: "Can't see a session that fits with what you class have been studying? Don't let this put you off organising a visit to FSZ. We can organise a tour of the park, taking in some Five Sisters highlights. Feel free to let us know the topics you have covered with your class and, where possible, we will be sure to include some relevant themes in a tour." - P4-P7, Habitats and Adaptations: "From oceans to mountain tops. Hot deserts to Wetlands. This education officer led session gives learners the opportunity to explore a diverse range of habitats and discuss how animals have evolved physical adaptations that allow them to survive in some of the most extreme places on earth." - P4-P7, Everything's Connected (Pond Dipping): "Everything in the Five Sisters Zoo wildlife pond is connected! In this education officer led session learners will have the opportunity to identify some of it's amazing inhabitants and piece together a real life aquatic food web." - P4-P7, Endangered Wildlife: "What does endangered mean? This session allows learners to engage with the IUCN red list and discuss what we can all do to help species that are listed as endangered." - Secondary, Conservation at the Zoo: "Wildlife conservation is at the heart of what we do at Five Sisters Zoo. this education officer led session allows learners to find out more about some of the incredible projects we support at FSZ and displays the importance of modern zoos for the conservation of species and their habitats." - Secondary, Ecosystems, Species and Genes: "BIODIVERSITY! Using real examples at Five Sisters Zoo, this session allows students to discover how a modern zoo contributes towards the conservation of biodiversity around the world. Using FSZ case studies students are challenged to discuss how a zoo can be successful conserving genetic diversity, species diversity and ecosystem diversity." - Secondary, Zoo Careers: "Ever wanted to work at a zoo? There may be more to consider the you first thought... This session allows students to explore the opportunities available in a modern zoo and, using FSZ case studies, encourages them to think about how to get into some of the many different roles available in this unique working environment."

green-thumb-farm.md.activities_verbatim: Excursions open with "a guided farm walk, in which they follow educational signs and discover key features of regenerative farming, composting, bees and how we manage the farm", then two rotations chosen from five: "Worm Farming & Compost: Students learn about what goes into making a good compost, as well as seeing samples. We discuss the role of compost in organic farming and why it is so important to be composting food scraps at home. We then look at the different worm farms we have on the farm, and the children do a hands-on activity with the worm farms and compost bays"; "Seeds & Bees: Students discover seeds growing on the farm and learn about the role of pollinators in natural ecosystems. Children can spot our insects and pollinators, we talk about making homes for them, and they can see our bee hotels, native bees and honey bee hives on the farm. They have hands-on experience with a sample of seeds collected from the farm which they can take home to grow"; "Herbs and Growing a Kitchen Garden: The students are encouraged to explore our kitchen garden, and are invited to see, touch, smell and taste a wide selection of culinary and medicinal herbs, including edible flowers. The students have the opportunity to prepare a herb blend of their choice to take home and use"; "Food and Fibre: We will discuss the food we grow on the farm that has a dual purpose as a fibre that can make things such as rope, baskets and clothing. They will see it grown, handle the raw material and see samples of products we can make. They get to experience weaving first hand and make a woven product"; "Making Healthy Soil + How to Make a No-Dig Garden Bed: The students look at our hugelkultur bed, raised beds, and in ground beds and we talk about natural ways that we build healthy soil through composting, worm farms, fertigation system, soil amendments and minimal till methods of farming. They are able to make a mini no-dig garden of their own to take home". Incursions offer a choice of three: "Exploring Herbs: Students explore herbs and their varying uses, discovering the wide range of culinary and medicinal benefits. We look at native and non-native herbs and how you can grow herbs at home. Students receive propagated herbs to grow in the classroom along with samples of herbs that they can dry and use"; "Farm-to-Fork Journey: Students map out the journey that food takes as it travels from farm to fork in varying situations. We consider environmental and sustainable considerations, the differences between organic and non-organic foods and the health benefits of eating fresh food. Students get to plant a pot of microgreens to grow at school or home"; "Living Soils: Students dive into soil exploration, record their findings and make predictions. We discover what makes great soil and how we can turn all soils into great soil for growing. Students make a liquid fertiliser from plants that they can watch over the coming weeks as it develops. This can then be used at school or at home"

Opening line: "Welcome to our Primary School Programs, where we bridge the gap between the classroom and the natural world." ## Note Animal feed making: no page read for this venue publishes anything resembling a recipe-based animal feed mixing or making activity. Green Thumb Farm is a horticulture and composting-led education venue; it holds no named livestock or poultry species on any of the four pages read, and the only creature-related hands-on content is a worm-farming and compost activity ("the children do a hands-on activity with the worm farms and compost bays") and a bee/pollinator-habitat activity, neither of which involves feeding an animal. The closest analogue to a "making" activity is soil and compost making, explicitly framed around plant and soil health rather than animal feed: "Students learn about what goes into making a good compost" and "we talk about natural ways that we build healthy soil through composting, worm farms, fertigation system, soil amendments and minimal till methods of farming", culminating in a take-home product ("They are able to make a mini no-dig garden of their own to take home") that is a soil/garden product, not a feed product. No wording using "feed", "feeding", or "mix" in connection with an animal appears on any of the four pages read.

harvest-farms.md.programme_names: Educational Farm Tours; Organic Farm Adventures, Bilpin
harvest-farms.md.activities_verbatim: From "What Students Can Expect" (Educational Farm Tours page): - Explore our seasonal veggie gardens and learn what plants need to thrive - Pick and taste fresh produce straight from the farm - Meet the worms in our giant worm farms and learn how they help build healthy soil - Discover the role of beneficial insects in regenerative farming - Learn about sustainable food systems and the paddock-to-plate journey - Understand how we use food waste to create compost and improve soil health - Breathe in fresh Bilpin air, connect with nature, and have some fun outdoors! From "During their visit to the Bilpin Harvest Farm, students will" (curriculum PDF): - Explore the huge worm farms, hold a worm, and understand why they are so important - Walk through the vegetable gardens and learn the characteristics and needs of different vegetables and fruit - Harvest some of the vegetables to taste the delicious difference between store bought and fresh from the farm! (Seasons will determine what is available) - Learn about insects and why some are so beneficial, and others are not so for the farm - Dig in the soil and learn why it's so suitable for growing delicious, household veggies - Discover why it is important for people to have the opportunity to be more directly involved in the farms where their food is grown - Explore the unique characteristics of Bilpin and why it is such a productive farming area - Identify and describe what plants need to grow in a sustainable, restorative farm environment - Understand how waste can be reduced and how food waste is used to improve soil health - Discover where the food goes once it is harvested and how the vegetables are used - Leave all their worries behind. Breath in the fresh mountain air, get muddy, laugh, play, and totally immerse themselves in the farm experience

highfields-pioneer-village.md.programme_names: "The Core Program"; "Our extra optional half hour segments (choose maximum of three)"
highfields-pioneer-village.md.activities_verbatim: Core Program: "Damper making - Dough making, open fire cookery in camp ovens (demonstration)"; "Puppet show - Animated wooden toys tell the story of land settlement on (in the Gallery) the Darling Downs, from 1840 to 1900 (suit all ages)"; "Slab cottage Housing - Grinke slab hut and Raatz stone cookhouse (1889) (guided tour), including homemade furniture, hides as carpets, handmade fly screen, open fire, fountain, vegetable garden, washing machines"; "Damper eating - Billy tea, damper, golden syrup at tables in the damper shed (Morning tea)". Optional half-hour segments: "The Big Cow- Walk inside and see how this incredible sculpture was made, learn about it's history and the Dairy Industry. Includes a Butter Making Demonstration on request."; "Heritage chapel - History and current use of the Meringandan Congregational Church (1909), conducted inside the chapel"; "Blacksmithing Working with iron - forge and anvil (demonstration) and horseshoe making"; "Water wisdom water - guttering and tanks, divining for underground water, (participatory) boring and windmills, wood-fired pumps, log stock troughs. Manually operated geared water pump demo (suit Years 4, 5, 6)"; "Harvesting machines - A guided visit to the machinery shed. Stripper, winnower, thresher, reaper & binder, Harvesters 1838 to early 1900's"; "Southern Cross - A guided walk through the Southern Cross Museum. Products made by Toowoomba Foundry 1876-1980's"; "Toowoomba Fire Brigade Historical Museum- A guided tour of the History of our local Fire Brigade and their trucks, technology and how it has changed. Fire Safety Talks can be included via prior arrangement"; "12. Free time - There are many buildings with stationary exhibits to explore the authentic slice of Australian heritage. Pupils to be in small groups with an adult"; "Aboriginal Culture Talk - Didgeridoo performance, dance workshop and boomerang throwing workshop. This involves an extra charge, please contact us for a quote."; "Sheep Shearing- the process by which the woollen fleece of a sheep is cut off. The person who removes the sheep's wool is called a shearer. This involves an extra charge, please contact us for a quote."; "Transport Museum and the James MacDonald Bike Collection - A guided walk through the Transport Museum: featuring penny farthings, horse drawn transport and vintage cars"; "Queensland Energy Exhibition Centre - A guided walk through the Energy Museum featuring the history of Energy usage in Queensland and the very first electrical appliances ever made"; "Horse works - Corn growing, husking, and cracking for farm use and as a cash crop. The use of draught horses as a source of power to work stationary machinery, horse whim demonstration. This involves an extra charge, please contact us for a quote."; "Ride Henry the Model T Ford Bus- was manufactured in 1924 and originally used as a school bus for the Kilcoy State School from 1924 to 1940. \$5 Adults and \$3 Child. (minimum booking of 12 persons)."; "School's In- The Upper Forest Spring's School was opened in 1898 and closed in 1961, sit in school and experience what it was like to be a student in the olden days."; "Coach House- Includes a Princess Coach, German Wagon, Sulkies, Buggies and an Ambulance Wagon. Let your volunteer guide take you on a walk through the history of Horse Drawn Transport in Australia." A closing note reads: "Please Note: If one of the demonstrators is away sick another segment will be substituted"

iris-lodge-alpacas.md.programme_names: School Alpaca Excursions on the NSW Central Coast; Educational Farm Visits
iris-lodge-alpacas.md.activities_verbatim: Preschool & Early (Ages 3-5): - Animal feeding & petting – Learning about textures, sounds, and movements. - Basic understanding of farm animals – Recognizing different species and their needs. - Exploring the farm environment – Engaging students through sight, sound, and touch. Primary School (Ages 6-12): - Food sources & lifecycles – Where food comes from and how animals contribute. - Animal habitats & adaptations – Learning about biodiversity and conservation. - Sustainability & farm management – Introduction to eco-friendly farming practices. High School (Ages 13-18): - Sustainability & Environmental Management – Real-world applications of eco-friendly farming techniques. - Agricultural Business & Economics – Understanding how farms operate as businesses. - Ethical Farming & Animal Welfare – Exploring responsible livestock care and industry practices. What's Included (general, not timed): - Animal Encounters & Feeding – Up-close experiences with friendly alpacas, llamas, sheep, and cows. - Sustainability & Environmental Education – Learning about sustainable farming, eco-friendly practices, and biodiversity. - Curriculum-Based Learning Modules – Tailored programs for different age groups and subject areas. - Teacher Resources & Lesson Extensions – Pre- and post-visit activities to reinforce learning. - Guided Farm Tour – Understanding the daily operations of a working farm. - Farm Life & Agriculture Insights – Exploring how farms contribute to local and global food systems.

island-bay-marine-education-centre.md.activities_verbatim: - "Stage 1: 'Fish Fingers' A full, hands-on, interactive plunge into discovering the variety of marine life which lives on a rocky shore. Level 1-2; 1.5 Hours*." - "Stage 2: 'Rock & Roll' An exploration of how marine plants and animals have adapted to living on the rocky shore. Level 3-4; 1.5 Hours *+." - "Stage 3: 'On the Rocks' A hands-on investigation of the inter-relationships of rocky shore plants and animals with each other and with their non-living environment. Level 5-6; 2 Hours * +, plus group field study time." - "Stage 4: 'Life on the Edge' A detailed, field-orientated study of zonation, the concept of dynamic equilibrium, and factors which influence continual change. Level 7-8; 2+ Hours* + plus group field study time." - "Programme 2. Introduction to Marine Ecology — A hands-on opportunity to discover the inter-connection of all life on earth, and how our continued survival and that of all creatures in the sea, from worms to whales and in rock pools to the deepest ocean, depends on healthy oceans. Level: 4-8; 2 Hours * + plus field study time." - "Programme 3. Life in Sand and Mud — A hands-on laboratory and field study of marine life that lives on Island Bay Beach. Level: 4-8; 2 Hours * + plus field study time." - "Programme 4. 'Exploring and Protecting Our Taputeranga Marine Reserve' — An introduction to the Marine Reserve concept and a hands-on, field exploration of some of the marine life within the TMR. Level: 4-8; 2 Hours *+ optional 'immersion' time." - "Option 1- 'Protecting Our Marine Reserve' — As part of our proposed TMR related 'Marine Reserve Immersion' programmes, we are offering schools with Level 4-8 students an opportunity to participate in a long-term monitoring programme to determine the potential impact of school groups and other visitors on rocky shore marine life immediately surrounding the IBMEC's Bait House facility." - "Option 2- 'Snorkelling Adventure Programme' — The second 'immersion' option we can offer local schools is participation in our 'Snorkelling Adventure Programme.' We offer this programme to local or regional schools as an additional option for students 12 years old and up to 24 students per session." - "Programme 5. Te Mara Moana 'The Living Sea' — A special, hands-on programme designed for kohanga reo, kura kaupapa, and Pasifika students wishing to know about Maori scientific knowledge and prospective on the sea and its uses. Level: 1-5. 2 Hours*." - "1. Exploring the Taputeranga Marine Reserve and Taputeranga Island — This Programme focusses on learning about Taputeranga Island and Marine Reserve. The programme will present a Maori and European perspective of the natural world, and its past and present cultural and spiritual importance to both cultures... The Programme will include lunch and a boat trip along the South Coast from Lyall Bay to Red Rocks." - "2. Seals and Red Rocks Reserve Exploration — This programme will provide a unique opportunity to explore, discover and learn about this diverse coastal location. Participants will begin their exploration at IBMEC's Octopus Headquarters for a brief overview of the day's activities followed by a walk to the award-winning, Owhiro Bay Interpretation Centre... The programme includes lunch and a copy of the Guide to Wellington's Red Rocks." - "3. Cook Strait Ocean Exploration — This hands-on, ship-based programme will take participants along the Wellington South Coast and into Wellington Harbour... The programme will be carried out on the Seafarer II a 50 foot, (15 m) Marko Sambrailo commercial charter and fishing vessel... The programme includes lunch and refreshments and an opportunity to catch local marine fish species for home or release with all appropriate equipment provided." - "4. Under the Surface- Master Class Snorkelling Adventure — This exciting programme offers a range of snorkelling explorations of local marine life within and around the Taputeranga Marine Reserve and Island. All our snorkelling programmes are led by highly qualified instructors and are suited to adults and children from 12 years of age and above... We will provide quality 7mm wetsuits, hoods, fins and mask/snorkel sets for each participant. Participants will also enjoy a hot shower and lunch, and a visit to our Bait House Aquarium."

Nine native lizard species: copper skink, shore skink, ornate skink, moko skink, suter's skink, common gecko, pacific gecko, forest gecko, green gecko. Also stick insects (re-introduced); Auckland tree weta; giant centipedes; banded rail; fernbird; pīhoihoi (pipit); fantail; grey warbler; silvereye; Australasian harrier; kukupa; morepork; shining cuckoo; tui; Australasian bittern. Shorebirds: Reef Heron/Matuku Moana, Caspian Tern/Taranui, Little Black Shag/Kawau Tūī, Royal Spoonbill/Kōuku Ngutupapa, Bar-tailed Godwit/Kuaka, Pied Shag/Kāruhiruhi, Variable Oystercatcher/Tōrea Pango, South Island Pied Oystercatcher/Tōrea. Also white-faced heron; kingfisher; black-backed gull; red-billed gull; oi (grey-faced petrel, reintroduced 2004); fur seals (regular winter visitors); a leopard seal (one-off visitor in 2017, resided on the floating pontoon for several weeks). matuku-link-wetland-education-programme..activities_verbatim: Guided Walks: Explore the wonders of wetland ecology with expert guides, delving into the flora, fauna, and cultural significance of our local wetlands. Water testing: Discover the macroinvertebrates that call our waterways home and learn about what they tell us about our water. For older students, engage in comprehensive water testing, including assessments of pH and dissolved oxygen levels, as well as measurements of water clarity. Bird identification: Learn about the diverse bird species that call our wetlands home, and how to identify them by call and how to read bird bands to identify individual birds. Customised Learning: We understand that every class is unique, which is why we'll work with you to tailor our programme to suit your curriculum objectives and student needs. From the sample timetable image: Arrive at Matuku Link; Brief introduction in the barn; Brain food and toilet break; Hīkoi / walk (Group 1 and Group 2 run concurrently); Morning tea; Water testing; Lunch; Bird calls / Bird bands (Group 1 and Group 2 run concurrently, then swap); Recap and Haere Rā; Leave Matuku Link.

middle-england-farm.md.activities_verbatim: - Animal care - including husbandry, feeding, cleaning - Animal handling - including alpaca and goat walking - Gardening - growing fruit, vegetables, herbs, spices and flowers - Talking Therapy - chatting in a relaxed way with staff to address every day problem solving in a none pressurised environment - Arts and Crafts - farm related activities such as decorating animal housing, making bird feeders and houses - Poultry breeding - from collecting the eggs to raising the chicks and integrating them into the flock - Lambs - learning how to take care of a young animal and training them to make good 'pets' - Forest school - hedge building, campfire building and cooking - Socialisation and personal growth - in safe space sessions, whilst being fun and enjoyable. Includes educational content, helping to fulfil many elements on the National Curriculum. Maths and science particularly - ASDAN qualifications - for students aged 13 plus who wish gain extra qualifications outside of school - Cooking - making everything from jam to soup, with products we've grown here on the farm. mount-pleasant-school-farm.md.programme_names: none listed (the site does not name a branded programme; the offer is described as "a day visit" / "the farm's activities")
mount-pleasant-school-farm.md.activities_verbatim: - The most useful preparation at school is to consider how we should behave on a farm and in the countryside i.e. the essence of the Country Code. - How about getting the children to come up with their own ideas for a code of behaviour? - After putting on appropriate clothing and footwear our first session will be in the classroom. We will consider how we should behave for the day on a farm and in the countryside with respect for Mr Charles, his family and the animals. - One of our outdoor activities will be to feed the hens and collect the eggs. We normally choose children to help with carrying the feed buckets and egg baskets out to the hen houses. - All the children will have a chance to feed and touch the hens and sheep during the morning and in the afternoon we spend time with the dairy cattle and calves, and any livestock around the farmyard. - In the morning session as well as feeding the chickens there will be an opportunity to see the sheep and their lambs. - We will also observe the pigs in the morning session. - For field to Fork topics we can discuss inside the classroom in between feeding, which animals give us food, food labels, foods grown here or abroad, how they are grown. We are happy to link the day to your farming topic. - Please remember that farms are a potentially dangerous and hazardous working environment. Children must stay with the adults at all times and must not touch any equipment or machinery around the farmyard. - The outline of the day remains flexible according to your specific requirements – we can always adapt if the weather alters, or we feel that the children need a change!
mount-pleasant-school-farm.md.duration: half day; whole day (1 class); whole day split for 2 classes. Plan for a 9.45–10.00am arrival; groups normally expected to leave between 2.00 and 2.30pm.
mount-pleasant-school-farm.md.group_size_min_max: none listed as a numeric minimum or maximum group size. "1 class" and "2 classes" are used as the unit for whole-day pricing.
mount-pleasant-school-farm.md.facilities: The Classroom (indoor teaching space, described on its own page as having "sustainable building features"); hen houses (built summer 2023); pig sty (purpose-built, close to the classroom); winter shelter for sheep behind the pig sty; sheep paddock by the reed beds; large cattle yards (5 large yards); reed bed sewage/filtering system; milk vat/dairy; slurry lagoon with separator; borehole water supply; silage clamps.
mount-pleasant-school-farm.md.equipment_provided: none listed (the "what to bring and wear" page instructs visitors on footwear/clothing to bring, but does not state the venue provides equipment)

Named roles are given without qualifications: Centre Manager Nina Hatch ("responsible for arranging and structuring the educational visits"); Nicky Jennings ("delivers the content of the day visits"); tenant farmers Peter and Emma Charles operate the working dairy farm.
mount-pleasant-school-farm.md.accessibility_provision: An "Additional Farm Risk Assessment for physical difficulties 25-26" document is provided for download, implying provision for visitors with physical difficulties, but the page text itself states no specific accessibility features.
mount-pleasant-school-farm.md.animal_species_held: dairy cattle (Holstein Friesians and Dairy Shorthorns, "just over 350 cattle" across sites, "180 milking cows"); pigs (2 young female pigs, Large White cross); sheep (with lambs); chickens/hens ("24 or so free range birds"). ## Curriculum
mount-pleasant-school-farm.md.curriculum_links: Cross Curricular: Food and Farming (All Key Stages) — where our food comes from, different types of farm, Food Miles & field to fork and sow, grow farm; Aspects of the EYFS framework, in particular ELG 14 The World. Mathematics (All Key Stages): practical applications of number, geometry, collecting data to create tally charts back at school. English, Language & Literacy (All Key Stages): spoken language, keywords & vocabulary relating to the Farm, reading and writing non-fiction, linking to stories e.g. the work of Dick King Smith. Science: Animals including Human (KS1, KS2); identifying carnivores, herbivores and omnivores; grouping animals around their body structures; Teeth & Nutrition (KS2); Seasonal changes (KS1); Everyday materials (KS1); Living things and their habitats (lower KS2). Design and technology: Cooking and Nutrition (KS1,2); Understand where food comes from (KS1); identifying the food groups found on the farm; food labelling. Geography: Place knowledge (formerly Town and Country) (FS, KS1); investigating the local area; Human and physical geography (KS2). Cross curricular Environmental/sustainability Awareness: sustainable features of the classroom building as an Eco-Status case study; recycling contents of lunchboxes; issues around food waste. History: Impact of the Roman Empire on Britain (the farm stands on a Roman Road to Droitwich); farming comparisons with Anglo-Saxon settlements; achievements of the earliest civilizations compared with farming in Ancient Egypt. Art and Design: using a range of materials to create farm animals (KS1); looking at the work of artists and craftsmakers who have interpreted farm animals (KS1); observation and drawing of farm animals (KS2).

national-aquarium-of-new-zealand.md.programme_names: - Native Animals - Classification - Nature's Little Explorers: 3-5 Year Olds - The Plastic Problem - Sharks and Rays - Rocky Shore Lesson - Rocky Shore Visit - Tuna - New Zealand's Native Eels - Dinosaurs and Fossils - Protecting Pania - Adaptations - Primo Penguins - Technology at the Aquarium - Life at the Boundary - Food Webs & Adaptations - Gas Exchange & Dissection - Rocky Shore Transects Study - Animal Responses Daphnia Lab - Tuna - New Zealand's Native Eels (NCEA level 1 AS91920 version) - Te Kawa O Tangaroa - MSC programme - Travel and Tourism - Native Animals at the National Aquarium
national-aquarium-of-new-zealand.md.activities_verbatim: - "Native Animals — In Native Animals, your tamariki will be engaged in an interactive educational session, learning about some of New Zealand's incredible animal taonga. We focus on kiwi, penguins and tuatara and the environments they live in. This session includes hands on activities, puppets and a story." - "Classification — Tamariki learn that animals are grouped in different ways, and how to identify which group an animal belongs to. This session includes hands on activities, puppets and a story." - "Nature's Little Explorers: 3-5 Year Olds — Education sessions designed just for 3-5 year olds. We're inviting friends and caregivers to bring along their little-ones to enjoy ocean themed activities, nature play, stories and crafts. Your little explorers will be immersed in nature and the world around them with changing themes such as learning about our wetlands, coral reefs, Antarctica, and a range of animals, reptiles and sea life." - "The Plastic Problem — In The Plastic Problem, students explore the impact plastic and rubbish have on aquatic environments. The interdependence of living things, food chains and pollution are also covered and examined by students during this unit." - "Sharks and Rays — Learn all about our cartilaginous friends, sharks and stingrays. Should we be afraid or them….or should they be afraid of US? Discover the fascinating biodiversity of the worlds shark species and handle real stingray barbs and shark teeth (live shark not attached!)" - "Rocky Shore Lesson — Life for animals on Hardinge Road's Rocky Shore in Napier is never easy! Every day these animals are battered by the tides, changes in temperature and salinity, and predators. In the Rocky Shore Lesson, students will discover how crabs, sea snails, starfish, sea anemones and fish adapt to protect themselves in this ever-changing rocky shore tide-pool habitat." - "Rocky Shore Visit — Our Aquarium educators can meet your class at Hardinge Road in Napier for a Rocky Shore Visit. While there they'll help with identification of the rocky shore's residents while discussing the adaptations, food chains, tidal zones and conservation of the rocky shore environment. The Rocky Shore visit has a minimal charge to cover our transportation and time, starting at $65 per class with discounts for larger groups." - "Tuna - New Zealand's Native Eels — Put your senses to the test as we learn about the incredible adaptations of our largest freshwater fish, the longfin eel. Sniff, taste and feel your way through our hands-on activities illustrating the way eels sense the world as they journey through their lifecycle. Discover the mystery of how these unique New Zealand fish journey thousands of kilometers across the Pacific ocean to find their home. (Note for food allergies - This lesson involves tasting a low concentration of sugar and food colouring in water)" - "Dinosaurs and Fossils — Dive into dinosaurs and learn about ancient life in Aotearoa. Discover what makes a dinosaur different from other reptiles, and how a fossil forms. Become a paleontologist as you handle real fossils from the amazing Joan Wiffen fossil collection, and then create your own plaster cast fossil to take home and extract yourself!" - "Protecting Pania — By listening to the local Māori legend Pania of the Reef, students learn about the local taonga that is Pania Reef. Discover the multitude of species that call the reef home, and how the use of the reef has changed over time. Pania also faces her share of challenges – learn about some of the sustainability issues of the ocean." - "Adaptations — Adaptations – all fish have them! In this session students discover how diverse ranges of aquatic animals adapt to survive in their environment. Learn how to tell instantly if a fish is fast or slow, predator or prey, and where they might live in an environment. Students will observe examples of fish defences including camouflage, schooling, fish communication and body design." - "Primo Penguins — In Primo Penguins students get to brush up close with these captivating little birds. They'll discover how penguins survive in the incredibly harsh environments they inhabit and learn about what really makes them who they are and live the way they do. Also covered in this unit are conservation issues and what we as humans can do to help protect penguins." - "Technology at the Aquarium — Ever wondered what it takes to operate the National Aquarium's Oceanarium? In Technology at the Aquarium, students will get a behind-the-scenes look at the technology that keeps the Aquarium running. They'll also get to test the salinity, pH and temperature of the water from the Aquarium's tanks to solve a mystery water puzzle." - "Life at the Boundary — Life at the Boundary – In-School Programme. This interactive session is now available on-site at your school for Napier, Hastings, and Central Hawke's Bay schools. Life at the Boundary brings the science of Aotearoa New Zealand's plate boundary to life. This engaging session offers a hands-on learning experience that explores how the Hikurangi Plate Boundary shapes life in our region. Learners will investigate the causes and impacts of earthquakes, tsunami, and liquefaction, all in the context of our local landscapes." - "Food Webs & Adaptations — Who eats who out there in the ocean? Food webs are central to understanding how aquatic ecosystems work. In the Food Webs & Adaptations students examine marine food webs to develop an appreciation of the interactions between life forms beneath the surface. Students will also handle biofacts that show the adaptations that animals have to help them feed (or avoid being food!)." - "Gas Exchange & Dissection — The Gas Exchange & Dissection lesson compliments NCEA 2.6 and comprises three activities: Dissection – Focus on the internal and external features of fish, in particular looking at the gill structures and how they work in the respiration process. Dissolved Oxygen Experiment – Students take samples at four different tanks around the Aquarium, and compare dissolved oxygen levels between various temperature levels. Gas Exchange Tour – Did you know there are fish that can drown underwater? Or that some types of turtle can breathe using their bottoms? This guided tour of the Aquarium focuses on the structures and techniques animals use to breathe in the aquatic world." - "Rocky Shore Transects Study — The Rocky Shore Transects Study lesson compliments Year 12 topics on distribution and zonation. Aquarium experts will meet your class at the Hardinge Road Rocky Shore and provide support as you run your transect studies. We can provide thermometers, hydrometers and ID Charts as well as expert knowledge on all of the species you will find in your quadrats." - "Animal Responses Daphnia Lab — The National Aquarium can facilitate your animal responses practical investigations for NCEA AS 91603. You group will be able to self-direct their daphnia response experiments in our well stocked lab, with a range of options for possible tests. Start with an introduction to daphnia by an aquarium educator and a tour of the lab equipment. Your class can then have the use of the lab and education room for the rest of the day to conduct your experiments." - "Tuna - New Zealand's Native Eels (NCEA) — This hands-on session introduces learners to the many specialised adaptations of native New Zealand tuna. Discover how these eels navigate their way across vast oceanic distances to find their freshwater habitats using super senses. Put your own senses to the test as you sniff, feel and taste your way through hands-on activities illustrating the biology of tuna. This session compliments freshwater studies as part of NCEA level 1 AS91920." - "Te Kawa O Tangaroa - MSC programme — Te Kawa O Tangaroa is an ocean-centred learning programme from the Marine Stewardship Council. Partnering with National Aquarium of New Zealand, the programme is focussed on solutions to overfishing and how we can ensure oceans teeming with life. The resource is aligned to the New Zealand National Curriculum and Te Marautanga o Aotearoa (Maori Curriculum) and designed for learners in Years 7-10 of the New Zealand education system." - "Travel and Tourism — Learn about our place in the New Zealand tourism scene, and chat to staff about how their career pathways lead to working at the National Aquarium. Your students can then experience the aquarium as tourists by exploring their way around our exhibits. The National Aquarium of New Zealand attracts over 100,000 visitors every year. It is home to a wide range of animals large and small, as well as a thriving café and gift shop. We are Qualmark Gold rated and a member of IAAPA, the International Association of Amusement Parks and Attractions." - "Native Animals at the National Aquarium — Introduce your international students to four of our NZ native superstar species that they will see at the National Aquarium. This 30 minute chat sets the scene for international students to see our nationally and culturally significant species: kiwi, little penguins, tuatara and tuna - our native eels. This session includes some hands-on exploration of biofacts such as kiwi feathers and a tuatara skull!"

new-hall-farm-ardsley.md.programme_names: none listed as a named programme. The education page is headed simply "Education"; the venue is described in search-result summaries as running "school visits & educational tours" but no branded programme name appears on the venue's own pages.
new-hall-farm-ardsley.md.activities_verbatim: (drawn from the risk assessment's activity/hazard column, which is the only place specific activities are named): - Weather conditions (farm walk exposure) - Arrival/exiting coach (in farm yard) - Arrival/exiting coach (large coach in layby) - Uneven and/or slippery surface - Injury from vegetation - Injury from infrastructure, fences etc - Water (farm pond) - Climbing - Sitting in a tractor - Milling wheat - Farm Chemicals - Treated crops - Ingestion - Farm animals - Ticks - Missing children - Insects and allergies - Grain stores - Farm operations - Trailer ride - Unstable structures The education page separately lists curriculum topic headings rather than activity names: "living things and classification", "rocks and soils", "carnivores and herbivores", "seasons and climate" (Science); "Use of weights / volumes / areas in farming", "Inputs required – seeds vs fertiliser", "expected yields vs Income", "Value of wheat in a loaf of bread etc." (Maths); "Machinery fit for purpose", "Building design" (Design & Technology); "Use of natural resources", "Sustainability", "Weather and climate, maps" (Geography); "Changes in farming practice", "Mechanisation", "Impact of transport /storage on farming systems", "Population pressure" (History).
new-hall-farm-ardsley.md.duration: none listed. new-hall-farm-ardsley.md.group_size_min_max: none listed on the venue's own pages. The visit-planner.pdf asks the school to state "Number in group" but sets no venue-side minimum or maximum.
new-hall-farm-ardsley.md.participant_thresholds: none listed. new-hall-farm-ardsley.md.equipment_provided: none listed as provided to visiting children (no mention of feed, worksheets, or wristbands). Purpose-made trailer used for trailer rides. Tractor available for children to sit in under supervision. Mill for "milling wheat" activity.
new-hall-farm-ardsley.md.staff_qualifications_stated: none listed. Contact named as "Helen Rhodes" with two phone numbers; no qualification, accreditation, or training level stated for her or other farm staff on the pages read. new-zealand-marine-studies-centre-touch-.programme_names: - Supper in the Sea - Seashore investigation and Marine Metre Squared - The secret life of sharks - Pāpaka Power - Ocean Caretakers - Aotearoa Ocean Histories - NZVR – Exploring our Marine Environment - Online Live from the Shore - Online Live from the Fish Tank - Aquavan Adventures - Mighty Molluscs or Crabs galore - Intertidal investigation - Diversity in form and function - Small animal study - Behaviour of marine animals - Meeting with a Marine Scientist - Marine plastics, from micro to macro - Ocean acidification - NZVR Caring for Taoka species - Monitoring the Moana participatory science
new-zealand-marine-studies-centre-touch-.activities_verbatim: - "Who eats whom in the ocean? Discover how local sea creatures are adapted to catch their food, avoid predators and stay alive. Explore issues regarding sustainability and human impact on the oceans." (Supper in the Sea) - "Uncover the secrets on the seashore by peeking under rocks and in tide pools. Investigate and understand why marine animals live where they do." (Seashore investigation and MM2) - "Find out what species of shark are found in the local areas of the Otago Harbour and off the coast and how they are different from each other. Discover how scientists gather data about sharks and what this information tells us. Explore the external and internal anatomy of a shark and examine the unique features and adaptations it has to survive." (The secret life of sharks) - "Investigate the incredible world of pāpaka (crabs)! Compare a range of local species and learn about their behavioural and structural adaptations to survive in different habitats." (Pāpaka Power) - "Why are humans concerned about plastics? How does it affect our moana? Investigate the local seashore through a Litter Intelligence survey and get up and close to the creatures that live along the coastline. Learn what you can do to be kaitiaki (guardians) of the coastlines." (Ocean Caretakers) - "An introduction to important kaimoana species and taoka marine species in Otago. Go on a Peninsula Headland walk to learn about how kaimoana was collected with different native plants and throughout different seasons, and get up close to some local marine species." (Aotearoa Ocean Histories) - "Experience Aotearoa New Zealand's marine environment through Virtual Reality videos (Blake NZ-VR, New Zealand Geographic). Compare northern and southern environments, pristine and degraded ecosystems. Investigate the causes of environmental damage and how we can be kaitiaki (guardians) for our moana." (NZVR – Exploring our Marine Environment) - "Join a marine scientist on an exploration of the local coastline while it is live-streamed to your classroom. Ask questions and learn great stories to tell your own whānau next time you go to the seashore." (Online Live from the Shore) - "Join a marine scientist and encounter the weird and wonderful adaptations found in the touch tanks. Live-streamed directly to your classroom, students will be encouraged to play along and compare their own adaptations to their distant swimming relatives." (Online Live from the Fish Tank) - "Specially designed to transport marine species, the Aquavan is equipped with chilled re-circulating seawater tanks. During visits to classrooms and community halls, a mobile touch tank supports encounters with a diversity of live marine animals." (Aquavan Adventures) - "How do adaptations identify a taxa and how do variations to these relate to a species' survival in it's niche? Classify molluscs or crustaceans, investigate how they feed and survey the intertidal zone to compare the distribution of their species." (Mighty Molluscs or Crabs galore) - "Investigate adaptations and community structure on the rocky shore using appropriate sampling techniques either as a practice (formative) or final (summative) assessment for NCEA." (Intertidal investigation) - "A comparative study to look at structure and function in relation to survival in particular niches. Adaptations observed and demonstrated with living examples. Laboratory series of comparative dissections." (Diversity in form and function) - "Carry out a practical investigation in a biological context. Focus on one animal species and investigate its behaviour in response to abiotic and biotic factors. Design and carry out individual student investigations." (Small animal study) - "Investigate the behaviour of marine animals in response to abiotic and biotic environmental factors. Living examples of symbioses, predator/prey adaptations, reproductive strategies and biological clocks." (Behaviour of marine animals) - "Investigate ocean currents and anthropogenic impacts through a survey of ocean litter, where data collected feeds directly into the New Zealand waste legislation. Provides students with the training, equipment and technology to take part as 'Citizen Scientists' in the Litter Intelligence Project." (Marine plastics, from micro to macro) - "Carry out a practical investigation in an Earth and Space Science context. Focus on abiotic changes of a future ocean (pH and/or temperature) and investigate the potential physical, ecological, or behavioural impacts." (Ocean acidification) - "Students will learn about the physiology and classification of marine mammals, explore the history of these animals in Aotearoa, and how scientists study them. Discuss environmental and anthropogenic factors that impact local extinctions." (NZVR Caring for Taoka species) - "Use scientific methods to monitor marine communities in all scales. Choose between using microscopes to identify and count plankton, underwater cameras to look for sharks and identify fish, or quadrats to survey the shoreline." (Monitoring the Moana participatory science)

northey-street-city-farm.md.programme_names: "School Activities"; "Basic Farm Tour"; "Farm Tour + Hands-On Activity"; "Primary school Curriculum Linked topics + Hands-on activities"; "Biomes and Food Security Curriculum Linked Tour + Hands-on activities"; "First Nations Schools" (free tour offer); "Group Tours and Experiences" (the general, non-school version of the same tour options); "Workshops for Teachers" (comprising "Successful School Gardening" and "Outdoor Learning and the Curriculum").
northey-street-city-farm.md.activities_verbatim: From the School Activities page: - Basic Farm Tour (1.5h) - All Year levels: "Take an interactive and sensory walk through the food gardens, fruit orchards, food forests, and recycling systems of Northey Street City Farm. Meet the farm and wildlife which make NSCF their safe haven and taste the yummy honey from our bees." - Farm Tour + Hands-On Activity (2-2.5h) - All Year levels, one of: - Compost-making (2h): "Explore the different compost systems on the farm, experience what is needed to create compost, and learn about its benefits." - Propagation (2.5h): "Discuss different methods of propagation and get your hands dirty while propagating some of the plants found around our gardens." - Soil investigation (2h): "Investigate soil health and explore its role in the web of life. Collect soil samples from our gardens and conduct tests to understand the elements that may impact plant growth and erosion." - Australian Bush plants exploration (2h): "Take a walk around the farm to explore the smells, textures, and tastes of some Australian native plants." - Earth Connection (2h): "Take a sensory walk through the bush regeneration area and observe the flora and fauna around you. This grounding activity may involve learning bird language, practicing sit spots, journaling, and/or creating ephemeral nature mosaics." - Primary school Curriculum Linked topics + Hands-on activities (2-2.5h) - Prep to Year 6: "Take a guided tour of the City Farm to see permaculture in action, with a focus on curriculum linked topics according to the year level and interests of the group. After the tour, students have a chance to engage in one of the hands-on activities described below." Hands-on activities to choose from: Compost-making (2h); Soil investigation (2h); Propagation (2.5h) (descriptions as above). - Biomes and Food Security Curriculum Linked Tour + Hands-on activities (2-2.5h) - Years 9 to 12: "Take a guided tour of the City Farm to see permaculture in action. Students learn how permaculture can contribute to food security and provide an important alternative to conventional agriculture. An education kit with curriculum-linked worksheets and resources for teachers is available for the 'Biomes and Food Security' Year 9 Geography unit." Hands-on activities in groups of up to 20 participants: Compost-making (2h); Soil investigation (2h); Propagation (2.5h); Mapping (2h): "Explore the concept of permaculture zones, food forests, and experience what is involved in designing a garden that contributes to food security. Participants can choose to map different areas of the farm, including the market garden, the kitchen garden, the backyard garden, the native food and medicine garden, the orchard, the allotment gardens, and the woodlot, or create their own design." - "First Nations Schools: We provide free tours to one year level for at least one First Nations school per year." From the Group Tours and Experiences page (worded slightly differently from the School Activities page for the same option set, and adding options not listed on the school page): - Basic Tour (1.5h) - All Ages: same wording as above with "delicious honey" in place of "yummy honey". - Farm tour + Hands-on Activity (2-2.5h) - All ages, additional options beyond those on the School Activities page: - Salad-making (2.5h): "Harvest fresh leaf greens, edible flowers, and fruits from our gardens and orchards to create a nutritious and delicious salad to share with your group. This hands-on activity is subjected to seasons and produce availability." - Eco-arts making (2h): "Express your creativity using natural, repurposed, and recyclable materials. This grounding, sensory activity may involve making clay sculptures, painting with natural pigments, or creating ephemeral art pieces." - Holiday Combinations - 5 years +, "a great option for Outside School Hours Care groups": - Farm adventure + nature games (2h): "The adventure experience may include activities such as a treasure hunt, bird watching, seasonal observations, tasting, and tree climbing. Participants will also enjoy nature-based games that expand their senses and foster a deeper connection with the outdoors, while having fun." - Farm adventure + gardening (2h): "The adventure experience may include activities such as a treasure hunt, bird watching, seasonal observations, tasting, and tree-climbing. For the gardening session, depending on the season, participants may be invited to plant, make seed balls, investigate soil creatures, make compost, build insect habitats, and/or do some weeding, mulching and watering." - Farm adventure + Seasonal Arts and Crafts (2h): "The adventure experience may include activities such as a treasure hunt, bird watching, seasonal observations, tasting, and tree climbing. Then, participants are invited to express their creativity using natural, repurposed, and recyclable materials to design amazing artwork! This grounding, sensory activity may involve making clay sculptures, painting with natural pigments, or creating ephemeral art pieces." - Shelter building + Nature-based games (2.5h): "Participants are invited to flex their muscles and build some awesome kid-sized shelters in the woodlot using bamboo grown at the Farm! Then, enjoy nature-based games to expand their senses and foster a deeper connection with the outdoors."
northey-street-city-farm.md.duration: Basic Tour: 1.5h. Farm tour + hands-on activity: 2-2.5h. Compost-making: 2h. Propagation: 2.5h. Soil investigation: 2h. Australian Bush/Native plants exploration: 2h. Earth Connection: 2h. Salad-making: 2.5h. Eco-arts making: 2h. Mapping: 2h. Holiday combinations: 2-2.5h.

The Group Tours and Experiences page states different, slightly higher prices for what appears to be the same option set: Basic Tour $18 per person ($270 group minimum); Compost-making $22 per person ($330 minimum); Propagation $28 per person ($420 minimum); Soil investigation $22 per person ($330 minimum); Australian Native plants exploration $22 per person ($330 minimum); Salad-making $28 per person ($420 minimum); Earth Connection $22 per person ($330 minimum); Eco-arts making $24 per person ($360 minimum). Holiday Combinations: Farm adventure + nature games $24 p/participant ($360 group minimum); Farm adventure + gardening $26 p/participant ($390 group minimum); Farm adventure + Seasonal Arts and Crafts $26 p/participant ($390 group minimum); Shelter building + Nature-based games $28 p/participant ($420 group minimum). "Prices are for weekdays only and are on a per person basis. Weekends may be arranged upon request and will have a higher cost."

northey-street-city-farm.md.price_visible_without_asking: Yes: per-participant prices and group minimums for every tour and activity option are published directly on the School Activities and Group Tours and Experiences pages.

northey-street-city-farm.md.testimonials_from_schools: Yes, one, on the School Activities page under "Teacher Testimonials": "OMG, our trip was absolutely amazing! The children had so much fun and learned so many new things. They had numerous experiences, from rubbing leaves between their fingers to feeding chooks, checking out a bush turkey's nest, picking and eating fresh vegetables and wild plums, exploring the inside of a beehive, and tasting the honey. I was in the group led by Richard, who was truly amazing with the kids — so patient and accommodating. The other educators were fantastic as well. We really want to thank them for their patience with our kids and for giving us the incredible opportunity to visit your farm. A special thank you to Bob! Many of the children mentioned that meeting him was one of the highlights of the trip." — Anna Megueria, Classroom Teacher, 1/2A, Runcorn Heights State School. (Additional testimonials on the Workshops for Teachers page are attributed to individual teachers, a Forest School Practitioner, a school gardening educator and a homeschool parent, not to schools as institutions, and concern the teacher professional-development workshops rather than the student school-visit programme.)
northey-street-city-farm.md.title_and_opening_line: "School Activities. Northey Street City Farm offers a range of educational activities suitable for all age groups. These activities provide students with an opportunity to learn about permaculture practices and experience the life of an urban farm. They have also been designed to work across curriculum and fit a number of learning outcomes."

orana-wildlife-park.md.activities_verbatim: - "Kaitiakitanga - Years 1-13 ākonga will observe a variety of native and exotic animal species and discover what makes them so unique in our world. They will discuss how humans can have positive and negative impacts on the natural world and learn how the concept of Tiakitanga can help protect living things and the environment." - "TUrangawaewae - Years 1-8 Tūrangawaewae is one of the most well-known and powerful Māori concepts that connects people to places. Ākonga will think about what it would have been like to be early arrivals in Aotearoa, and learn how different cultures' tools and technolgies helped them to adapt to the new environments they encountered." - "ADAPTATIONS - YEARS 1-11 ākonga will observe a wide range of animals from around the world and learn about their behavioural, structural and physiological adaptations, that help them survive in their particular habitat." - "THE ROLE OF MODERN ZOOS - YEARS 1-13 Through observing animals in captivity, ākonga will learn how animals are cared for to ensure their well-being and the efforts made to prevent their extinction." - "COMMUNITIES AND ROLES - YEARS 1-10 ākonga will observe a variety of animals living in different communities and learn how these communities are structured to ensure the survival of group members." - "KAIMAWHAIWHAI (FOOD WEBS) - YEARS 1-8 Through observing native and exotic wildlife, ākonga will discuss the sources of energy and energy flow from one organism to another in a food web." - "HUMAN EVOLUTION - YEAR 13 L3 Biology AS 91606 Developed to specifically support achievement standard AS 91606, this programme covers the human journey over the last six million years." - From the Activities page: "Animal feeds are scheduled throughout the day and these can be incorporated into the programme for appropriate species." - "Special animal encounters can be arranged with the keepers to allow a closer look at the animals, including, but not limited to, rhinoceros, tuatara, giraffe and tortoise." - "Behind-the-scenes access can also be arranged for many areas of the Park where these will add to the students' learning." - "Creating enrichment for the animals is a constant challenge for keepers and students can apply their innovation and dexterity to develop special devices that will keep animals healthy and stimulated." - "CITES Items are those animal 'parts' that, under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species, are confiscated from people entering New Zealand... a special arrangement with Department of Conservation and NZ Customs allows us to utilise their educational value in our programmes." - "Replica skulls for a range of primates and hominins, and carnivores and herbivores can be utilised in programmes to allow students to conduct more detailed biological analysis of adaptations."
