otari-wiltons-bush-wellington-botanic-ga.programme_names: - Soil to Plate (Hands-On Food Learning in the Discovery Garden) - From Ngahere to Moana: Exploring a Living Catchment - Food - 2026 - Hands-on learning (Seed Sowing & Paper Pots / Healing Plant Balm / Wormery Workshop) - Planting through the seasons - Plants in Space - Be with a Tree and its Community - Healing Plants: Nature's Remedies - Building with Plants - Early Childhood Visits
otari-wiltons-bush-wellington-botanic-ga.activities_verbatim: - "Soil to plate — Hands-On Food Learning in the Discovery Garden. Students explore plants, soil, and food through three hands-on activities during a 2 hour session. Every session is curriculum-aligned, flexible to the season, and designed to be engaging, interactive, and age-appropriate." - "Planting & Potting: Sow seeds in paper pots or refresh the mara kai, learning how to care for plants." - "Soil & Wormery Exploration: Observe soil life, explore decomposition, and understand nutrient cycles." - "Harvest & Taste: Pick and taste seasonal kai, link plant parts to meals, and plan seasonal menus." - "From Ngahere to Moana: Exploring a Living Catchment — Bring your students into the heart of a living catchment, where forest, stream, and city connect. Set within Ōtari–Wilton's Bush, this hands-on, curriculum-aligned session gives ākonga the opportunity to explore how water moves through the environment, how ecosystems are connected, and how we can act as kaitiaki to protect them." - "Many Waters, One Stream - Observe a tributary meeting the main stream and explore how water comes from multiple sources across the landscape." - "Catchment Filter Challenge - Build and test a model to see how water changes as it moves from ngahere to awa and toward the moana, and how this affects the mauri of the system." - "Planting for the Awa - Become kaitiaki by selecting and growing native plants to protect and restore the stream environment." - "Food — Location: Discovery Garden at Wellington Botanic Garden. Seeds, soil, sustainable planting, and self-sufficiency are just some of the levelled elements of this programme. Tamariki will learn through different activities about the parts and functions of a plant, their growing needs, how environmental changes affect their productivity, and urban planting. Making a paper pot and planting seeds in the potting garden, exploring the productive food garden, and feeding worms in the wormery are just some of the things to expect during this hands-on programme." - "Seed Sowing & Paper Pots: Students make paper pots, sow seeds, and take home their seedlings to grow their own kai." - "Healing Plant Balm: Explore native and introduced plants such as kawakawa and lavender, and make a take-home balm, learning about plant properties and traditional uses." - "Wormery Workshop: Learn to create a worm farm at home or school, recycling organic waste and enriching soil while connecting to zero-waste principles." - "Planting through the seasons — Wellington Botanic Garden ki Paekākā Education team have taken a giant leap into space with this, one of two ELC programmes which are designed to complement a visit to Space Place. This programme makes real-world links to our seasons. Tamariki will learn why we seasonally plant different things by taking part in some hands-on relevant mahi in the Discovery Garden based on the maramataka." - "Plants in space — Location: Discovery Garden at Wellington Botanic Garden. This second space related programme is designed for years 5-8. Plants in space looks at how we depend heavily on Earth's natural resources and how we need alternative ways to grow productive, healthy plants in space... One activity is looking at seeds in different growing medium and learning how well they grow inside a growing tent with artificial light, a similar process to that used in the space station. Hydroponics and aquaponics are other alternative growing methods introduced during this programme." - "Be with a tree and its community — Your tamariki will explore the mauri or life force of some very old trees on site at Ōtari-Wilton's Bush. Using science capabilities, they will learn about the role of trees not only for our survival but for the many other communities which rely on them and who we share this amazing planet Earth with." - "Healing Plants: Nature's Remedies — Did you know that during World War I, sphagnum moss was used as a life-saving wound dressing? On this learning session, students explore healing plants through hands-on activities that connect science, history, culture, and wellbeing." - "Medicinal plant walks (native plants and the Lotions & Potions garden)" - "Balm making or herbal tea making" - "Propagation using a handmade paper pot (sown seed and/or cutting)" - "A kawakawa tea break is always included." - "Building with Plants — Hands-on exploration of native and introduced plants for tools, structures, and craft. Students explore how plants support practical life and resourcefulness. Through hands-on activities, tamariki learn how Māori used native plants — such as harakeke for weaving strong fibres and tī kōuka for building materials — to make tools, shelters, and implements." - "Māori Plant Exploration Walks: Identify native trees and introduced plants used for practical purposes, such as weaving or crafting." - "Hands-On Construction: Build temporary shelters, small kites, or weaving projects." - "Environmental Construction: Construct a simple fish ladder using native plants, learning how traditional knowledge informs sustainable environmental solutions today." - "Early Childhood Visits — Join our educators for an hour-long session at just $5 per child to experience both the wider garden and the Discovery Garden. Tamariki will learn about plants with fun activities that cater to your group's needs (minimum of 10 children)."

parc-marin-du-saguenay-saint-laurent.md.participant_thresholds: none listed Note: the site's main menu (Visiter, Naviguer, Protéger, Connaître, Emplois, Nouvelles, Projet d'agrandissement, À propos) carries no schools or education-programme item. The "Connaître" page covers conservation projects and environmental monitoring, not a school offer. The "Visiter" page describes whale watching, boat excursions, sea kayaking, diving, hiking and interpretation-centre visits open to the general public, with no school-specific programme, activity list or age-graded content. ## Inventory
parc-marin-du-saguenay-saint-laurent.md.facilities: Interpretation centres at Cap-de-Bon-Désir, Pointe-Noire and other locations; hiking trails and viewpoints; a Parks Canada office in Tadoussac (182, rue de l'Église) and a SÉPAQ office in Rivière-Éternité (91, rue Notre-Dame); a seasonal reception post in La Malbaie during summer.
parc-marin-du-saguenay-saint-laurent.md.animal_species_held: none listed. The park is a marine protected area for wild, free-ranging species; the site states "une région marine où la diversité animale et végétale est exceptionnelle : des algues microscopiques à la gigantesque baleine bleue" with over 2,000 wildlife species observed in the park, but this describes wild populations in situ, not species held by the venue. ## Curriculum
parc-marin-du-saguenay-saint-laurent.md.price_and_structure: "L'accès au territoire du parc marin est gratuit" (access to the marine park territory is free). "Les excursions en mer, les visites dans les musées et centres d'interprétation et certaines randonnées sont payantes" (boat excursions, museum/interpretation-centre visits and some hikes are paid), but no specific figures are given on the pages read.
parc-marin-du-saguenay-saint-laurent.md.booking_lead_time: Reservations are "strongly recommended, particularly during high season (mid-July to end of August)"; no lead-time figure given. ## Conversion
parc-marin-du-saguenay-saint-laurent.md.how_to_book: none listed on the pages read. A "Professionnels de voyage" (travel-trade professionals) link exists on the homepage, pointing to an external Parks Canada page.
parc-marin-du-saguenay-saint-laurent.md.price_visible_without_asking: No. The Visiter page states that excursions, museum/interpretation-centre visits and some hikes are payable, but no prices appear on the pages read.
parc-marin-du-saguenay-saint-laurent.md.title_and_opening_line: Homepage title/nav: "Visiter" as first menu item; mission statement from the About page: "La mission du parc marin est de rehausser, au profit des générations actuelles et futures, le niveau de protection de ses écosystèmes aux fins de conservation, tout en favorisant les activités éducatives, récréatives et scientifiques."

parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.school_offer_detail_level: activity_list_no_timings: a named activity for school groups at Jacques-Cartier is described, with a curriculum link and a stated price (free), but no duration or timed schedule.
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.programme_names: "Activités scolaires en nature" (network-wide) is the umbrella name; within it, "Les ateliers fauniques" is a sub-category. A separate general offer is signposted as "Activités scolaires pour le primaire" and "Activités scolaires pour le secondaire" on the park's own page, but no activity names are given under those headings in the content read.
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.activities_verbatim: Sur les traces de la faune
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.facilities: Centre de découverte et de services (km 10). Amphithéâtre of 100 places ("notre amphithéâtre de 100 places situé en plein coeur de la vallée offre un magnifique cadre naturel pour des présentations en tout genre"). Pavillon du Lac-à-l'Épaule, stated as the origin of the expression "faire un lac-à-l'épaule". Camping sectors: L'Escarpement, Alluvions, Bétulaie, Grand-Duc, Héron, Morillon, Hirondelles, plus a designated "camping de groupe" area. 16 "prêt-à-camper Étoile" units in the L'Escarpement and Alluvions sectors, described as cubic wood-frame units sleeping 6 with three double beds. Chalet Écho units, described as two-bedroom four-season chalets with kitchen and bathroom. Boutique Nature, where wildlife and flora identification guides are sold. 13 named snowshoe trails totalling "près de 94 km", including L'Escarpement (11.2 km loop). Three mountain-bike trails, "plus de 30 km de sentiers".
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.equipment_provided: Snowshoe rental ("location de raquettes"), stated as free for children ("gratuit pour les enfants"). Canoe rental and shuttle service for canot-camping ("possibilité de réserver votre canot et le service de navette").
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.staff_qualifications_stated: Activities are led by a "garde-parc naturaliste" or "garde-parc passionné"; no further credential, certification body, or qualification level is stated.
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.animal_species_held: none listed. The park's "Observation de la faune" section names moose (orignal), beaver (castor), white-tailed deer (cerf de Virginie), red fox (renard), porcupine (porc-épic), brook trout (omble de fontaine), and "plus de 130 espèces d'oiseaux" as wild species observable in the park, but these are described as wild and free-ranging, not as animals the venue holds. ## Curriculum
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.curriculum_links: "Sur les traces de la faune": "Cette activité répond aux objectifs du PFEQ « Science et technologie - Univers vivant » pour le secondaire 1."
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.accreditations_displayed: The park's shuttle-tour partner Quatre Natures is described as "membre d'Aventure Écotourisme Québec (accrédité Qualité-Sécurité)", a partner's accreditation, not the park's own. ## Commercial
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.price_and_structure: "Sur les traces de la faune": "Activité gratuite." General public interpretation activities (not school-specific) carry adult prices: "Sous les roches géantes", 9,25 $ par adulte; "En rabaska au fil de l'eau", 13,50 $ par adulte; "Rendez-vous avec la lune", 13,50 $ par adulte; "Castor, un maître bâtisseur", stated as "Activité gratuite (nombre de places limité, premier arrivé premier servi)"; "Mystères de la nuit", 13,50 $ par adulte. Each of these general activities states children are free in a family context ("Gratuit pour les enfants de 6 à 17 ans en contexte familial" or "de 10 à 17 ans" depending on the activity); this is a family-visit condition, not a school-group rate.
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.booking_lead_time: Backcountry access permits: "Prévoyez au maximum 7 jours pour le traitement de votre demande." ## Conversion
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.how_to_book: "Informations et réservations: 418 848-3169, poste 6930, groupes.pnjc@sepaq.com" (stated for "Groupes jeunesse: se connecter à la nature" and for corporate/group camping bookings). The schools section separately shows a "Réserver" button beside "Activités scolaires pour le primaire" and "Activités scolaires pour le secondaire" without further detail in the content read. The network-wide "Sur les traces de la faune" activity carries a "Détails et inscriptions" link and a "Remplir le formulaire de demande" link for the "Destination nature pour tous!" ministry-funded access programme.
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.price_visible_without_asking: Partially. The one named school activity states its price ("Activité gratuite"); no price is shown for any other school programming.
parc-national-de-la-jacques-cartier.md.title_and_opening_line: Schools page title: "Activités scolaires" (breadcrumb shows this nested under Parc national de la Jacques-Cartier). Opening line: "Il n'y a rien de plus fascinant que la nature! Elle suscite la curiosité, émerveille nos sens et apporte son lot de découvertes. Grâce à nos activités éducatives amusantes et adaptées au programme scolaire, offrez à vos élèves la chance de se connecter avec la plus belle nature du Québec." Park home page title: "Parc national de la Jacques-Cartier". The "Groupes scolaires" section opening line: "Lieu de conservation et d'éducation, les parcs nationaux sont de véritables laboratoires en milieu naturel. Venez y faire classe en compagnie de nos gardes-parcs passionnés ou accueillez-les dans votre école!"

pensthorpe-natural-park.md.programme_names: - Discover: Food chains - Discover: Habitats - Discover: Pensthorpe's dinosaurs - Discover: Plants and Pollinators - Discover: Classification - Discover: Life cycles - Discover: Birds
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.activities_verbatim: - Discover: Food chains - Discover: Habitats - Discover: Pensthorpe's dinosaurs - Discover: Plants and Pollinators - Discover: Classification - Discover: Life cycles - Discover: Birds - Pond dipping - WildRootz outdoor play - Hootz House indoor play - Craft activities - Bird feed
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.duration: none listed as a stated number of hours; the venue describes a mix of "short indoor activities" in the Discovery Centre and a purpose-built classroom-sized hide, combined with outdoor exploration, without giving a session length.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.participant_thresholds: "1 free adult per 5 paying students; additional adults charged at £6.95" (a supervision ratio, not a group-size minimum or maximum). ## Inventory
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.facilities: Discovery Centre; a purpose-built classroom-sized hide; seven family-friendly bird hides; Wader Scrape with two hides; Wader Aviary; Wildflower Meadow with boardwalk; Pensthorpe Explorer (off-road vehicle experience); four garden spaces described on the education page context as "five stunning gardens" elsewhere (Millennium Garden, Wildlife Habitat Garden, Corten Infinity Garden, The Glade Sculpture Garden, Wave Garden, Biosonification Garden listed on the things-to-do page); WildRootz and Hootz House play areas; Courtyard Café; shop and gallery.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.equipment_provided: none listed specific to school visits beyond the activity sheets noted under teacher_materials; four wheelchairs available at no cost (general visitor provision, not school-specific) and three electric scooters for hire at £10 per day.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.staff_qualifications_stated: "Pond dipping" is noted as "always staff-led"; no named qualification (e.g. DBS, first aid certificate) stated on the pages read.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.accessibility_provision: "Wheelchair users can explore all five of our stunning gardens, as well as the popular Wetland Hide." Disabled parking approximately 100 metres from the entrance, with drop-off near the courtyard. "We have three electric scooters available for hire at a cost of £10 per day." Four wheelchairs available at no cost, first-come first-served, reservable by phone. "Interpretation boards have pictorial representation where applicable and large print copies of our park guide are available upon request." Audio systems used in various locations. Accessible toilets outside the main entrance near the coach park, in the Courtyard Café, WildRootz, and Hootz House. Dietary accommodation for vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, dairy-free, nut-free, and sugar-free diets, with a request to call ahead. "Strictly no animals are allowed to enter the park, except accredited assistance dogs."
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.animal_species_held: Bittern, Bearded Tit, waders (described collectively as "breeding waders"), waterfowl (described collectively as "wintering waterfowl"), birds of prey, dragonflies, butterflies, demoiselle damselflies. ## Curriculum
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.curriculum_links: The seven "Discover" sessions are stated to be "produced using the national curriculum as a guideline"; no individual subject or key-stage links beyond that general statement were found on the pages read.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.teacher_materials: "activity sheets which is completed during the visit and retained by the pupils" [sic]. "Complimentary tickets for two teachers" are offered for pre-visit planning. Downloadable resources found on the education page: "Bee Friendly Activities" PDF (https://pensthorpe.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/Project-Pollinate-Top-Tips-2022.pdf) and "Wildlife Activities (Nature Playlist)" PDF (https://pensthorpe.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/Nature-Play-List_2022_English.pdf), neither explicitly framed as school-visit teacher packs on the page text. Park Map PDFs also found: https://pensthorpe.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/04/Pensthorpe_Park-Map.pdf and https://pensthorpe.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/New-Map-V7-spring.pdf. ## Trust
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.price_and_structure: "Base rate: £6.95 per student" (school visit). General admission (non-school) varies by season: Summer Holidays (18 July - 2 September) adult £16.95 (£15.95 online), senior £15.95 (£14.95 online), child (3+) £16.95 (£15.95 online), child (0-3) £3.00 (£2.00 online); September-October term time (3 September - 22 October) adult £15.95 (£14.95 online), senior £14.95 (£13.95 online), child (3+) £15.95 (£14.95 online); October half term reserve-only adult £10.95 (£9.95 online), child £10.95 (£9.95 online), senior £9.95 (£8.95 online); Pumpkin Patch Only £5.00 all ages; Pumpkin & Play Pass adult £12.95 (£11.95 online), child £12.95 (£11.95 online), senior £11.95 (£10.95 online); Winter (2 November - 25 December) adult £10.95 (£9.95 online), senior £9.95 (£8.95 online), child (3+) £10.95 (£9.95 online); Twixmas (26 December - 3 January) adult £13.95, senior £12.95, child (3+) £13.95. Camping "From £30"; glamping "From £120". Optional add-ons for school visits: pond dipping £1/child (April-October, always staff-led); craft activities £1.50/child; bird feed £1.50/child (unavailable during DEFRA restrictions); WildRootz and Hootz House play free. Group & School Visits are noted to exist but the pricing page directs visitors to contact admissions directly for group rates rather than listing them there.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.adults_free_ratio: "1 free adult per 5 paying students; additional adults charged at £6.95." Registered carers for 1:1 students attend free (noted on booking form). Separately, for general (non-school) admission: "One essential carer receives complimentary entry with proof when accompanying a full-paying person who is physically or mentally impaired."
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.catering: Pre-booked packed lunches £5.95/child, £9.95/adult. Courtyard Café serving "drinks, snacks, light lunches and freshly prepared hot meals." Dogs welcome at the café (no dogs on the reserve except assistance animals).
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.cancellation_and_weather: "Rainy Day Guarantee: If your visit is disrupted by more than one hour of consecutive rain, we will issue you with a ticket for a free return visit." Stated as "Not applicable to group/school bookings or Gardeners' World 2 for 1 passes." No school-specific cancellation policy stated.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.booking_lead_time: "Save £1pp by booking online 48 hours in advance" (general admission, not stated as school-specific). ## Conversion
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.how_to_book: Phone 01328 851465 (option 2); email education@pensthorpe.com; online booking form at pensthorpe.com/school-booking-form/. Schools may choose "led visits" or "self-led" visits.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.price_visible_without_asking: Yes — "£6.95 per student" base rate is stated directly on the school visits page.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.downloadable_pack: Yes — "Bee Friendly Activities" and "Wildlife Activities (Nature Playlist)" PDFs found on the education page, plus park map PDFs, though none is explicitly labelled as a school-visit teacher pack.
pensthorpe-natural-park.md.title_and_opening_line: Title: "School Visits" (page heading context: "outdoor classroom"). rainforestation-nature-park.md.programme_names: "School Programs & Educational Groups"; "Cairns Vacation Care Programs"; from the brochure: "All Australian Experience", "Rainforest & Wildlife", "Dreamtime Discovery", "Indigenous Experience"
rainforestation-nature-park.md.activities_verbatim: From the School Programs page: "Our All Australian Experience includes a 45 minute Army Duck Tour on which children can learn about various rainforest flora and fauna."; "Your class can enjoy a cultural experience on the Pamagirri Aboriginal Experience."; "View indigenous dances at the Pamagirri Dance Show and embrace Indigenous culture on the Dreamtime Walk. Children will watch a didgeridoo and spear throwing presentation and will learn to throw a boomerang themselves!"; "Students can get up close to a plethora of Native Australia animals on a 30 minute interactive wildlife tour, including tree kangaroos, Tasmanian Devils, snakes and koalas."; "We also offer solely indigenous experiences so that students can experience Indigenous culture in an authentic setting in the midst of World Heritage Rainforest. Students join a Pamagirri Aboriginal Guide as he shares a personal insight into his culture on the Pamagirri Rainforest Walkabout. They will learn about traditional customs including totems, body painting and rainforest survival." From the brochure, per named combo package: "Army Duck Tour (45 Minutes) — Students will board an amphibious World War II Army Duck for a land and water adventure through the rainforest, as their Duck Captain identifies and explains fascinating plants, including ferns, orchids, strangler figs and the infamous stinging tree. Students will keep an eye out for turtles, fish, eels, birds, pythons and other reptiles on land."; "Pamagirri Dance Performance (30 Minutes) — The Pamagirri Aboriginal Experience offers students the opportunity to see a traditional dance performance in the setting of a beautiful Rainforest Amphitheatre. This cultural experience is not only educational, but fun, with the opportunity for willing students to get up on stage and join a dance!"; "Dreamtime Walk (30 Minutes) — This guided tour, along an all-weather walk-way, gives insight into Aboriginal traditions and beliefs, and how several ancient implements were used. After a Boomerang throwing demonstration and lessons from their guide, students can test their boomerang throwing skills. Next their guide will explain how the didgeridoo is made and used in ceremonies, then will demonstrate techniques used to play this ancient instrument. Students will also be amazed at the distance their guide can throw spears using a Woomera during the spear throwing demonstration."; "Wildlife Park (30 Minutes) — Students will have 30 minutes to explore the wildlife park, hand feed the free-roaming Kangaroos and learn about a variety of native Australian wildlife including the three most special to Tropical North Queensland – the Saltwater Crocodile, Tree Kangaroo and Southern Cassowary."; "Optional Tree Planting Experience (60 minutes, includes Rainforest Tour) — Along the track, the Army Duck will make a stop allowing the students to disembark and begin their tree planting experience. Students will be planting locally sourced native rainforest species selected for their ability to attract wildlife. Their driver will guide them within the rainforest provide instructions on how to plant the tree and teach them about the importance of reforestation."; "Aboriginal Face Painting — Many Aboriginal communities have been painting their bodies for thousands of years. During this face painting session, students learn about the significance of body painting and experience it first-hand."; "Pamagirri Rainforest Walkabout or Yarning Circle (45 minutes) — For groups of 12 students or less, the Rainforest Walkabout is an interactive tour that will teach students about the diversity of Indigenous cultures around Australia and some common customs such as totems and body painting before embarking on a guided walk in the Rainforest to identify plants used for bush tucker or medicinal remedies as well as traditional artefacts, tools and weapons. To cater for larger groups, the Yarning Circle provides a safe forum for open sharing and discussion of issues related to Indigenous Culture. Each discussion is led by Pamagirri Guides and subject matter can be directed by the participating students or their attending teachers."; "Boomerang Painting (30 mins) — With guidance from a Pamagirri Artist, each member of the group paints their own Boomerang to take home on the day – 1 Boomerang per person."; "Canvas Art Workshop (30 mins) — With guidance from a Pamagirri Artist, each member of the group creates their own small 5"x7" canvas of Aboriginal style artwork. All canvases can be taken home on the day." From the Group Activities & Team Building page, offered to groups of all kinds including schools: "Tree Planting — A fun and rewarding way for guests to learn about forest conservation. road-farm-countryways.md.programme_names: none listed (no named programme titles; the offer is described as a general "School Visits" service)
road-farm-countryways.md.activities_verbatim: - Climate emergency: covering sustainability, and climate change and how farming is addressing this. - Farming Everyday: lambing, calving (only in the spring) and general running of a mixed farm. - Field to Plate: Looking at arable crops as well as livestock, where they start and where they finish. - Geology & Development: The role of Flints & water in historic settlement and importance of FIRE! - Historic Landscapes: considering succession, grassland management, hedge maintenance etc - Mini-beasts and Meadows: Grasslands and woodlands as vital habitats - Orchards: Management and maintenance, using the produce - Sustainability & Subsistence: Exploring world agriculture including keyhole gardens & donkeys.

road-farm-countryways.md.facilities: - Purpose built and fully accessible toilet and hand washing block with Changing Places facility; portable four-hand-washing facility. - Kitchen area. - Areas for wet weather shelter are also in agricultural use ie. Working barns for hay/straw and livestock. - Parking available. - Historic, recently restored buildings around a courtyard. - Small pond, easily & safely viewed. - Arable fields, grassland and typical Chilterns geology - Woodland, hedgerows and plentiful wildlife (in Countryside Stewardship). - 'Tent in the orchard' and well stocked orchard

road-farm-countryways.md.accessibility_provision: "Purpose built and fully accessible toilet and hand washing block with Changing Places facility; portable four-hand-washing facility."

rockhampton-zoo.md.programme_names: none listed. Rockhampton Zoo publishes no named school programme or excursion product; visiting groups take part in the same general-public offering as any visitor.
rockhampton-zoo.md.activities_verbatim: "Rockhampton Zoo is unable to provide private tours or talks for schools and groups. However, if you do wish to have a guided tour customised to your group, there is a company called TIME SAFARIS Rockhampton who do offer this service." "Rockhampton Zoo has a range of online Keeper Talks on our website." "Rockhampton Zoo runs daily Keeper Talks, where you can meet our keepers in person and learn all about our animals. You may also get to see our keepers offering food or enrichment items to our animals. There is opportunity to ask a couple of questions at the end of each talk." "Rockhampton Zoo also has an online self-guided tour, which guests can access using their phones during their visit," which "includes individual animal profiles and fun facts about them."
rockhampton-zoo.md.duration: none listed as a number; the Keeper Talks page states "Keeper Talk times can be found here," linking to a page (Daily keeper talks at the Zoo) whose only timing content is an image graphic (keeper-talk-times.png) that could not be read as text after WebFetch and curl were both blocked with HTTP 403
rockhampton-zoo.md.facilities: "a toilet block with an accessible toilet and baby-change table at Rockhampton Zoo's main entrance"; "four large picnic tables with umbrellas...on the grassy area just inside the Rockhampton Zoo main entrance"; "benches...located throughout Rockhampton Zoo"; "picnic tables, a playground and public BBQs located within the Botanic Gardens, a short walk from Rockhampton Zoo"; "The Gardens Tearooms is a cafe that offers delicious food, drink and seating areas in the botanic gardens"; free parking "available for all vehicles" with "Bus parking...a short walk along a footpath to the zoo main entrance," and, per the Useful Information page, free parking additionally stated for "buses, caravans, and motorcycles" plus bicycle racks, though "bicycles, rollerblades, skateboards, and similar personal transport devices cannot be taken inside the zoo"
rockhampton-zoo.md.staff_qualifications_stated: none listed. Keepers are described by role only ("meet our keepers in person"), with no stated qualification or training standard.
rockhampton-zoo.md.accessibility_provision: "a toilet block with an accessible toilet and baby-change table" is the only accessibility-specific provision named on the pages read; no wheelchair-access statement, sensory provision, or assistance-animal policy specific to school groups appears, though the Useful Information page states registered service animals are welcome generally, with the request that they "do not stop at the chimpanzee or dingo enclosures, or enter the kangaroo paddock"

rockhampton-zoo.md.curriculum_links: none listed. The Our contribution/Education page (read as an extra source) carries no curriculum content of its own, stating only "Check out our learning opportunities and materials Here," which links back to the online Keeper Talks and Schools and Groups pages already read.
rockhampton-zoo.md.accreditations_displayed: "Rockhampton Zoo is an accredited member of the Zoo and Aquarium Association, the peak body representing the community of leading zoo and aquariums throughout the Australasian region." "Please see our ZAA certificate here.(PDF, 206KB)" (link given, not followed, as it is a certificate rather than an information pack, price list or risk assessment). "Rockhampton Zoo abides by the Zoo and Aquarium Associations Australasian Species Management Program which is a framework designed to cooperatively manage animal collections to promote collection sustainability and its value as a conservation resource." ## Commercial
rockhampton-zoo.md.price_and_structure: "Entry to Rockhampton Zoo is FREE." "Rockhampton Zoo is owned and operated by Rockhampton Regional Council." No school-specific charge, package or add-on price is published on the pages read; entry is free for all visitor types alike.

rockhampton-zoo.md.catering: "The Gardens Tearooms is a cafe that offers delicious food, drink and seating areas in the botanic gardens"; the same Useful Information page adds "public BBQs...within the Botanic Gardens, just a short walk away"; no school-group catering package, pre-order, or price is stated

rockhampton-zoo.md.downloadable_pack: none listed. The ZAA accreditation certificate is a PDF link but is a certificate, not an information pack, price list or risk assessment, so it was not followed and is not counted here.
rockhampton-zoo.md.title_and_opening_line: Title: "Schools and Groups". Opening line: "Please email Rockhampton Zoo to confirm your visit." ## Note Rockhampton Zoo passes the spec's selection standard on a narrow basis: it explicitly states it "is unable to provide private tours or talks for schools and groups," so a school's weekday visit is organised only to the extent that any visitor's is, through the daily public Keeper Talks and the online self-guided tour, both available to a booked-in-advance school group as they would be to any visitor. royal-albatross-centre-otago-peninsula-t.activities_verbatim: - "Engage with experts" - "from fortification to conservation" (Toroa at Taiaroa) - "conservation status" and "current environmental issues impacting the seabirds and potential solutions" (Save Our Seabirds) - "investigate the impact of marine debris on the local wildlife" (Litter Free Oceans) - "investigate behaviour of shags and albatross in response to their external environment" (Seabird Behaviour) - "investigate the impact of introduced species, changed vegetation, tourism, site development, pollution etc." (Human Impact) - "activities which illustrate the monitoring and protection methods" including weighing birds, trapping predators, and assessing hazards (Conservation Management)

royal-albatross-centre-otago-peninsula-t.facilities: guided tours (Unique Taiaroa, Albatross Classic, Fort Taiaroa); Fort Taiaroa European Fortification with disappearing gun; gift shop and online merchandise; Toroa Café; live webcam ("Royal Cam") streaming 24/7 from nest sites; galleries; accessible bathrooms; observatory.
royal-albatross-centre-otago-peninsula-t.accessibility_provision: "Access into the Royal Albatross Centre is free of charge, with galleries, a giftshop, café and accessible bathrooms." Self-driven mobility carts for accessing the observatory via a steep paved pathway, advance notice required. sanctuary-mountain-maungatautari.md.activities_verbatim: - "Come to the sanctuary and learn! We plan our conservation education programme in collaboration with teachers to meet local curriculum needs." - "This experience could include, but is not limited to, any of the following: The key conservation challenges facing New Zealand's wildlife and the technologies Sanctuary Mountain is using to protect them." - "Encountering rare and endangered New Zealand species in their natural forest habitat. Examples include pītoitoi/North Island robins, kākā, tūī, korimako/bellbirds, hihi, tīeke/saddlebacks, pīwakawaka/fantails, pōpokotea/whiteheads, kererū and wētā." - "Visiting the Tautari wetland and potentially seeing takahē and tuatara while learning about the importance of this habitat." - "Building on knowledge about New Zealand's unique biodiversity, the adaptations of our flora, fauna and fungi and the interconnectedness of ecosystems." - "Learning about how native species as well as introduced pests are monitored and managed in a sanctuary environment. Some hands-on activities include interpreting tracking tunnels and reading bird bands." - "Discovering the rich history of a community-led conservation project that is New Zealand's largest fenced sanctuary." - "Mātauranga Māori and the significance of the maunga for Mana Whenua." - "Identifying how to take action to help care for our native species and environments that are also important for our own wellbeing." - "Bring your ākonga along to see the maunga in a totally different light. What do glowworms, wētā and batman have in common? Yes, you're more likely to see them when it's dark! We are now offering educational night walks." (Night Walk Education) - "Bringing the sanctuary to the world in our virtual classroom! Sanctuary Mountain® Maungatautari would love to bring conservation to your classroom through a virtual online learning session. It's the next best thing to a visit!" (Virtual Education) - "Spend the night in our Education Centre to extend your time on the maunga and immerse yourself in the environment. Have you visited the maunga before and not wanted to leave? Well with this option you don't have to (for a bit longer anyway)." (Education Centre Overnight)

sarina-sugar-shed.md.programme_names: "School tours"; the underlying tour taken is named "Sugar Shed Tour" elsewhere on the site
sarina-sugar-shed.md.activities_verbatim: "Sarina Sugar Shed provides educational and informative tours ideally suited to school students from primary to secondary age." "Tour the facility where students will be excited to see the processes involved in producing sugar from sugar cane." "Students will have the opportunity to taste fairy floss and ginger beer." "If the tour is fully booked (20 or more participants) by a school, then the tour guide can personalise the tour for the age of the students attending." The Sugar Shed Tour page describes the underlying tour content in full: "This one-hour guided interpretative tour takes you on an interactive journey through the sugar cane growing and crushing process, from getting an up-close view of sugar cane in our own patch to tastings of products made with sugar that are produced onsite. We offer the only such tour in Australia." "During the tour, we will share a brief background of the history of sugar cane farming in the region and explain how sugar cane is grown and harvested. Then it's into our own miniature mill area where we show the same crushing process that the operating mills use, featuring a variety of demonstrative aids. The tour includes the various tastes of sugar cane production, such as freshly-crushed juice, molasses and maybe even a nibble of the cane stalk itself." "The whole paddock-to-bottle sugar journey is completed with tastings of our liqueur products, our chutneys, relishes and sauces, our non-alcoholic ginger beer, and our freshly-spun fairy floss." "Please note, this is an interpretative tour explained through a replica non-operating miniature sugar cane mill in our sheds. The Sarina Sugar Shed is not associated with the Wilmar Plane Creek Mill located behind us, and tours do not operate through the Plane Creek Mill."

sea-world.md.programme_names: "Stayin' Alive" (Prep, Year 1); "Dive into the Past" (Year 2); "Let's Get Sorted" (Year 3, Year 7); "From Little Things, Big Things Grow" (Year 4, Year 6); "The Hunger Games" (Year 4, Year 7); "Antarctic Adventure" (Year 5, Year 6); "Ever Changing Environments" (Year 5, Year 10, Years 11 & 12); "Bear Essentials" (Year 8, Year 9); "Marine Investigators" (Year 9, Year 10, Years 11 & 12); "Reef Romance" (Year 9); "How to Train a Seal" (Year 10, Years 11 & 12, Vocational); "Go with the Flow" (Years 11 & 12); "What's in the Water" (Years 11 & 12); "Paws, Claws and Roars" (All years); "Environmental Issues" (All years); "Getting Smart About Sharks" (All years); "In Depth with Dolphins" (All years); "The Real Deal with Seals" (All years); "Currents and Creatures" (All years); "Marine Wildlife First Aid" (Primary and Secondary, run by the Sea World Foundation); "SharkSmart" (a free self-guided education trail at Shark Bay, not tied to a year level); "Tropical Reef Snorkel" (an add-on, 14 years and over, participation criteria apply, priced separately from the core \$80.00 Educational Program fee)
sea-world.md.activities_verbatim: "During this full day program, students will investigate the basic needs of plants and animals for their survival, and the effects of seasonal change and human impact on their habitats." (It's Alive and I Know Why / Stayin' Alive family, Prep-level framing on the shared page); "During this program students will focus on either Dolphins or Sharks for an up-close encounter to identify the external features of the chosen animal!" (Stayin' Alive, Year 1); "Year 2 students will Dive into the Past of Sea World Marine Park to assist in developing their knowledge and understanding of patterns of observation and connections to history...Through observations and interactions with a range of the objects, animals, technologies and scientific activities at Sea World's Shark Bay Exhibit, students will review the past vs the present." (Dive into the Past); "In this program, students will be introduced to the diversity of life in the ocean to assist them in developing their knowledge and understanding of classification. Through observations and interactions with the amazing animals found at Sea Worlds Shark Bay exhibit, students will review what makes something living or non-living." (Let's Get Sorted); "During this program, students will gain an understanding of the variety of ways offspring are born (such as eggs and live young). Using sharks as a focus animal, students will compare life cycles in different species." (From Little Things, Big Things Grow); "Year 4 students will observe the inhabitants of Shark Bay to determine their interconnectedness with each other and their environment and how humans are interlinked to all life in marine ecosystems. Students will construct food chains." (The Hunger Games, Year 4); "During this program, students will observe two species of Antarctic Penguins to learn how animals' bodies are equipped to suit the conditions of their environment." (Antarctic Adventure); "This program allows students to consolidate their understanding of climate change with a focus on how it is affecting the survival of Polar Bears." (Ever Changing Environments, Year 10 framing); "During this program, students will learn how reef ecosystems consist of communities of interdependent organisms...in Shark Bay's underwater viewing gallery." (Marine Investigators); "Students will explore the reproductive strategies of a range of marine animals, including sharks and rays, and investigate how these strategies are adapted to the challenges of life in the ocean." (Reef Romance); "This program enables students to gain a firsthand understanding of how Sea World's animals are cared for. Students will get an in-depth look at the care and management of seals and sea lions." (How to Train a Seal); "This interactive program provides a unique behind-the-scenes look into the mesmerizing world of Sea Jellies at Sea World." (Go with the Flow); "Students will use technical equipment to identify, measure and compare water quality parameters in a closed aquarium setting and an open, natural system." (What's in the Water); "This interactive program provides a broad overview of polar bear biology and ecology for students of all ages." (Paws, Claws and Roars); "This program introduces students to the numerous ways humans are interconnected to the oceans and their inhabitants...how fishing activities, spark nets, marine debris and pollution are collectively contributing to loss of biodiversity." (Environmental Issues); "During this interactive program, students of all ages will learn about the amazing biology and ecology of sharks!" (Getting Smart About Sharks); "This interactive program provides a broad overview of dolphin biology and ecology for students of all ages." (In Depth with Dolphins); "During this interactive program, students of all ages will learn about the fascinating biology and ecology of seals." (The Real Deal with Seals); "Step into the glowing world of sea jellies and uncover the science behind one of the ocean's most misunderstood creatures." (Currents and Creatures); "During this interactive program students are introduced to the marine wildlife species commonly found in Australia [and] the threats they face that can result in marine wildlife incidents. Students will be equipped with tools and information to contact the relevant rescue organisations and provide first aid for a marine animal in distress." (Marine Wildlife First Aid); "Learn how to be SharkSmart in our interactive education trail at Sea World! Proudly supported by the QLD Government, students will learn about shark species and biology, fascinating facts about sharks, how to be SharkSmart in the water and new technology being used in Queensland to monitor sharks and keep people safe." (SharkSmart)
sea-world.md.duration: none listed in hours or minutes on the pages read. The booking form states only that "Educational Programs have pre-scheduled arrival times" and that "Education program times are unable to be adjusted. All education programs run to a fixed schedule to align with park operations and daily schedules," directing enquirers to a separate program-times page (themeparks.com.au/education/program-times) that falls outside the four pages read.
sea-world.md.group_size_min_max: "Minimum of 10 students per school group booking is required" for general admission. For the Educational Program itself, the booking form states only that "minimum and maximum participants apply" without giving the numbers.
sea-world.md.participant_thresholds: "We do not have a specified teacher-to-student ratio for excursions, however we recommend no more than 20 students per teacher." The \$80.00 Educational Program fee is "charged per session, not per student"; "Selected programs incur a per student fee of \$13.00 or an additional fee for the Tropical Reef Snorkel" (\$40.00, 14 years and over, "participation criteria applies"). ## Inventory
sea-world.md.facilities: Shark Bay (named as the setting for multiple programs, including an "underwater viewing gallery" and a "Tropical Reef Lagoon"); a general-attractions page names Leviathan (Thrill Level - Max, thrill ride), Trident (Thrill Level - Mild, family ride), Vortex (Thrill Level - Max, thrill ride), the ONE Dolphin Presentation, the Thunder Lake Stunt Show (listed as in its "Final Days - Ends 31st Aug"), and The New Atlantis (Thrill Level - Moderate, outdoor precinct), out of a stated "34" total attractions of which only these six had loaded on the page read; lockers are available for hire "with costs ranging from \$15 to \$25 for a large size locker" (FAQ)
sea-world.md.equipment_provided: none listed as general equipment; the Year 11 & 12 Marine Investigator Program offers an option to have "quadrats and a transect set up in the Tropical Reef Lagoon for a more-in-depth survey during your snorkel," requiring set-up prior to arrival
sea-world.md.staff_qualifications_stated: none listed by title or credential; programs are described as delivered by "our team" and, for the Marine Investigators and How to Train a Seal programs, framed around exposure to Sea World's own animal-care staff practice
sea-world.md.accessibility_provision: "Accessible and private changing facilities are available. Please contact our Education Team prior to your visit to discuss your needs and ensure the appropriate facilities are reserved." A separate Accessibility page exists in the site's main navigation but falls outside the fixed four-page set for this research pass.
sea-world.md.animal_species_held: dolphins, sharks and rays, seals and sea lions, polar bears, Antarctic penguins ("two species"), sea jellies, and reef animals generally (named across the program descriptions read); the attractions page adds no further species beyond the ride and presentation list ## Curriculum
sea-world.md.curriculum_links: "Our Australian Curriculum aligned educational programs are available for each year level." Several programs carry a "Version 9" tag (aligned to Australian Curriculum Version 9.0) and others carry a "QCAA" or dated "QCAA 2024"/"QCAA 2025" tag, indicating alignment to the Queensland Curriculum and Assessment Authority syllabus for that subject.
sea-world.md.teacher_materials: "Yes. Curriculum-aligned worksheets and learning resources are available for our Sea World programs. These will be provided on arrival, depending on your program." A "Pre-Visit Questionnaire" is provided as part of the booking form, asking teachers to state the unit of study, where the excursion sits within it, whether it links to an assessment task ("Yes. Please attach the task sheet" / "No"), any request for specific inclusions, and any student requirements such as "ESL or special needs." ## Trust
sea-world.md.risk_assessment_available: none listed on the pages read
sea-world.md.child_safety_checks_stated: none listed; the only identification requirement stated is that "Bona-fide Teachers/PWD Carers are eligible for free of charge park admission upon presentation of relevant school, OSHC or carer identification," which is an admission-eligibility check, not a child-safety credential
sea-world.md.accreditations_displayed: "Sea World is proudly positive animal welfare accredited by the Zoo and Aquarium Association Australasia." (attractions page) ## Commercial
sea-world.md.price_and_structure: Education admission: Prep & Primary Students \$30.50; Prep & Primary Accompanying Adults \$30.50; Prep & Primary Teachers \$0.00; Secondary Students \$42.00; Secondary Accompanying Adults \$42.00; Secondary Teachers \$0.00; Tertiary Students \$45.00 ("Requires Participation in Education Program"); Persons With Disabilities Groups \$29.50; Persons With Disabilities Carers \$0.00. Educational Program: \$80.00 "per program," "charged per session, not per student," with "Selected programs" also incurring "a per student fee of \$13.00" or the separate Tropical Reef Snorkel fee of \$40.00 (14 years and over). A flat Booking Fee of \$6.00 "applies to all bookings." Rates are stated as "valid 19 December 2025 - 18 December 2026."
sea-world.md.adults_free_ratio: Teachers attend free of charge ("Prep & Primary Teachers \$0.00"; "Secondary Teachers \$0.00"), as do "Bona-fide...PWD Carers," but no numeric ratio of free teachers per student group is stated; "Accompanying Adults" who are not teachers are charged the same rate as students in their age band (\$30.50 Prep & Primary, \$42.00 Secondary).
sea-world.md.catering: Prepaid meal vouchers: Maxi Meal Voucher \$20.00 ("Choose from Beef Burger, Chicken Burger, Chicken Nuggets, Veggie Burger...served with chips and regular soft drink or Mt Franklin Water," or a pizza-slice option, pickup at "Plaza Prime Burgers or Pizza Shack"); Ultimate Triple Treat Deal \$29.00 (burger meal, bottomless-refill drink, ice cream, pickup at "Plaza Prime Burgers"); Sandwich Pack \$16.00 (choice of fillings plus "Mini fruit salad and a Mini Muffin," a water or juice popper, vegetarian option available on request, pickup at "Fresh Focus"); Mini Meal Voucher \$15.00 (cheeseburger or kids' chicken nuggets, chips, small soft drink or water, pickup at "Plaza Prime Burgers"); Single Serve Ice-Cream Voucher \$6.50. "All meal vouchers require minimum 48 hours notice of cancellation or full cost incurred."
sea-world.md.cancellation_and_weather: "Cancellation Fees apply within 72 Hours of scheduled program" for the Educational Program component. Meal vouchers separately "require minimum 48 hours notice of cancellation or full cost incurred." No weather-specific policy is stated on the pages read.
sea-world.md.booking_lead_time: "All orders must be received a minimum of five business days in advance" (ticket order). "Educational Programs are only available during Queensland School Terms, excluding weekends and public holidays." ## Conversion
sea-world.md.how_to_book: "Simply click on your location, download the form, and email your completed form to education@vrtp.com.au" (schools page). The Sea World-specific completed booking form, with the Pre-Visit Questionnaire attached, is emailed to the same address. "For further information, please phone our School Excursions & Education Department. Phone: 07 5519 6210. Email: education@vrtp.com.au." The schools page also carries an "Enquire Now" contact form and states "contact us on 07 5519 6210 to plan your next excursion."
sea-world.md.price_visible_without_asking: yes. The full education admission schedule, the \$80.00 Educational Program fee, the \$13.00 per-student add-on for selected programs, the \$40.00 Tropical Reef Snorkel fee and the \$6.00 booking fee are all published on the freely downloadable 2026 booking form, with no login or quote request required.
sea-world.md.downloadable_pack: the Sea World Education Booking Form 2026 (four pages: booking-details cover sheet, ticket and meal order, educational program selection, and pre-visit questionnaire) is freely downloadable from the schools page without registration; a separate "Booking Form" is likewise downloadable for each of the other Village Roadshow Theme Parks.
sea-world.md.testimonials_from_schools: none listed on the pages read
sea-world.md.title_and_opening_line: Title: "School Excursions & Programs" (themeparks.com.au/education, the shared schools page); the Sea World-specific booking form is separately titled "School Excursions & Educational Programs 2026 Booking Form." Opening line (shared schools page): "Searching for your next school excursion, hands-on learning experience, or end-of-year celebration? Bring the curriculum to life in the ultimate immersive learning experience at Australia's best theme parks!" Opening line (Sea World booking form): "Sea World Education rates are available to Australian Domestic and Secondary Schools as well as pre-approved Outside of School Hours Care providers." ## Note Several Sea World education programs carry titles borrowed from film franchises with no continuity to their content ("The Hunger Games" at Year 4 and Year 7 is, per its own description, a Shark Bay food-web and marine-ecosystem session with no stated connection to the film beyond the name). This is reported as published, not corrected. Two FAQ answers on the shared schools page bear directly on scope for a comparator business: "Are Home School groups eligible for Education rates? Yes, home school groups are eligible to receive education rates, provided registration is supplied for each child attending. Please note, Teacher Free of Charge tickets do not apply to home school bookings," and, on tailoring, "Education programs at Sea World are unable to be tailored to specific tasks or assessments, however our team are more than happy to answer additional questions for inclusion" — a more restrictive tailoring stance than Warner Bros. Movie World's, which is stated on the same page as open to tailoring requests "considered" case by case.

splitters-farm.md.programme_names: "School Camps & Educational Programs at Splitters Farm"; "Vacation Care Farm Tours"; "Half-Day School Farm Experience"; "Overnight Camping for Students"; the School Camp Options pack additionally gives suggested itineraries titled "2 Day / 1 night Camp" and "5 Day / 4 night Camp"
splitters-farm.md.activities_verbatim: "At Splitters Farm, we believe not all classrooms have four walls. Our farm provides an immersive, hands-on learning environment where students of all ages can connect with nature, understand where their food comes from, and experience sustainable farming practices firsthand." Topics offered: "Paddock rotation and livestock management"; "The importance of pollination and native bees"; "Organic farming and healthy soil practices"; "Composting and waste management"; "Crop cultivation and seasonal produce"; "Ethical and sustainable farming methods." Vacation Care Farm Tours: "Students can collect eggs, feed animals, and interact with farm babies, all under the guidance of our experienced staff." Half-Day School Farm Experience: "Guided farm tours with our farmers"; "Meeting the livestock and learning animal care"; "Visits to the orchard and market garden"; "Discussion time on sustainable farming and ethical practices"; "A BBQ lunch to finish the day." Overnight Camping for Students: "Learn campfire skills and cook damper"; "Participate in star gazing and evening farm activities such as cinema under the stars"; "Take part in farm tours and educational programs"; "Work in teams to race kayaks across the creek." The School Camp Options pack's "2 Day / 1 night Camp" suggested itinerary reads, verbatim in full: "DAY ONE 9am arrival at Splitters Farm; 9am – 9:15am - Safety Briefing and Welcome to Splitters Farm; 9:15am – 10am – Tents will be set up prior to arrival – Students to set up bedding/pillows etc; 10am – 10:30am – Morning Tea – provided by Splitters Farm – students split into 3 groups with corresponding wristbands; 10:30am – 12noon – Rotational Activities x 30 students each group (1. Guided Tour / 2. Kayaking / 3. Go Karts & Paddle Boats); 12noon – 12:45pm - Sausage sizzle Lunch & Free time – provided by Splitters Farm; 12:45pm – 2pm - Rotational Activities x 30 students each group (1. Guided Tour / 2. Kayaking / 3. Go Karts & Paddle Boats); 2pm 2:30pm – Fruit & Water Break – provided by Splitters Farm; 2:30pm – 3:30pm - Damper Making Group 1 -kids split into 2 groups. Damper teams of 2 will cook one damper between 2 students / Other students have free time to swim / fish etc; 3:30pm – 4:30pm - Damper Making Group 2 -kids split into teams of 2 and cook one damper between 2 students / Other students have free time to swim / fish etc; 4:30pm – 6pm Showers & Free time (5min each); 6pm – Dinner – Nacho Bowls – To be provided by Splitters Farm; 6:30pm – Cinema Under the stars (movie list to be provided) Please bring a rug/towel or camp chair to sit on; 9pm – Lights Out. DAY TWO 7am – Breakfast – Mixed Cereals/Milk – provided by Splitters Farm; 8am – 9:30am - Rotational Activities x 30 students each group - (1. Guided Tour / 2. Kayaking / 3. Go Karts & Paddle Boats); 9:30am – 10:30am Morning Tea – Provided By Splitters Farm; 10:30am – Self-guided Farm Access / pack up bedding etc in tents ready for bus; 11:30am – Lunch – Provided by Splitters Farm – sandwiches and/or wraps; 12noon – Board Buses and depart Farm." No equivalent timed detail is given beneath the "5 Day / 4 night Camp" heading in the same pack.
splitters-farm.md.duration: Half-Day School Farm Experience is described only by its name, no clock hours given beyond "half-day"; Vacation Care Farm Tours state no duration ("Tours can be tailored to your school holiday or vacation care program"); Overnight Camping for Students is offered as a "2 Day / 1 night Camp" (per the timed itinerary above) and a "5 Day / 4 night Camp" (heading only, no published detail)

splitters-farm.md.catering: "Meals are prepared by our food safety-qualified staff with all dietary needs catered for"; the venue states it caters to "Gluten-free, dairy-free, and vegetarian options", "Respect for religious dietary requirements" and "Consideration for animal welfare-conscious meals." The School Camp Menu PDF lists full breakfast, lunch, dinner, morning/afternoon tea and supper menus, each item coded for dietary alternatives (GF/DF/LF/VEG/V/H), whether it is a takeaway option for off-site activities, whether it suits groups over 50 students, and a budget scale of \$/\$\$/\$\$\$; items marked with an asterisk carry the note "*Not Suitable for Egg / Nut or seed allergies."
splitters-farm.md.cancellation_and_weather: from the Booking Terms & Conditions PDF's "School Camps Payments" section: "Once a school has accepted a written quote, a non-refundable 50% deposit is due to confirm the dates based on min numbers agreed"; "6 weeks prior to the arrival date, schools must confirm the following: Number of Students / Teachers; Dietary needs & allergies; Bedding configurations (if required); Any students with special needs"; "Final invoices are issued and payable 30 days prior to arrival based on the information provided above. Where there is a credit due to a decrease in numbers, the credit is held until the end of the school camp and can be refunded"; "School Camps that are cancelled are not eligible for a refund however bookings can be placed into credit for future dates agreed by both parties." No school-camp-specific weather clause is stated; the general (accommodation-wide) clause reads: "Weather Cancellations: If you or your group do not wish to travel due to extreme weather events (proof of said event must be evident and recognised by the BOM) you will need to contact us immediately to discuss. A change booking fee will be applied and may be credited for a period a 1-year from the date of the cancellation." The general Events/Tour Refunds section adds: "Guided and Self-Guided Farm Access Tour bookings are not refundable however can be changed to an alternate date."
splitters-farm.md.booking_lead_time: no minimum lead time is stated for school camps specifically, beyond the 6-week-prior confirmation and 30-day-prior final-invoice deadlines quoted above; the general accommodation terms state "Splitters Farm only take bookings 12-18 months in advance." ## Conversion

General day-tour and camping bookings elsewhere on the site route through "Book now!" links to FareHarbor (fareharbor.com/embeds/book/splittersfarm) and a Newbook accommodation portal (bookingsau.newbook.cloud/splittersfarm), but the schools page itself directs teachers to email or phone rather than to either online booking system.

stepney-city-farm.md.programme_names: Guided tours; Workshops; Self-led visits; Farm to Fork: Food Systems; Plants, food growing & gardening; Habitats: Homes for Plants and Animals; Introduction to Farm Animals; Life Cycle of a Chicken; Animal Teeth & Feed; Our Pollinator Trail
stepney-city-farm.md.activities_verbatim: - Guided tours — "A guided tour is a great chance to find out more about the farm. We will show you around, introduce the students to the plants and animals, answer questions and feed the animals." - Workshops — "We offer a range of workshops for schools visiting the farm including sessions looking at animals, plants and the environment." - Self-led visits — "Self-led visits are possible Monday-Friday, but must be booked in advance. We will provide you with a map of the farm and information about the animals and plants." - Farm to Fork: Food Systems — "Understanding that all food comes from a plant or an animal, and that fruit and vegetables grow in the ground. Understanding that food is imported from all around the world as well as growing here." (Session Information PDF) - Plants, food growing & gardening — "Understanding what plants need to grow, and that we eat different parts of the plant. Practical experience of a seasonal gardening activity." (Session Information PDF) - Habitats: Homes for Plants and Animals — "Understanding the food chains and feeding relationships within habitats on the farm, how nearly all food chains start with a green plant, and how creatures are adapted to their environment." (Session Information PDF) - Introduction to Farm Animals — "Understanding which animals live on the Farm, and what they need to stay healthy." (Session Information PDF) - Life Cycle of a Chicken — "An understanding of a chicken's needs, the different stages in their life cycle and the differences between males and females." (Session Information PDF) - Animal Teeth & Feed — "Understanding the diets of different animals & how this impacts on what kind of teeth we all have." (Session Information PDF) - Our Pollinator Trail — "While you're here, look out for our Pollinator Trail. There are six stops, marked on the map."

Our education programs can be modified to complement your current classroom learning and are suitable for primary and secondary students." ## Note The attractions page states general admission is "Free Admission", with tours, rides, and activities individually priced or bundled, including for school groups. Across all four sources and the linked school packages document, the venue publishes no activity resembling animal feed making, meaning children following a recipe to mix or make feed and then feeding it to an animal. It contains no reference to hand feeding, mixing, or preparing feed. The venue's other named "making" activity, "DYO Gingerbread Person" ("Decorate your own gingerbread person. Includes icing & lollies. Take home or enjoy at The Ginger Factory"), is a human-food decorating activity, not animal feed making, and is noted here only to rule it out. thunderbird-park.md.title_and_opening_line: No school-specific page exists to title. The nearest page, "Groups", opens: "Unforgettable Events for Every Group" / "Whether you're planning a high-energy team building day, a milestone birthday bash, or a professional conference with a difference, Thunderbird Park offers the perfect blend of nature, adventure, and hospitality." ## Note Thunderbird Park is an adventure and events park (ziplines, treetop ropes courses, mini excavators, gemstone fossicking, mini golf, pickleball, laser skirmish, waterfall walk) with one small nature activity, the free daily bird feeding session, rather than a farm or animal-education venue. Its own site navigation has no schools, education, or excursions section; the "Groups & Events" section is built entirely around team building, birthday parties and conferences. "School holidays" appears repeatedly on the site but always refers to the school-holiday calendar period for family/leisure visitors, not a school-group education booking. On the specific research question of animal feed making: the only animal feeding activity published is "Bird Feeding", and the page is explicit that the park, not the visitor, prepares the feed: "At Thunderbird Park, we feed them a special nectar mix that keeps them healthy and strong!" The page further warns "Giving them the wrong food, like bread or seeds, can hurt their beaks and make them sick", framing feed composition as something staff control rather than something visitors, let alone schoolchildren, mix or make. Visitors watch and get "up close" while "guided by our friendly and experienced staff" as the birds feed; no wording anywhere on the pages read describes children following a recipe or mixing ingredients to prepare the feed. Nothing resembling animal feed making is published.

tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.programme_names: Primary and Intermediate School (Up to Y8); Secondary School (Y9-13); Growing Minds; Nature of Science and Living World syllabus programme (primary/intermediate); focused secondary units: "Pest-Free Tiritiri Matangi", "Genetic Variation and Change", "The Use of Open Sanctuaries"
tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.activities_verbatim: - Guided walk through native forest - Close-up wildlife encounters with birdlife - Lunch break - Student-led activities (younger students) - Targeted learning session (senior students)
tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.duration: Full day structure: morning guided walk, lunch break, afternoon student-led activities or targeted learning session. No clock-time durations stated.
tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.group_size_min_max: Y3-4: maximum 55 students. Y5-13: maximum 65 students. First-time visits: maximum 50 students. Minimum adult-to-student ratio for the guided walk: 1:8.
tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.participant_thresholds: Guided walk minimum ratio 1 adult to 8 students; Y3-4 group maximum 55 students; Y5-13 group maximum 65 students; first-time visiting groups maximum 50 students; Growing Minds funded visits up to 85 students per school visit (per Growing Minds programme, EQI 430+ schools). ## Inventory
tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.facilities: Former lighthouse keeper's cottage with 15 bunks across three rooms, cooking and bathroom facilities; small shop for souvenirs; no food sales on island; New Zealand's third-ever built lighthouse, still operating.
tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.staff_qualifications_stated: "Our educators have an in-depth understanding of the science curriculum and are able to offer a range of educational experiences on the island that are closely tied to the syllabus." Island guides identify wildlife, birdsong, and give insight into conservation work.
tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.animal_species_held: Tīeke (North Island Saddleback), Hihi (stitchbird), Takahē, Kōkako, tuatara, Duvaucel's geckos, shore skinks, wētāpunga (giant wētā), bellbirds, tui, kiwi. Over 31 native bird species overall stated. ## Curriculum
tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.curriculum_links: Primary/Intermediate: Nature of Science and Living World syllabus, aligned with the New Zealand Science Curriculum. Secondary (Y11-13): Levels 1-3 NCEA (National Certificate of Educational Achievement Standards), the International Baccalaureate Curriculum, and Cambridge International New Zealand. Named NCEA achievement standards by year: Year 11 - AS90951 (Pest Free Tiritiri), AS91009 (Sustainability Tiritiri); Year 12 - AS91157 (Population Genetics), AS91158 (Between The Tides & Biodiversity/Seed Dispersers/Succession); Year 13 - AS91602 (Open Sanctuary), AS91603 (Responses to Environment), AS91605 (Speciation).
tiritiri-matangi-open-sanctuary.md.teacher_materials: Teacher Planning Guide (downloadable PDF); Day Programme (downloadable PDF); School Visit Information (downloadable PDF); Tiritiri Matangi Map; Bio Security Flyer; RAMs document; Animal List; pre-visit video (Primary/Intermediate); Tiritiri Matangi student activities resource; Scavenger Hunt: Rainy Day lunchtime activity (student and teacher versions); four downloadable worksheets for the ferry journey/lunch breaks; Year 11-13 student worksheets by NCEA achievement standard (listed under curriculum_links). ## Trust

tokes-farm-education.md.school_offer_detail_level: timed_programme The site carries a dedicated "Schools/Teachers" menu section with four sub-pages: Day Visit, Weekly Visits, Residentials, SEN & SEMH. The Day Visit page publishes a full timed running order.
tokes-farm-education.md.programme_names: "Day Visit"; "A day at the Farm"; "Weekly Visits"; "A Year on the Farm"; "Residentials"; "SEN, SEMH & AP"
tokes-farm-education.md.activities_verbatim: , Day Visit page (typical "A day at the Farm" programme, described in prose, not itemised as a bullet list):** "feeding the animals, milking the goats, working in the market or kitchen garden, helping to prepare lunch, heading into the woods, or joining in with seasonal jobs around the farm, such as harvesting hazel, planting hedges or chopping wood" Curriculum topic-led day description: "starts with a short tour around the farm followed by the chosen learning content delivered in 45-minute slots" Worked examples given on the same page: "A day with Year 3 who learnt about Roman numerals by making large sundials enabling them to tell the time using both."; "A day with Year 6 saw them exploring area and perimeter through a series of tasks and challenges based in different fields around the farm."; "A morning with Year 4 was spent in the woods to awaken the children's senses, as well as to deepen their skills in descriptive writing and story work. They spent the afternoon telling stories out loud."; "Year 1 - 6 as well as secondary school groups who came for a day at the farm enriched their scientific knowledge by identifying plants and animals, discovering the life cycles of these plants and animals, delving into different habitats and observing simple food chains as well as all important water cycles." Residentials page: "The children can take part in a range of farming, cooking and forest school activities led by their own teachers or us." Holiday sessions page (not school-specific, but on the same site): "activity days and courses ... blacksmithing, creative arts, woodwork, animal husbandry and growing vegetables"
tokes-farm-education.md.duration: Day Visit: a full school day, per the timed table below. Weekly Visits: "Coming to the farm once a week during term time." Residentials: "One-night, two-night or three-night residentials." Curriculum-topic teaching sessions are stated as "45-minute slots."
tokes-farm-education.md.participant_thresholds: none listed **Example Timings of a day visit** (Day Visit page, verbatim, with the venue's own caveat: "Timings will vary due to schools individual timetables"): | Time | Activity | |---|---| | 9.30am - 10am | Arrival and Welcome | | 9.50am - 10am | Health and Safety talk | | 10am - 11am | teaching session 1 in the amphitheatre | | 11am - 11.30am | Snack and play | | 11.30am - 12.15pm | Teaching session 2 | | 12.15pm - 1pm | Teaching session 3 | | 1pm - 1.30pm | Lunch and play | | 1.30pm - 2.15pm | Teaching session 4 | | 2.15pm - 2.30pm | End of day session in the amphitheatre | | 2.30pm - 3pm | Goodbye | (Note: the 9.30-10am and 9.50-10am rows overlap exactly as published on the source page; transcribed as given.) ## Inventory
tokes-farm-education.md.facilities: From The Farm page: "86 acres of organic pasture", "a strip of ancient woodland", "timber-framed school house ... a multi functional meeting space. Here we warm up around the wood burner on wet, grey winter days, hold lessons when we can't be outside, run cookery, arts and crafts classes and more", "market garden and kitchen garden – suitably sited with wheelchair access next to our school house." Day Visit page also references "the amphitheatre" as a teaching space used at the start and end of the day.
tokes-farm-education.md.staff_qualifications_stated: The Team page: Lily McClleland is "A qualified Steiner Waldorf Teacher, specialising in teaching, 7-to-14 year olds" who "also holds a fine art degree from Brighton Art College" and was "a class teacher for seven years at the Steiner Academy in Frome." Bryony Gardiner "trained as a Primary School Teacher in central London, and has been plying her trade for over six years," is "a Forest School Leader, and head of Key Stage 1 Music and English." Emily Hudson (Visiting Teacher) has taught "in mainstream, Steiner and forest schools." The SEN & SEMH page states: "All the staff that will be working with groups at Tokes Farm have experience of working with children and young adults with varying additional needs."
tokes-farm-education.md.accessibility_provision: The Farm page states the market garden and kitchen garden are "suitably sited with wheelchair access next to our school house." No other accessibility provision is stated.
tokes-farm-education.md.animal_species_held: The Farm page: cattle ("We rear organic calves before moving them to join the milking herd on our partner farm"); sheep ("Our flock of sheep headed up by Fleur, our eldest ewe, are a mixture of native Dorset Down and Jacobs. We recently added two Black Welsh Mountains for diversity and interest"); goats ("Our latest addition are Patti and Pan, two wonderful goats"); hens and a cockerel ("Our hens provide us with delicious eggs while Boris the cockerel wakes us up at dawn"). The Day Visit page also references "milking the goats" as an activity. ## Curriculum
tokes-farm-education.md.curriculum_links: Weekly Visits page: "The blocks can be organised as 'A Year on the Farm', focusing on seasonal farming activities or driven by a specific curriculum topic such as Science, Geography, Maths or English." Day Visit page gives the same structure ("a day driven by a specific curriculum topic") and the worked examples above cite Roman numerals, area and perimeter, descriptive writing, plant/animal life cycles, habitats, food chains and water cycles as content actually delivered, without naming a specific national curriculum stage document.
tokes-farm-education.md.teacher_materials: Day Visit and Weekly Visits pages both state: "Programme and lesson plans can be created by Tokes Farm staff or a combination of Tokes Farm staff and the class teacher." No downloadable lesson-plan pack was found; the only downloadable document found on the site is the registration/permission form (see Trust, below). ## Trust
tokes-farm-education.md.risk_assessment_available: none listed as a public document; the registration form's declaration states "I understand that there is an element of risk and I accept that."
tokes-farm-education.md.child_safety_checks_stated: The SEN & SEMH page states: "Our safeguarding policy will always be accessible on request, whether digitally or in physical form at the farm." tokes-farm-education.md.accreditations_displayed: The Farm page states: "The farm is home to a range of livestock and is 100% organic." No formal visitor-safety or education-sector accreditation (e.g. LOtC Quality Badge, CEVAS) is stated on any page read. ## Commercial
