tommerups-dairy-farm.md.programme_names: the page is titled "Farm School"; the FAQ refers throughout to "the Farm School program" and "Farm School visits"; no further discrete programme titles (for example a separate kindy or vacation-care programme name) are given, though the FAQ confirms the same programme is offered in modified form to vacation care groups: "We offer the Farm School program in school holidays for vacation and outside hours school care groups."
tommerups-dairy-farm.md.activities_verbatim: "Your school group visit can be as simple as immersing your students into a real working farm environment where they'll see our cows being milked, explore sustainable production of vegetables, grain, dairy, eggs and meat, and get up close to our menagerie of farm animals, right through to the full farm to fork supply chain or business case study for secondary subjects."; "We have chickens, ducks, sheep, goats, calves, pigs and cows on the farm. Whilst we may not get to feed all the animals during the visit, the children are able to feed and pat farm animals as part of the experience on the farm."; "Visits to the dairy include watching some of our Jersey Girls being milked. For safety reasons and the welfare of our cows, children don't have the opportunity to milk the cows but will see the whole process in our 100 year old dairy."; "The farm is a learning environment where students can see the processes of growing, harvesting, and rearing, to the processing and packaging stages, right through to marketing, sales and distribution at the farm shop and beyond."; "hands-on learning around historical artefacts, changes over the past 6 generations, and the important role history plays in our future"; "Our program facilitates genuine Q&A and natural inquiry processes, assisting with the development of critical and creative thinking as your students gain firsthand knowledge from real farmers and their lived experience."
tommerups-dairy-farm.md.duration: "We encourage school groups to arrive between 10 and 10.30am so the students can have some time to enjoy morning tea in the picnic paddock along with a chance to stretch their legs and use the bathroom after their bus trip. A break for lunch is included, with departure time generally between 1 and 1.30pm."
tommerups-dairy-farm.md.group_size_min_max: "We prefer groups of up to 60 students at one time but will consider higher numbers on a case-by-case basis. We understand the challenges around transport costs and are happy to discuss group sizing to get the best outcome for everyone." No minimum group size is stated.
tommerups-dairy-farm.md.participant_thresholds: the only numeric threshold published is the preferred ceiling of "up to 60 students at one time", offered as a flexible rather than hard limit ("will consider higher numbers on a case-by-case basis"). upper-thames-river-conservation-authorit.activities_verbatim: - "Participants use their senses to gain awareness and appreciation of plants and animals while exploring various natural communities. Games and activities throughout the hike encourage interaction with group members and the environment." (Sensory Nature Hike) - "Participate in a 'choose your own adventure' activity to simulate the Monarch migration, and learn the cardinal directions along with butterfly anatomy and life cycle." (Flap 'n' Map) - "The birds are returning! Gain knowledge by watching them with binoculars and playing games. Let us help you discover and examine other springtime secrets and mysteries!" (Sensational Spring) - "Explore with dip nets at the pond, and hike into the forest. Play a game that lets you pretend to be a dragonfly or damselfly going through their life cycle!" (Pond and Forest) - "Learn what orienteering is and how to use a map and compass, then find your way to a series of locations." (Map & Compass Orienteering) - "This series of games will complement ecological concepts being studied in your group." (Environmental Games) - "Collect and identify creatures in all of these three areas! Discover their adaptations and habitat requirements." (Pond, Field and Forest) - "Discover basic ecological concepts as we explore aquatic and terrestrial communities to identify and classify a variety of plants and animals. Discover how ecosystem health depends on biodiversity and use authentic field work tools including sweep nets to explore habitats." (BIO: Biodiversity and Interactions in Our Local Environment) - "Through exploration, active games, and hands-on activities, our educators inspire students to engage with nature through curiosity, investigation, and discovery." - "Our flexible programming allows us to tailor your visit to what subjects/topics/badges your group is currently working on. Contact us to see how we can help!"

walby-farm-park.md.programme_names: "Educational Packages"; "Numeracy and Literacy activity days"; "Cooking on the Farm"; "Father Christmas on the Farm" (described as a seasonal school visit)
walby-farm-park.md.activities_verbatim: - We can deliver educational visits from KS1 and KS2 to GCSE and A-Level on our mixed working farm. - We offer tailor-made Numeracy and Literacy activity days for KS1 and KS2. - Our Cooking on the Farm package links food and farming and gives students the chance to produce a healthy meal. - All of our packages are developed on the principle of hands-on learning. - We run seasonal school visits such as for 'Father Christmas on the Farm'. - Put your pupils at the heart of our farm where they can meet and feed our animals, encounter the countryside and explore the links between the food they eat and our beautiful surroundings, with our fantastic educational trips. - If the weather's wet then our large indoor adventure play area and undercover Milecastle 62 provide entertainment, as does our dedicated under-5's soft play area for your younger groups. - We can offer CEVAS-trained guides and some exclusive demonstrations to fit in with your requirements for formal or informal teaching.

walby-farm-park.md.participant_thresholds: minimum group size of 15 for educational trips (no stated maximum) ## Inventory
walby-farm-park.md.facilities: Indoor Adventure Play Barn (described elsewhere as "Cumbria's largest Adventure Play Barn"); Milecastle 62 (undercover Adventure Play, built on the line of Hadrian's Wall); dedicated under-5's soft play area; Animal Barn; Animal Paddocks and fields; Nature Trail including Jubilee Wood; The Cowshed Café (has a large-scale farm map on the wall); outdoor play areas.
walby-farm-park.md.staff_qualifications_stated: "We can offer CEVAS-trained guides." Walby Farm Park has been awarded the CEVAS (Countryside Educational Visits Accreditation Scheme) Learning Outside the Classroom Quality Badge.
walby-farm-park.md.accessibility_provision: Access Card Scheme supported, with free Essential Companion tickets for Access Card holders showing +1 or +2 symbols; Digital Access Pass administered by Nimbus Disability available specifically for Walby Farm Park; Assistance Dogs welcomed (other dogs not permitted on site due to close contact with animals); a downloadable Access Statement document is provided (Access-Statement-Walby-Farm-Park-2025-01-FINAL.pdf).
walby-farm-park.md.animal_species_held: alpacas; calves/cows; chickens (Maran Hen pictured); ducks; goats (West African Pygmy Goats pictured); guinea pigs; horses & donkeys (including a named Clydesdale, "Lady Alice"); pigs; rabbits; reindeer; sheep and lambs; Red Deer (seen via seasonal tractor and trailer rides). ## Curriculum

wingham-wildlife-park.md.activities_verbatim: (Talks with our Education Team, "Key Stage 1,2 & 3", in the order listed): - "A bug's life – the one about the lives and life cycles of terrestrial invertebrates." - "African safari – the one about animals' native to Africa." - "Australian species – the one about animals' native to Australia." - "Cold blooded – the one about the lives of reptiles around the world." - "Different teeth for different jobs – the one about how different types of teeth work." - "Dinosaurs, fossils and extinctions – the one about prehistoric animals." - "Evolution of animals – the one about how modern life came about." - "Forests and their inhabitants – the one about non tropical forests & their inhabitants." - "Habitats – the one about the different places animals live." - "Jungles and their inhabitants – the one about tropical rainforests & their inhabitants." - "Life Cycles – The one about different life cycles in nature." - "On the hunt; the circle of life – the one about carnivores and the food chain." (Talks with our Education Team, "Key stage 4-5"): - "Rainforest S.O.S – the one about deforestation and the palm oil debate." - "The role of a zoo – the one about the important role of zoos in conservation, education and welfare." - "Zoo careers – the one about the different roles within a zoo and how to get into them." - "Evolution of animals, including us – the one about how modern life came about including for humans." - "Let's talk about poo, pellets and digestion – the one where we dissect animal waste products." (Educational Workshops for EYFS, Key Stage 1 & 2): - "Animal diets (EYFS, Key stage 1&2) – the one about identifying a species diet from a poo sample! (not real faecal matter used)" - "Weird wildlife (EYFS, Key stage 1&2) – the one about unusual adaptations and you create your very own species!" - "The role of a zoo (EYFS, Key stage 1&2) – the one about the importance of zoos in conservation and you help us create enrichment for our animals. yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.accessibility_provision: none listed on the pages read.
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.animal_species_held: Polar bears; African penguins; golden lion tamarin; sea lions; giraffes (Rothschild); cheetahs; leopards; baboons; titi monkeys; red pandas; capybaras; Lar gibbons. ## Curriculum
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.curriculum_links: Sessions are described generally as "linked to the national curriculum," with sessions grouped by Foundation Stage, Key Stage 1, Key Stage 2 (including Year 4+ and Year 6-focused sessions) and secondary/KS4+; no specific subject or standard-by-standard mapping given on the pages read.
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.teacher_materials: none listed as a downloadable pack on the pages read; a pre-visit form must be completed after booking ("complete the pre-visit form to receive your ticket") and the education team offers advice by phone/email Monday–Friday. ## Trust
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.risk_assessment_available: none listed as a downloadable document; a pre-visit is recommended to help plan the day and route, but no risk assessment document or template is referenced.
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.accreditations_displayed: LOTC (Learning Outside the Classroom) Quality Badge recognition; BIAZA, EAZA, WAZA and Visit England logos displayed on the general site; "Employability Day" described as a "BIAZA award winning session"; reference to the "European Association of Zoos and Aquaria (EAZA) Ex-situ Breeding Programme (EEP)" in relation to animal placement. ## Commercial
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.price_and_structure: Students aged 3–16: £8.50. Students 16+: £9.50. Additional adults/teachers: £15.50. Ages 1–2: £5.50. Carers with documentation: £0.00. Education sessions: £1.80 per child, minimum £45 charge for groups under 25. Employability Day: £150 excluding admission, maximum 20 students. These prices apply to "organised educational group visits to the park taking place on weekdays during Doncaster LEA term time only."
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.adults_free_ratio: "Primary = 1 free adult for every 5 students and secondary 1 free adult for every 10 students."
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.catering: none listed on the pages read.
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.cancellation_and_weather: "Refunds are unavailable for both admission & pre-booked sessions once the payment is made." Groups may be rescheduled to alternative dates instead. No separate weather policy stated.
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.booking_lead_time: none listed as a specific number of days/weeks; all visits require advance booking and pre-payment: "No, we are unable to accept payment on the day of your visit. All visitors must pre-book and pre-pay for their visits in advance." A pre-visit is recommended before the school visit and a pre-visit form must be completed to receive tickets. ## Conversion
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.how_to_book: Online enquiry form with fields for organisation name, contact details, group size estimate, session type (at park/virtual/at school) and message; stated response: "A member of our team will be in touch soon regarding this enquiry."
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.price_visible_without_asking: Yes — published on the education-pricing-tcs page.
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.downloadable_pack: none listed on the pages read.
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.testimonials_from_schools: "All staff we met in the park interacted with our children and the animals were amazing." "The teaching was outstanding, and all three classes were buzzing when they left."
yorkshire-wildlife-park.md.title_and_opening_line: Page title: "School Trips & Educational Visits". Opening line: "Enjoy a unique and truly WILD Educational Experience at Yorkshire Wildlife Park!"

zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.programme_names: - Nature at Your Place (Yr 1-8) - Zealandia at Your Place (Yr 1-8) - Experience Zealandia: self-guided (Yr 1-8) - The Family of Life - Tales Through Time - Mini Beasts - Nature & Nurture - A 500-year Journey - Pests & Predators - The nature of Science - Special Species - Nature at Your Place (Yr 9-13) - Zealandia at Your Place (Yr 9-13) - Experience Zealandia: self-guided (Yr 9-13) - Don't Feed the Kākā - A Living World - Citizen Scientists - Sanctuary & Society - Pests & Predators: Managing Mammals - Where Have all the Takahē Gone? - Understanding Plant & Animal Responses - Experience Zealandia (Ages 7-18) (for New Zealand and international youth groups)
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.activities_verbatim: - Nature at Your Place (Yr 1-8): "Nature at Your Place is a free programme for high EQI schools in the greater Wellington region, including two school outreach visits by Zealandia Educators and a sanctuary trip for your students." - Zealandia at Your Place (Yr 1-8): "Can't quite find the right date to visit the sanctuary or enough adults to accompany you on your trip? No problem; let us come to you! Our educators will visit you to explore nature at your place." - Experience Zealandia: self-guided (Yr 1-8): "Happy to show yourself around Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne? Self-guided school visits are available — come and explore at your own pace and see what you can discover!" - The Family of Life: facilitated session: "Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne provides a wonderful context for students to experience the rich biodiversity of Aotearoa New Zealand and consider the impact of people upon it – both positive and negative." - Tales Through Time: facilitated session: "The Zealandia valley is loaded with history: from hunting ground to goldrush, from waterworks to sanctuary. Students learn stories from past, present and future as they visit the now thriving valley." - Mini Beasts: facilitated session: "Storytelling is intertwined with a bug hunt in the sanctuary, where students will see what's hidden under leaves and in the ground in a place like Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne." - Nature & Nurture: facilitated session: "Learn about the importance of acting as kaitiaki of te taiao / nature while exploring the amazing mammalian predator-free valley at Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne." - A 500-year Journey: facilitated session: "Students learn about the past, present and future of Zealandia as they experience the valley. What can the valley tell us of the past and what does the future hold in its 500-year restoration journey?" - Pests & Predators: facilitated session: "Students learn about the ecological role and effect of endemic, native and introduced predators in Aotearoa, the strategies of their prey and the methods used by people to manage introduced species." - The nature of Science: facilitated session: "Students become scientists in the field as they experience the valley and document the many amazing and unique species they can see. Ask questions, make observations and draw conclusions!" - Special Species: facilitated session: "Students experience and learn about the unique biodiversity of Aotearoa New Zealand's native and endemic species." - Nature at Your Place (Yr 9-13): same wording as the Yr 1-8 entry above. - Zealandia at Your Place (Yr 9-13): same wording as the Yr 1-8 entry above. - Experience Zealandia: self-guided (Yr 9-13): same wording as the Yr 1-8 entry above. - Don't Feed the Kākā: facilitated session: "Get involved in the solution! This session presents Year 9-10 students with a real-world situation challenging them to devise a campaign to help prevent an undesired public behaviour — feeding kākā." - A Living World: facilitated session: "Students experience the unique biodiversity of Aotearoa New Zealand at Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne and learn about the dramatic impact of people upon it." - Citizen Scientists: facilitated session: "Students become scientists in the field as they experience the Zealandia valley and document the amazing and unique species that live there. Ask questions, make observations and draw conclusions!" - Sanctuary & Society: facilitated session: "Students learn about the Zealandia sanctuary's origins, societal impact and ongoing growth as a successful ecotourism project in the heart of Aotearoa New Zealand's capital." - Pests & Predators: Managing Mammals: facilitated session: "Learn about the ecological role and effect of endemic, native and introduced predators in Aotearoa New Zealand, the strategies of their prey and the methods used to manage introduced pest species." - Where Have all the Takahē Gone? (facilitated session, NCEA Biology): "'Where Have all the Takahē Gone?' explores the communities in which takahē currently live and the impact of the presence or absence of introduced mammals within these communities." - Understanding Plant & Animal Responses: facilitated session (NCEA Biology): "Engage and enthuse your students by letting them see how Aotearoa New Zealand species respond to their external environment." - Experience Zealandia (Ages 7-18): "Discover some of Aotearoa New Zealand's rare and unique fauna, flora and fungi. Join the Zealandia Educators to explore the sanctuary and witness native wildlife once again thriving on the mainland."
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.facilities: "Rātā Café is located on Level 2 of the Visitor Centre and offers delicious seasonal and sustainable cuisine with a picturesque view of the Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne sanctuary"; General Admission ticket described as offering "flat accessible walking options to more rugged tramping tracks" within the valley.
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.staff_qualifications_stated: School visits are stated to be "facilitated by experienced and knowledgeable educators"; sessions are led by "Zealandia Educators". No formal qualification, certification, or accreditation body is named.
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.accessibility_provision: General Admission ticket offers "flat accessible walking options to more rugged tramping tracks" within the valley; a separate "Accessibility information" page is linked from site navigation but its content was not one of the four pages read.
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.animal_species_held: kākā; tuatara; glowworms; kiwi; takahē. ## Curriculum
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.curriculum_links: Learning at Zealandia "supports the New Zealand Curriculum, Te Marautanga o Aotearoa or Te Whāriki" and "can be part of your Learning Experiences Outside the Classroom (LEOTC) school trips"; two sessions are labelled "NCEA Biology" ("Where Have all the Takahē Gone?" and "Understanding Plant & Animal Responses").
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.teacher_materials: "Explore our growing collection of resources for families, teachers, and researchers. From kids' activity booklets to colouring pages, discover fun and educational ways to connect with nature" (Resources section, described on the Learn/Education landing page; the Resources page itself was not one of the four pages read). ## Trust
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.accreditations_displayed: none listed (an "Awards and Recognition" footer link exists but its content was not one of the four pages read). ## Commercial
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.catering: Rātā Café hours stated in footer: "Rātā café: 9:00am–4:00pm; Kitchen: 9:00am–2:00pm."
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.how_to_book: School-visits page states: "If you can't find what you're looking for or would like to discuss specific requirements, please get in touch. Phone: 04 920 9204. Email: education@visitzealandia.com."
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.price_visible_without_asking: No. No price appears on any of the four pages read.
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.downloadable_pack: none listed on the four pages read.
zealandia-te-mara-a-tane.md.title_and_opening_line: School visits page heading: "School visits". Opening line: "Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne provides a range of learning programmes and resources that give students and teachers positive and inspiring nature-based learning experiences."

zoo-de-granby.md.programme_names: - Groupes scolaires (park visit) - Trois types d'ateliers: visite au zoo, Zoomobiles (en classe), Classes-Safaris - Exploration du monde animal (atelier TSA et DI) - À la bouffe - Les animaux sauvent Noël - Les métiers du Zoo - SOS, espèces en péril! - Naître et grandir - Planète mammifères! - Frissons nocturnes: bestioles au grand jour - Ouache! Un reptile! - Opération flocons: guide de survie en hiver - Halloween, chauves-souris et cie - L'univers des insectes - Les sens aux aguets - Le comportement animal - Reproduction animale sous la loupe
zoo-de-granby.md.activities_verbatim: - Exploration du monde animal (atelier TSA et DI): "Partons explorer le monde animal! Que ce soit dans l'eau, sur la terre et même dans le ciel, les animaux sont partout autour de nous. Atelier conçu et adapté pour les classes spécialisées avec des élèves à besoins particuliers (TSA et DI)" - À la bouffe: "Carnivore, herbivore ou omnivore, mais quelle est la différence? Découvrez de quoi et comment se nourrissent les animaux, qu'ils soient à plumes, à poils ou à écailles!" - Les animaux sauvent Noël: "Rudolf, le renne, s'est cassé la patte ! Vite, il faut remplacer notre ami au nez rouge, mais qui pourra relever ce défi ?" - Les métiers du Zoo: "Du vétérinaire au technicien en soins animaliers en passant par les biologistes, le zoo de Granby est une véritable ruche où de nombreuses spécialités se côtoient afin de veiller au bien-être de nos animaux." - SOS, espèces en péril!: "Les espèces animales disparaissent à un rythme effréné : inquiétant ou normal? Apprenez pourquoi elles sont toutes si importantes à préserver!" - Naître et grandir: "Découvrez les petits secrets de la séduction, de la naissance et des soins parentaux chez les animaux par une présentation colorée, interactive et amusante!" - Planète mammifères!: "Partez à la découverte des mammifères dans ce tour du monde endiablé! Découvrez les caractéristiques uniques de ces animaux dont nous faisons partie!" - Frissons nocturnes: bestioles au grand jour: "Serpents, araignées et chauves-souris hantent peut-être vos cauchemars, mais sous la loupe de nos biologistes, vous les découvrirez sous un tout nouveau jour!" - Ouache! Un reptile!: "Qu'est-ce qu'un reptile? Nos biologistes passionnés répondent à cette question en démontrant que c'est ni gluant, ni méchant!" - Opération flocons: guide de survie en hiver: "Brrrr! Il fait froid, les animaux font quoi? Explorez les différentes stratégies des animaux à l'arrivée de l'hiver et découvrez quels indices ils nous laissent de leur passage dans notre cour!" - Halloween, chauves-souris et cie: "Une fête de l'Halloween sous le thème des chauves-souris! Levons le voile sur ces créatures de la nuit et découvrons ce sympathique petit mammifère volant dans une ambiance ensorcelante!" - L'univers des insectes: "Pas besoin de travailler comme une fourmi pour piquer la curiosité sur le monde passionnant des insectes et autres bibittes." - Les sens aux aguets: "Participez à l'aventure rocambolesque d'un animal vedette qui doit utiliser tous ses sens afin de surmonter plusieurs obstacles!" - Le comportement animal: "Une initiation ludique et interactive à l'étude du comportement animal permettant d'en apprendre davantage sur les besoins des animaux. Découvrez aussi tous les efforts mis en œuvre pour favoriser les comportements naturels chez nos animaux!" - Reproduction animale sous la loupe: "Notre biologiste vous conduit sur les chemins de la reproduction animale. Découvrez la séduction en passant par la naissance jusqu'aux soins parentaux chez les animaux!"
zoo-de-granby.md.duration: Exploration du monde animal (atelier TSA et DI): 45 minutes. À la bouffe: 60 minutes. Les animaux sauvent Noël: 60 minutes. Les métiers du Zoo: 60 minutes. SOS, espèces en péril!: 60 minutes. Naître et grandir: 60 minutes. Planète mammifères!: 60 minutes. Frissons nocturnes: 60 minutes. Ouache! Un reptile!: 60 minutes. Opération flocons: 60 minutes. Halloween, chauves-souris et cie: 60 minutes. L'univers des insectes: 60 minutes. Les sens aux aguets: 60 minutes. Le comportement animal: 75 minutes. Reproduction animale sous la loupe: 75 minutes.
zoo-de-granby.md.group_size_min_max: none listed for individual workshops. Groupes scolaires park visit: group ticket rate applies "à l'achat de 20 billets et plus" (from 20 tickets and up).
zoo-de-granby.md.participant_thresholds: Groupes scolaires ticket rate: applicable at purchase of 20 tickets or more, "avec 1 billet gratuit offert pour chaque tranche de 21 billets vendus" (1 free ticket per 21 tickets sold). Zoomobile en classe: "*Un minimum de deux présentations est nécessaire pour autoriser le déplacement" (minimum two presentations required to authorise the trip). "Obtenez un rabais de 7% par présentation lorsque deux présentations ou plus sont planifiés sur un même contrat." ## Inventory
zoo-de-granby.md.facilities: Three parks: Parc animalier, Parc aquatique Amazoo (open only during summer period), Parc des manèges. "Nos terrasses" available for reservation (11h30, 12h15 or 13h00, free to reserve).
zoo-de-granby.md.equipment_provided: Zoomobiles (mobile units that travel to schools); "Bracelet 20 jetons pouvant être utilisés aux manèges et pour les activités payantes (bassin des raies, volière des loriquets, etc.)" offered as an optional add-on for school groups, not standard equipment.
zoo-de-granby.md.staff_qualifications_stated: "Naturalistes-interprètes" who go to meet students; "une équipe de biologistes chevronnés" (seasoned biologists); veterinarian, "technicien en soins animaliers," and biologists named among zoo professions in the "Les métiers du Zoo" workshop description.
zoo-de-granby.md.accessibility_provision: "Atelier conçu et adapté pour les classes spécialisées avec des élèves à besoins particuliers (TSA et DI)" (Exploration du monde animal workshop). General school-groups page: "Pour chaque personne à besoins particuliers, un accompagnateur est admis gratuitement. Si votre groupe est composé exclusivement de personnes à besoins particuliers, vous bénéficiez d'un ratio privilégié de 1 accompagnateur par participant. (1 pour 1)."
zoo-de-granby.md.animal_species_held: Rhinocéros blanc (white rhinoceros), named individuals Alice and Hazina, explicitly introduced on the homepage ("Deux poids lourds font leur entrée! Rencontrez Alice et Hazina"). Other species pictured with named individuals in homepage headlines include a "Tigre de l'Amour" (Amur tiger) named Jack. Beyond these two explicit mentions, the site organises "Animaux par continents" into Asie, Océanie, Afrique and Amérique du Sud without naming further species on the pages read. ## Curriculum
zoo-de-granby.md.price_and_structure: Groupes scolaires tarifs par personne (varies by age and season): Bambin (2 ans) 13,00$ été / 12,00$ pré-saison et automne; Enfant (3 à 12 ans) 26,00$ été / 24,75$ pré-saison et automne; Régulier (13 ans+) 35,75$ été / 33,75$ pré-saison et automne. "Applicables à l'achat de 20 billets et plus, avec 1 billet gratuit offert pour chaque tranche de 21 billets vendus." "Les prix sont sujets à changement sans préavis." Ateliers éducatifs (Zoomobile, distance/travel fee, in addition to workshop fee — workshop fee itself not stated on the page read): 0-10 km 40$; 11-25 km 65$; 26-50 km 105$; 51-75 km 145$; 76-100 km 185$; 101-125 km (et Montréal) 225$; 126-149 km 280$; plus de 150 km 280$ + 1$ du km excédentaire. "Frais supplémentaire par naturaliste sur l'île de Montréal et sur la rive-nord de l'île de Montréal: 30$." "Obtenez un rabais de 7% par présentation lorsque deux présentations ou plus sont planifiés sur un même contrat."
zoo-de-granby.md.adults_free_ratio: "Pour chaque personne à besoins particuliers, un accompagnateur est admis gratuitement." For groups composed exclusively of special-needs participants: "un ratio privilégié de 1 accompagnateur par participant (1 pour 1)." No general (non-special-needs) adult-to-student free ratio stated.
zoo-de-granby.md.catering: "Sac à lunch" and "Trios sur le pouce" and "Forfait sucrerie" listed as optional add-ons ("Bonifiez votre visite!") but no catering menu or pricing detail given.
zoo-de-granby.md.booking_lead_time: "La réservation doit être effectuée au moins 5 jours ouvrables avant la date prévue" (groupes scolaires park visit). "Le bureau des réservations sera en pause du 8 au 23 août!" (ateliers éducatifs page, a temporary seasonal closure notice, not a standing lead-time rule). ## Conversion
zoo-de-granby.md.how_to_book: Online reservation form (linked as "Réservation" / "Réserver" buttons) for both the park-visit groupes-scolaires offer and the ateliers éducatifs workshops. "Pour réserver une activité de type «Sortie de fin d'année» en mai et juin, veuillez remplir le formulaire."
zoo-de-granby.md.price_visible_without_asking: yes — per-person group ticket tariffs and Zoomobile travel-fee tables are both stated directly on the pages read
zoo-de-granby.md.title_and_opening_line: Groupes scolaires page title: "Groupes scolaires". Opening line: "Faites du Zoo de Granby la destination de votre prochaine sortie scolaire! Offrez à vos élèves une sortie scolaire inoubliable, remplie de découvertes. Une aventure enrichissante vous attend, pour tous!"
